## 8. Live target profile (`hdd.live.yaml`, git-ignored)

The profile describes the operator's deployment and the targets the acceptance suite may touch. In `saas` mode it still lists **only the operator's own** test and sandbox hosts; tenants' domains are never in it.

```yaml
schema_version: 5
lifecycle_stage: pilot                  # pilot | production (section 2.7)
deployment_mode: owner_only             # owner_only | saas (saas is refused when runtime.profile is local)
runtime:                                # R-31; section 8.2
  profile: hosted                       # hosted | local
  local:                                # read only when profile is local
    data_dir: ''                        # empty = per-OS user data directory
    database: embedded                  # embedded | external | compose
    kv: memory                          # memory | redis
    ports: {web: 8443, proxy_http: 8080, proxy_https: 8444, dns: 5300, api: 8000}   # unprivileged defaults
    local_domain_suffix: hdd.localhost  # Chromium and Firefox resolve *.localhost to loopback
    tls: local_ca                       # local_ca | http_only (loopback only)
    lan_exposure: false                 # true binds protected-site listeners to the LAN; needs the acknowledgement (section 2.11)
    loopback_client_identity: ua_keyed  # ua_keyed | single
    test_client_header: false           # accept X-HDD-Test-Client on loopback; selftest and acceptance runs enable it
    dogfood: false                      # true routes the product surfaces through the HDD proxy like hosted (platform_internal); off by default
    tunnel: {provider: none, trusted_cidrs: []}   # operator-run tunnel: none | cloudflared | ngrok | wireguard | other
  hosting:                              # read only when profile is hosted
    profile: H1                         # H1 to H5 (C18.10)
    watchdog: true
    backups: {schedule: '0 3 * * *', target: local, remote_env: ''}
    last_known_good_snapshot: true
# ---- REQUIRED when runtime.profile is hosted (local needs only runtime, operator_email and signup; section 8.2) ----
platform_domain: example.com            # operator-owned apex hosting www/app/admin/api/ns/status
domain: example.com                     # apex zone the operator owns and will protect first
test_hostname: hddtest.example.com      # real-site mirror: benign + GET/HEAD attack shapes
sandbox_hostname: hddsbx.example.com    # forwards only exact canary paths; Class B and body vectors go here
surfaces:
  public_host: www.example.com
  app_host: app.example.com
  admin_host: admin.example.com
  api_host: api.example.com
  status_host: status.example.com       # ideally served from outside this VPS (T-0100)
  admin_exposure: tunnel_only           # tunnel_only | routed_with_cidr (admin_cidrs + MFA required)
origin:
  url: https://203.0.113.10             # real origin, scheme included
  tls_server_name: example.com
  host_header: example.com
  tls_verify: {mode: webpki, pin: ''}   # webpki | pinned_ca | pinned_spki; verification can never be disabled
  lockdown_state: pending               # pending | applied (origin firewall / secret header, set by operator)
  canary: {base_path: /__hdd_canary/, use_hdd_canary_agent: true}
platform:
  public_ipv4: ['198.51.100.20']        # VPS IPs running HDD
  public_ipv6: []
  ns_hostnames: ['ns1.example.com', 'ns2.example.com']
  edge_cname_zone: edge.example.com     # saas/cname modes: <site-id>.edge.<platform_domain>
  acme_cname_zone: acme.example.com     # DNS-01 delegation target: <zone-id>.acme.<platform_domain>
  uplink_mbps: 0                        # contracted or measured; 0 = unknown (capacity then UNVERIFIED)
  deploy_mode: on-vps                   # on-vps | ssh
  ssh: {host: '', user: '', key_path: ''}
  min_resources: {vcpu: 2, ram_mb: 4096, disk_gb: 40}
dns:
  topology: self_authoritative          # self_authoritative | hidden_primary
  public_ns: []                         # hidden_primary: NS names served by the external secondary
registrar: {provider: '', api_token_env: ''}   # env var NAME only; registrar changes are manual unless a token is supplied
existing_dns: {provider: '', export_method: zonefile, zonefile_path: ''}   # axfr | api | zonefile | manual
test_runner:
  public_ip: auto                       # auto = discovered through the canary echo via HDD; bannable by design
  control_plane_access: ssh-tunnel      # ssh-tunnel | wireguard
admin_cidrs: []                         # never-ban + admin-hostname allowlist; must NOT contain the runner IP
ssh_allow_cidrs: []                     # port 22 only; may contain the runner IP
egress_allowlist: []                    # section 2.1; must cover SMTP relay, CAs, resolvers, feeds you enable
acme: {email: '', directory: staging}   # staging first; production only after staging passes and operator confirms
operator_email: ''                      # receives test mail and alerts; the only address the agent may mail
# ---- PRODUCT (required when the UI is enabled; defaults shown are the safest) ----
signup:
  mode: invite_only                     # disabled | invite_only | open (open needs operator approval in chat)
  email_verification: required          # always required; field kept for explicitness
  allowed_email_domains: []             # empty = any (subject to policy below)
  disposable_email_policy: challenge    # block | challenge | allow
  password_breach_check: offline_list   # offline_list | hibp_range | off  (hibp_range needs egress entry)
  min_password_length: 12
  require_mfa_for: [platform_admin]     # roles for which MFA enrollment is forced; org owners may require it for members
smtp: {host: '', port: 587, tls: starttls, username_env: '', password_env: '', from_address: '', from_name: 'Hack Dev Defence', reply_to: ''}
branding: {product_name: 'Hack Dev Defence', logo_path: '', legal_entity: '', support_email: '', terms_url: '', privacy_url: ''}
plans: {mode: unlimited}                # unlimited | tiered (tiered quotas editable in the admin panel)
geoip: {db_path: '', asn_db_path: '', source: ''}   # HDD_GEOIP_DB; source records the license/provenance
locales: [en]                           # UI languages shipped
# ---- OPTIONAL (missing => UNVERIFIED, never faked) ----
secondary_dns: {provider: '', tsig_key_env: '', addresses: []}
vantage_points: []                      # [{name, ssh_host, ssh_user, ssh_key_path}] or SOCKS proxies
origin_access_log: {ssh_host: '', path: ''}
site:
  platform: custom                      # wordpress | static | custom | other (drives honeypot defaults)
  har_file: ''                          # scrubbed before use (AC-06)
  crawl_start_url: ''
  replay_methods: [GET, HEAD]           # state-changing methods need explicit per-path allowlisting
  non_http_services: [smtp, imap, ssh]  # forced grey-cloud
  extra_proxied_ports: []
  auth_paths: ['/login', '/wp-login.php', '/signin', '/api/auth/login']   # drives auth-endpoint hardening
upstream_cdn: {enabled: false, trusted_cidrs: []}
alerts: {webhook_env: '', heartbeat_url_env: ''}   # heartbeat = external dead-man monitor the operator runs
retention: {events_days: 30, audit_days: 400}   # audit floor 180; plan caps may lower the events value
lab: {enabled: false, host: '', cidr: '', vulnlab_enabled: false}   # closed lab for L3/L4 and the Vuln-Lab
load_profile_approved: false            # true only after the operator's written approval for a `load` run
```

### 8.2 Local-profile rules

With `runtime.profile: local` the only required fields are `runtime`, `operator_email` and `signup` (mode `disabled` or `invite_only`; `open` is refused). `platform_domain` defaults to `hdd.localhost`, `deployment_mode` must be `owner_only`, and `surfaces.admin_exposure` is forced to `tunnel_only` (loopback). Domains are added from the UI, not the profile. The fields `platform.*`, `dns.*`, `registrar`, `acme`, `upstream_ddos` and `secondary_dns` are ignored and reported as "not applicable in local". `hddctl preflight` and `hdd-local doctor` print which acceptance checks can run (the `local` tier of AC-55 and every unit, integration and browser test) and which are UNVERIFIED(`environment_unsupported`) (authoritative DNS on 53, kernel enforcement, ACME, DDoS and cutover checks). Moving to a server later is a profile change plus `hdd-local export` and `hddctl import` (C18.12).

### 8.1 Fields required for production cutover

The pilot may run with `upstream_ddos.mode: none`, but the report then shows DDoS readiness as **NOT READY** and the cutover checklist fails.

```yaml
upstream_ddos:
  mode: none                    # always_on | on_demand | none
  provider: ''
  advertised_capacity_gbps: 0   # copied from the contract; never assumed by the agent
  over_capacity_behavior: ''    # for example null-route for N minutes; from the contract
  mitigation_api: {kind: '', token_env: ''}
  standby_edge_ips: []          # pre-provisioned standby or scrubbed edge IPs for DNS failover
  provider_contact: ''
  risk_acceptance_volumetric: false   # true only after the operator's written confirmation in chat (date recorded)
  lab: {host: '', private_link: ''}   # closed lab machine the operator owns for L3/L4 tests (never the live VPS)
secondary_dns_required_for_cutover: true
app_inventory:
  components: []                # [{name, version, ecosystem|cpe|purl, internet_facing, notes}]
  sbom_path: ''                 # CycloneDX or SPDX
  patch_sla_days: {kev: 2, critical: 7, high: 30, medium: 90}
  vuln_feed_mode: online        # online | offline (file import)
  origin_owner_contact: ''      # receives patch-SLA alerts
```

If a REQUIRED field is missing or unreachable, **stop and list exactly what is missing and how to provide it**. Never invent values. Generate `hdd.live.example.yaml` with every field documented, publish a JSON Schema (`schemars`), and validate the real file with `hddctl preflight`. `serde_yaml` is archived; vet maintained alternatives (for example `serde_yaml_ng`, `saphyr`) and if none is acceptable switch the profile to TOML and tell the operator (T-0006).

---

## 9. First response protocol

Before writing any code, the agent's first response contains only:

1. A short restatement of the mission and the safety envelope.
2. Validation of `hdd.live.yaml` against section 8, listing every missing or unreachable required field and exactly how the operator can provide it (if the file does not exist, list all required fields).
3. The environment-discovery results (read-only commands only), including what degrades if something is missing (rule R-05), and the **build-track decision**: *Track H* (Linux builder with Docker: testcontainers) or *Track L* (no Docker, for example a Windows or macOS builder: the embedded PostgreSQL and in-process stores of `hdd-local` via `cargo xtask db up`; hosted-only checks are UNVERIFIED(`environment_unsupported`) until a Linux host is supplied). A missing Docker, Redis, nftables or `dig` never blocks the build; it selects the track.
4. The P00 to P03 plan with acceptance criteria and the milestone dates it implies.
5. The human-gated steps the operator should expect and roughly when: M1 design sign-off (P03), STOP #1 at M5 (canary files, pilot NS/A delegation, provider AUP confirmation), M3 SMTP details, STOP #2 at M12 (registrar preparation, origin firewall and secret header, secondary DNS, provider contract details, DS-check inputs), production ACME approval, any `load` run, cutover.
6. The DDoS-readiness questions (Part C, C11) and the origin-inventory questions (Part C, C12), plus the **product questions** in Appendix E8 (deployment mode, signup policy, brand, languages, SMTP, GeoIP database, plans, password-breach-check mode, status-page hosting, legal text ownership), with what each unanswered item blocks:

| Unanswered or missing | Blocks |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime profile choice (local, hosted, or both) | the build track, the acceptance tiers that can run, and which of M5 and M12 apply |
| Hosting provider and profile (H1 to H5) for 24/7 operation | STOP #1 at M5 and any uptime statement |
| Required profile fields (hosted) | P00 preflight and everything live (P11 deploy) |
| Provider AUP confirmation | the first live test |
| `egress_allowlist` entries | feeds, propagation checks, ACME, SMTP, GeoIP download |
| SMTP details | real email delivery tests in P06 (a local SMTP sink is used until then) |
| Brand and legal ownership | publication of the public site (P05 can be built, not published) |
| `signup.mode: open` approval | enabling public signup |
| `upstream_ddos` details | cutover only; pilot reports NOT READY |
| `secondary_dns` | cutover gate, AC-21, AC-28 |
| Lab machine | AC-26, AC-29, AC-38, AC-39 lab portions (UNVERIFIED `capability_not_supplied`) |
| `platform.uplink_mbps` | shield capacity figures (UNVERIFIED) |
| Inventory or SBOM | real matching in AC-30 and the exposure-board cutover gate |
| GeoIP database | country rules and geo analytics (UNVERIFIED) |

Then wait for the operator's reply if anything required is missing; otherwise begin P00.

# PART B: PRODUCT DEFINITION

## B1. Personas and jobs to be done

Design every screen for these people. Each persona has accessibility needs that are requirements, not afterthoughts.

### B1.1 Maya, the site owner (primary)

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Who | Runs a small online shop or content site on WordPress or a custom PHP/Node app; hired a freelancer once; not a network engineer. |
| Goals | "Stop the weird traffic and the hacking attempts without breaking my site." Understand what is happening in plain language. Add a domain in minutes. |
| Fears | Breaking the live site during DNS changes; being locked out; paying for something she cannot verify; jargon. |
| Context | Laptop and phone; low tolerance for multi-page docs; edits DNS at a registrar UI she barely understands. |
| Needs from HDD | A guided wizard that detects her current DNS, offers the simplest integration (CNAME or nameservers), says what each step changes, tests before cutover, offers an instant way back, and shows a Protection Readiness checklist. A block page her customers can understand. |
| Success | Site is proxied, in monitor mode for a few days, then block mode, with an email when something serious happens. |
| Key journeys | J-02, J-07, J-08/J-09, J-12, J-15, J-16, J-22/J-23, J-25 |
| Accessibility | Screen magnification, large text, keyboard use after injury; reduced motion. |

### B1.2 Dan, the developer / DevOps engineer

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Who | Maintains several apps; uses Git, CI, Terraform; reads logs. |
| Goals | Automate: create domains, rules and API keys from code; stream events to his SIEM; know exactly why a request was blocked (rule ID, field, evidence). |
| Fears | Opaque magic; rules that break deploys; no API parity with UI. |
| Needs | Complete REST API with OpenAPI, scoped API keys with expiry and IP restriction, webhooks with signatures, Ray ID lookup, dry-run endpoint, exportable events, config revisions with diff and rollback. |
| Key journeys | J-19, J-20, J-21, J-27, J-28 |
| Accessibility | Keyboard-first; command palette; copy buttons; monospace readability. |

### B1.3 Sara, the security analyst

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Who | Triage attacks, tune rules, reduce false positives, report to management. |
| Goals | See attacks live, pivot by IP/ASN/path/rule, ban or allow, create scoped exceptions, produce weekly reports. |
| Fears | Alert fatigue; a rule change that silently opens a hole; bans that hit legitimate shared IPs. |
| Needs | Live Threat Monitor with filters and pause; event detail with redacted evidence and policy branch; collateral-risk hints; rule dry-run against recent traffic; attack timeline grouping; saved views. |
| Key journeys | J-16, J-17, J-18, J-19, J-23, J-34 |
| Accessibility | Dense data tables with density control; screen-reader friendly table semantics; color not the only signal. |

### B1.4 Omar, the platform operator

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Who | Runs the HDD installation (in `owner_only` mode he is also Maya). |
| Goals | Keep the platform healthy; onboard tenants; handle abuse; roll out rule packs safely; know when the VPS is saturated; take backups and restore them. |
| Fears | A bad global rule outage; a tenant abusing the proxy; a compromised admin account; being unreachable during an incident. |
| Needs | Separate, locked-down admin surface; health of every service; global jail and never-ban controls; staged rule-pack rollout with auto-rollback; impersonation that is read-only and audited; emergency controls; shield state; DDoS readiness. |
| Key journeys | J-29, J-30, J-31, J-34 |

### B1.5 Vi, the blocked visitor

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Who | A legitimate end user of a protected site whose request was blocked (shared IP, odd input, privacy tool). |
| Goals | Understand what happened, get back in, tell the site owner. |
| Needs | A calm, branded, accessible block page with a Ray ID, no technical blame, a short explanation, an appeal form that needs no account, a challenge alternative for soft blocks. Never reveal which rule matched or hints useful to attackers. |
| Key journeys | J-22 |
| Accessibility | Works with screen readers, no CAPTCHA puzzle, works on old phones, no required JavaScript for reading the page (challenge needs JavaScript; provide an explanation and an alternative contact path). |

### B1.6 Alex, the agency manager

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Who | Manages domains for several clients under one or more orgs. |
| Needs | Org switcher, domain lists with filters and bulk actions, per-member role scoping, per-client reports. |
| Key journeys | J-26, J-28 |

### B1.7 Adversary A (design for them, never for their convenience)

Scanners (sqlmap, nikto, nuclei), credential stuffers, scrapers, botnets, a curious attacker reading error pages, an attacker who tries to poison bans by luring victims, an attacker who tries to hijack signup or password reset, an attacker who tries to claim someone else's domain. Every flow is reviewed with an abuse case (T-0011 to T-0028, `[SEC]` tasks). Rule: error pages, block pages and API errors give attackers no rule names, no stack traces, no internal hostnames, no confirmation of account existence.

---

## B2. Information architecture

### B2.1 Surfaces and hosts

| Surface | Host | Audience | Exposure |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `public` | `www.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}` | anyone | public (proxied by HDD itself in dogfood mode) |
| `app` | `app.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}` | signed-in tenant users, plus auth pages | public when `deployment_mode: saas`; allowlist or tunnel in `owner_only` |
| `admin` | `admin.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}` | platform staff | never public by default: tunnel/WireGuard, or routed with `admin_cidrs` + MFA + step-up |
| `api` | `api.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}` | API clients | public in `saas`; **bearer API keys only** (no cookies are accepted or set on this host); rate-limited |
| `status` | `status.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}` | anyone | hosted outside the VPS where possible |
| `ns1/ns2` | `ns1.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}` | DNS clients | UDP/TCP 53 |
| Customer domains | tenant-owned | their visitors | HDD data plane; reserved path prefix `/__hdd/` |

**Same-origin API mount.** The browser UI never calls `api.` cross-origin. `app.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}/api/v1/*` and `admin.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}/api/v1/*` are mounted same-origin by the router (T-0355) and forwarded to `hdd-api`, so cookie sessions, `__Host-` cookies, SameSite=Strict and CSRF checks work without CORS. The `admin` mount serves only `/api/v1/admin/*` and platform-scoped routes and is subject to the same `admin_cidrs`/tunnel rule as the admin host. The `api.` host serves the same OpenAPI document but accepts only `Authorization: Bearer` credentials; a request to it that carries a session cookie is answered `ERR-AUTH-001` and the cookie is ignored.

**Local profile hosts.** With `runtime.profile: local` (C18), `{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}` is `hdd.localhost`: the surfaces are `www.`, `app.`, `admin.`, `api.` and `status.` under it on the unprivileged web port (default 8443), `admin` is always loopback-only, and protected local sites are `<slug>.hdd.localhost` (Chromium and Firefox resolve every `*.localhost` name to loopback; Safari and command-line tools may need the hosts helper, C18.8).

The break-glass path (SSH tunnel to loopback `:3000` and `:8000`, plus `hddctl`) always works regardless of proxy state.

All routes are lowercase, hyphenated, without trailing slash. IDs in URLs are prefixed identifiers (`org_`, `dom_`, `usr_`, `rule_`, `ban_`, `evt_`, `whk_`, `key_`, `cert_`, `rpt_`, `inv_`, `apl_`) followed by 26 characters of lowercase base32 over a UUIDv7. Organizations are addressed by slug.

### B2.3 Navigation model

- **Org sidebar** (left, collapsible, icons plus labels): Overview, Domains, Live events, Bans, Analytics, Reports, Notifications, Integrations, Team, API keys, Audit log, Plan and usage, Settings. Items the user lacks permission for are hidden, not disabled with a mystery tooltip; where the feature exists but needs a higher plan, show a clearly labeled upgrade note that never hides security controls (R-28).
- **Top bar**: org switcher, domain switcher (type-ahead), global search / command palette (Ctrl/Cmd+K), notification bell with unread count, theme toggle, help menu, user menu.
- **Domain context**: a header (domain name, status pill, mode pill WAF `block|monitor|log|off`, readiness ring) and tabs: Overview, DNS, SSL/TLS, Security, Origin, Events, Bans, Analytics, Settings. **Security** has a secondary list: WAF, Categories, Shield, Rules, Rate limits, Bots and challenge, Access lists, Access gate, API, Business flows, Exceptions, Honeypots, Outbound, Block page, Coverage, Revisions, Emergency.
- **Breadcrumbs** on every nested screen; **page title** (`<title>`) always `Screen · Domain · Org · Hack Dev Defence`.
- **Keyboard shortcuts** (discoverable with `?`): `g o` overview, `g d` domains, `g e` events, `g b` bans, `/` search, `c` copy focused value, `Esc` close.
- **Admin surface** uses a visually distinct accent (a persistent "Platform admin" banner color band) so staff never confuse it with the tenant app.

---

## B3. Core user journeys

Each journey lists persona, trigger, steps, success criteria, failure paths, screens, and the acceptance check that proves it. Tasks reference journeys by ID.

### J-01 Visitor discovers HDD and reads honest claims
Persona Maya. Trigger: search result or referral. Steps: (1) lands on S-001 and reads a one-sentence value statement; (2) opens S-003 and reads what is and is not protected; (3) opens a docs quickstart; (4) clicks "Create account". Success: reaches S-020 in three clicks or fewer; page weight within budget; no tracking cookies. Failure paths: JavaScript disabled still renders everything; slow connection loads text first. Check: AC-40, AC-41 (public pages), claims-lint.

### J-02 Visitor signs up and verifies email
Persona Maya. Preconditions: `signup.mode` is `open`, or the visitor holds an invite. Steps: (1) S-020 enters email, name, password; strength meter and breach check give live, kind feedback; (2) submits; always sees S-021 "Check your email" regardless of whether the address already exists; (3) receives the verification message; (4) opens link, S-022 shows a confirm button; (5) confirms (POST) and is signed in or sent to login; (6) lands in S-035 onboarding. Success: account is `active`, org created, audit event written. Failure paths: expired token shows a resend form (rate-limited); disposable email triggers the configured policy with a neutral message; password found in breach list is rejected with guidance; signup closed shows a request-invite message. Check: AC-35, AC-46.

### J-03 New user enrolls MFA
Persona any. Trigger: forced for platform roles and for orgs that require it; recommended for others. Steps: (1) S-030 shows a QR code (SVG) and manual key; (2) user scans, enters a six-digit code; (3) S-031 shows ten recovery codes once, with download/print/copy and a required "I saved these" confirmation; (4) optional passkey enrollment. Success: MFA active; recovery codes hashed at rest. Failure paths: wrong code (with drift window); lost phone (recovery code); reset by owner (org) or `hddctl` (platform). Check: AC-35.

### J-04 Returning user logs in
Steps: (1) S-023 email + password; (2) if MFA or passkey: S-024/S-026; (3) device cookie suppresses repeat prompts only where policy allows; (4) lands on the last org overview. Failure paths: generic "Email or password is incorrect"; lockout/backoff message that does not confirm existence (S-034 when locked); suspicious login triggers email notice. Check: AC-35.

### J-05 User resets a forgotten password
Steps: (1) S-027 enters email; (2) always sees "If an account exists, we sent instructions"; (3) link opens S-028 (confirm, then set new password); (4) all sessions revoked; notification email sent. Failure paths: expired or used token; rate limit. Check: AC-35, AC-46.

### J-06 User accepts a team invite
Steps: (1) invite email; (2) S-029 shows org name and role; (3) existing user signs in or new user signs up with the invited email locked; (4) membership created; owner notified. Failure: expired/revoked invite; email mismatch. Check: AC-35, AC-36.

### J-07 Owner completes the onboarding checklist
Steps: S-035 wizard: profile, org name and slug, MFA recommendation, first domain CTA, alert email, notification preferences. The checklist persists on S-040 until done or dismissed. Success: first domain started. Check: AC-37.

### J-08 Owner adds a domain using full nameserver delegation
Steps (S-042): (1) enter `example.org`; (2) HDD scans existing DNS and shows what it found; (3) choose "Use HDD nameservers (recommended)"; (4) review imported records, proxy toggles, mail records forced grey, parity report; (5) prove ownership (TXT) if required by mode; (6) configure origin and test connectivity; (7) TLS pre-issuance plan; (8) choose protection preset (starts in monitor); (9) copy the two nameservers; HDD polls delegation; (10) go-live checklist; rollback instructions shown before the NS change. Success: domain `active`, traffic proxied, readiness at least 70. Failure paths: DS record present at parent (warning with steps); unsupported record types (acknowledge); delegation not propagated (live status with next check time). Check: AC-37, AC-02, AC-03.

### J-09 Owner adds a domain using CNAME (partial) setup
Steps: as J-08 but step 3 chooses "Keep my DNS provider; point `www` to HDD". HDD gives `www CNAME <site-id>.edge.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}`, the verification TXT, and an optional `_acme-challenge` CNAME for pre-issuance. HDD polls until the CNAME resolves. Success: `www` proxied; apex handled by J-10. Check: AC-37.

### J-10 Owner attaches an apex via A/ALIAS or only a subdomain
Steps: wizard explains that CNAME cannot sit at the apex; offers (a) A records to HDD IPs, (b) ALIAS/ANAME to the edge name if the provider supports it, (c) full NS delegation. Warns that A-record mode needs the operator to keep HDD IPs current (HDD announces changes with 30 days notice). Check: AC-37.

### J-11 Owner verifies ownership
Steps: HDD shows both methods (DNS TXT, HTTP file); copy buttons; verification poller with timestamps; re-verify later automatically. Failure: wrong content; CDN caching the file; wildcard TXT conflicts. Check: AC-37.

### J-12 Owner configures and tests the origin
Steps: scheme, host/IP, port, Host header, SNI name, TLS verification mode (webpki, pinned CA, pinned SPKI, or acknowledged plaintext), health-check path; "Test connection" shows DNS result, connect time, TLS result, status code, response headers (redacted), and clear remedies. SSRF guard errors are explained. Check: AC-17, AC-37.

### J-13 Owner imports existing DNS and resolves parity warnings
Steps: S-047 shows source vs HDD diff per record; unsupported types listed with explanations; owner acknowledges each; parity must be clean before the NS step. Check: AC-02.

### J-14 Owner edits DNS and toggles orange/grey
Steps: S-045 table; inline edit; S-046 type-specific editor; preview "what will resolve"; toggle proxied with consequence text; change history S-048. Failure paths: CNAME conflicts, wildcard shadowing, mail records proxied (blocked). Check: AC-03.

### J-15 Owner issues TLS and enables HSTS
Steps: S-050 shows TLS mode and status; S-051 shows certificates and renewal; enabling HSTS shows a preload caution and a staged max-age ramp. Check: AC-04.

### J-16 Owner enables protection in monitor mode, reviews, switches to block
Steps: preset "Monitor first"; after traffic, S-054 shows "would have blocked" counts with examples; owner reviews false positives via S-065/S-066, creates exceptions (S-064) if needed; "Switch to Block" dialog states consequences, shows 48-hour readiness hint, offers scheduled switch; undo within one click. Check: AC-06, AC-13.

### J-17 Owner enables the Vulnerable-Origin Shield
Steps: S-057 explains in plain language ("Assume your site has bugs"); sets strictness (Balanced or Paranoid), marks auth endpoints, enables ban-on-first-hard-hit, shows the exact payload classes blocked, offers a "Try a payload" box that calls the inspect API; shows learning-mode suggestions. Success: shield on, SQLi ban policy visible. Check: AC-38, AC-39.

### J-18 Analyst investigates an attack
Steps: S-065 live monitor; filter by category `sqli`; open S-066 for evidence (redacted), rule, policy branch; see the IP's other events; ban/unban; create exception for a false positive; link to the Ray ID. Check: AC-07, AC-08.

### J-19 Owner builds a custom rule
Steps: S-059 builder: conditions (field, operator, value), action (block, log, allow, ban, challenge), scope (path/method), expiry; "Test" runs the inspect API on samples and dry-runs against recent traffic (S-060); save creates a revision; auto-rollback explained. Check: AC-12, AC-13.

### J-20 Owner configures rate limits for login
Steps: S-061 pick preset "Login protection" (e.g., 5/min per IP per path with progressive ban), apply to detected auth endpoints; test with the burst helper. Check: AC-11.

### J-21 Owner configures alerts and webhooks
Steps: S-076 choose events (critical attack, mass ban, cert expiry, origin down), channels (email, webhook, Slack, Discord, Telegram, PagerDuty), quiet hours; S-078 create a webhook, see the signing secret once, send a test; S-079 inspect deliveries and retries. Check: AC-45.

### J-22 Blocked visitor files an appeal
Steps: S-140 shows Ray ID and a short explanation; visitor opens S-145, enters optional contact and a note, passes a light proof-of-work, submits; sees S-146. Owner is notified. Failure: abuse attempts rate-limited. Check: AC-43.

### J-23 Owner handles an appeal
Steps: S-069 inbox lists appeals with Ray ID and evidence; owner can unban, allowlist for N days, create a scoped exception, or decline with a reason. Check: AC-43.

### J-24 Owner locks down the origin
Steps: S-098 wizard: select stack; copy firewall allowlist of HDD IPs; set the secret origin header and a snippet to enforce it; verify with real probes; mark `applied`. Check: AC-18.

### J-25 Owner views Protection Readiness and fixes items
Steps: S-044 lists checks with weight, status, "why it matters", and a one-click path to fix; score animates only if reduced motion is off; footnote about meaning. Check: AC-53.

### J-26 Owner invites teammates and assigns roles
Steps: S-081/S-082/S-083; role descriptions; last-owner protection; invitation expiry. Check: AC-36.

### J-27 Developer creates an API key and uses the API
Steps: S-080 create key with scopes, expiry, IP restriction; secret shown once; example `curl`; usage graph; revoke. Check: AC-35, AC-45.

### J-28 Owner exports reports and audit logs
Steps: S-073/S-074 generate or schedule reports; S-084 filter and export CSV/JSON; hash-chain verification indicator. Check: AC-47.

### J-29 Platform admin onboards and manages tenants
Steps: S-101/S-102 view usage, plan, domains, abuse flags; suspend with reason (customer notified); delete with grace period. Check: AC-42.

### J-30 Platform admin investigates abuse and global bans
Steps: S-114 triage; S-106 global jail; S-109 never-ban management with collision warnings. Check: AC-51.

### J-31 Platform admin toggles safe mode, maintenance, checks infra
Steps: S-110/S-111 health; S-122 emergency controls with typed confirmation; S-121 maintenance banner. Check: AC-13, AC-42.

### J-32 Owner removes a domain safely
Steps: S-094: choose desired end state (return DNS to previous provider, or keep DNS-only), export zone, show exact record changes to revert, revoke certificates optional, type-to-confirm. Success: domain `removed`, no dangling HDD references. Check: AC-37.

### J-33 User exports data or deletes the account
Steps: S-090: request export (async, emailed link), request deletion (grace period, owner transfer prerequisites). Check: AC-47.

### J-34 Incident: attack spike
Steps: alert fires; S-054 shows elevated state; owner enables "Under attack" (challenge all new clients) from S-093; analyst bans campaign IPs/ASNs; after calm the mode de-escalates; incident timeline saved. Check: AC-44, AC-27.

## B4. Roles and permissions

### B4.1 Roles

| Scope | Role | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Org | `owner` | Full control incl. billing/plan, deletion, transfer. At least one per org (last-owner protection). |
| Org | `admin` | Everything except org deletion, ownership transfer and plan changes. |
| Org | `analyst` | Read all security data; manage bans, exceptions, appeals, rules (not DNS or TLS or team). |
| Org | `viewer` | Read-only on domains, events, analytics. |
| Org | `billing` | Plan and usage only (no security data). |
| Platform | `platform_owner` | All platform permissions; may manage platform staff. Exactly the bootstrap admin initially. |
| Platform | `platform_admin` | Operate the platform; cannot manage other platform admins or change signup/legal settings without step-up. |
| Platform | `platform_support` | Read tenant metadata; read-only impersonation; no mutations. |
| Platform | `platform_auditor` | Read platform audit logs and reports only. |
| API key | scoped by permission IDs | A key never exceeds the creating user's permissions at creation time and is re-evaluated on each call. |

Platform roles and org roles are independent. Platform roles require MFA (forced), a distinct session cookie scope, short idle timeout (15 min), absolute timeout (8 h), and step-up re-authentication for mutations flagged `S`.

### B4.3 Authorization rules

1. Every handler declares its permission ID; a missing declaration fails the build (xtask check of the route table).
2. Org-scoped handlers resolve the org from the path, verify membership, then verify the permission for that role, then verify the resource's `org_id` (defense in depth on top of RLS).
3. Step-up (`S`) requires a successful re-authentication within the last 10 minutes (platform: 5 minutes); the UI prompts with S-032 and retries the action.
4. Platform staff reach tenant data only through explicit platform endpoints (`/api/v1/platform/...`) that log a reason string for every access to tenant resources; there is no "superuser bypass" of RLS in application code.
5. Impersonation sessions carry a flag that makes every non-GET request fail with `ERR-AUTH-014` at the middleware layer, and every page shows a non-dismissible banner with the remaining time.
6. API keys carry explicit permission IDs; the effective permission is the intersection of the key's scopes and the creator's current role.
7. Permission checks are unit-tested by a generated matrix test: for every route and every role, the expected status code is asserted from this table.

## B5. Data model (PostgreSQL) and Redis

### B5.1 Conventions

- Primary keys are `uuid` generated as UUIDv7 in the database default (`gen_uuidv7()` function created by migration 1 if the server lacks one). The API exposes prefixed base32 identifiers (B2.2). Every table has `created_at timestamptz not null default now()`; mutable tables also have `updated_at` maintained by trigger and `version int not null default 1` for optimistic concurrency (`ETag` = `W/"<version>"`).
- **Every tenant-owned table has `org_id uuid not null references orgs(id)` from migration 1** and a row-level-security policy: `using (org_id = nullif(current_setting('app.org_id', true), '')::uuid)`. The application roles never have `BYPASSRLS`; only `hdd_backup` does, and it cannot write (with `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, a dump by any other role would silently contain no tenant rows). Platform operations use `SECURITY DEFINER` functions that insert an audit row with a mandatory `reason`.
- Roles: `hdd_owner` (migrations only), `hdd_api` (read/write, subject to RLS), `hdd_worker` (read/write, subject to RLS plus system tables), `hdd_proxy` and `hdd_dns` (read-only on config tables; their only write is `INSERT`/`COPY` into the unpartitioned `waf_events_ingest` table described in B5.7), `hdd_readonly` (analytics, subject to RLS), `hdd_backup` (`LOGIN`, `BYPASSRLS`, `SELECT` only; used solely by backup jobs, never by services).
- Enumerations are Postgres `text` with `check` constraints (easier expand/contract than native enums).
- Time-partitioned tables: `waf_events` (monthly), `audit_log` (monthly), `login_attempts` (monthly), `webhook_deliveries` (monthly), `mail_outbox` (monthly), `rollup_*` (yearly). Retention drops partitions; there is no row-by-row delete job on the hot tables.
- **Partitioned-table rules (PostgreSQL).** A primary key or unique constraint on a partitioned table must contain the partition key, so these tables use composite keys: `waf_events (ray_id, ts)`, `audit_log (id, ts)`, `login_attempts (id, ts)`, `webhook_deliveries (id, created_at)`, `mail_outbox (id, created_at)`, `rollup_* (org_id, site_id, bucket, dimension, key)` with `bucket` as the partition key. **No foreign key references a partitioned table**; references to them (for example `ip_bans.ray_id`, `ban_appeals.ray_id`) are logical, resolved by `(ray_id, ts)` lookups and checked by a nightly integrity job. Foreign keys *from* a partitioned table to an ordinary table (for example `waf_events.ban_id`) are allowed. Each migration that creates a partitioned table also creates the next two partitions and registers it with the partition manager (T-0442).
- Secrets at rest (TLS private keys, ACME keys, TOTP secrets, SMTP/webhook secrets, provider tokens) use an envelope: `HDD_MASTER_KEY` wraps per-secret data keys (AES-256-GCM, 96-bit random nonce, AAD = table+id+column). Stored as `bytea` with a `key_version int`.
- Indexes follow query patterns listed in each migration's header comment. Every foreign key is indexed.
- Expand/contract only: add nullable column, backfill, enforce, then (later release) drop.

### B5.2 Identity and access

| Table | Key columns | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `users` | id, email_normalized unique, email_display, email_verified_at, password_hash, password_pepper_kid smallint not null default 1, password_updated_at, status (`pending\|active\|locked\|disabled\|deleted`), locale, timezone, theme (`system\|dark\|light`), display_name, last_login_at, failed_login_count, locked_until, is_test bool, platform_role (`none\|platform_owner\|platform_admin\|platform_support\|platform_auditor`), deleted_at | No `org_id` (users span orgs). Email normalization: NFKC, lowercase, trim; plus-addressing preserved. |

Rows reach it only through `waf_events_ingest` (below); `hdd_proxy` never writes it directly. |
| `waf_events_ingest` | the same columns as `waf_events`, plus `received_at` | **Ordinary `UNLOGGED` table, no RLS, no partitioning.** `hdd_proxy` and `hdd_dns` hold `INSERT` (and `COPY`) on it and nothing else; they cannot `SELECT` it. `hdd_worker` drains it in batches of at most 5,000 rows, grouped by `org_id`: for each group it runs `SET LOCAL app.org_id = ...` and inserts into `waf_events` (so RLS applies and COPY semantics are respected), then deletes the drained rows in the same transaction. Rows older than 10 minutes without an `org_id` match are moved to a quarantine counter and dropped. **Durability contract:** `UNLOGGED` rows can be lost on a crash, which is acceptable for telemetry; bans and audit rows never travel this path (bans are written to `ip_bans` by the API/worker, and the proxy's local jail keeps enforcing from memory and the kernel set). |

### B5.12 Redis keys and channels

| Key / channel | Type | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hdd:banned_ips` | zset (score = expiry epoch) | Platform-wide jail membership. |
| `hdd:ban:{org}:{site}:{ip_key}` | hash + TTL | Ban detail for fast lookup and display. |
| `hdd:ban:g:{ip_key}` | hash + TTL | Platform-wide ban. |
| `hdd:rl:{site}:{scope}:{key}` | sorted set / Lua sliding window | Rate limiter state. |
| `hdd:offence:{org}:{ip_key}` | counter + TTL | Progressive TTL ladder with decay. |
| `hdd:acme:challenge:{token}` | string + TTL | HTTP-01 and DNS-01 values (Postgres fallback). |
| `hdd:sess:{session_hash}` | hash + TTL | Session cache. |
| `hdd:chal:nonce:{nonce}` | string + TTL | Challenge replay protection. |
| `hdd:cred:{site}:{user_hmac}` | counter + TTL | Per-username failure tracking (HMAC key per site). |
| `hdd:camp:{site}:{sig}` | hll / set + TTL | Rotating-IP campaign detection. |
| `hdd:shield:state` | string (JSON, revisioned) | Current shield state for all nodes; `hdd-shield` is the only writer. |
| `hdd:fw:ack:{revision}` | hash + TTL | Firewall agents acknowledge a ban-set revision (reconcile proof). |
| `hdd:cache:purge` | pub/sub | Cache purge requests (key or tag). |
| `hdd:node:{id}:hb` | string + TTL (15 s) | Node heartbeat for `platform_nodes`. |
| `hdd:events:{site}` | pub/sub | Per-site live event feed for SSE (bounded, sampled under load). |
| `hdd:events:config`, `hdd:events:ban`, `hdd:events:unban`, `hdd:events:notify` | pub/sub | Every message carries a monotonic `revision`; a consumer that sees a gap or reconnects resyncs from Postgres immediately (does not wait for the 30 s timer). |

All of these keys and channels are accessed through the `KvStore`, `Bus` and `Limiter` traits of `hdd-common::kv` (R-31). The Redis backend implements them with Redis; the in-process backend of the `local` profile implements the same semantics (TTL, atomic increment and compare operations, ordered revisions on the bus) and is checked by the same conformance suite (T-0562). Extra keys: `hdd:gate:sess:{site}:{token_hash}` (access-gate session, hash + TTL), `hdd:flow:{site}:{flow}:{key}` (business-flow counters and sequence state, hash + TTL), `hdd:lo:{ua_hash}` (local loopback identity registry, local profile only).

Proxy and DNS hold immutable compiled `Arc<Snapshot>` values swapped atomically (`ArcSwap`) plus `moka` caches. After every swap they also write the snapshot atomically to `HDD_SNAPSHOT_CACHE_DIR` (the last-known-good snapshot, C18.11) so a restart without Postgres or Redis still serves with the last good policy. Migrations are expand/contract only, each tested forward and with a restore from backup.

## B6. API catalog (`hdd-api`, JSON over HTTPS, base `/api/v1`)

### B6.1 Conventions

- Shorthand: `O` = `/api/v1/orgs/{org}`; `D` = `O/domains/{dom}`; `P` = `/api/v1/platform`. Org is addressed by slug or `org_` id; domain by `dom_` id.
- Auth: browser sessions (cookie, CSRF header on mutations) are accepted **only** on the same-origin mounts `app.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}/api/v1/*` and `admin.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}/api/v1/*` (B2.1). `Authorization: Bearer hdd_<prefix>_<secret>` API keys are the only credential accepted on `api.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}`. Public routes are marked `public`.
- Errors: RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with `type` = `https://docs.{{PLATFORM_DOMAIN}}/errors/<slug>`, `code` = `ERR-...` (B7), `request_id`, optional `errors[]` with JSON-pointer field paths. No stack traces, no internal hostnames.
- Pagination: cursor (`?limit=50&cursor=...`, max 200); response `{data:[...], next_cursor}`. Filters are explicit query parameters; unknown parameters are rejected with `ERR-VAL-002`.
- Concurrency: `ETag` on GET of mutable resources, `If-Match` required on PATCH/PUT/DELETE of those resources (`ERR-CONC-001` on mismatch, `428` if missing). Idempotency: `Idempotency-Key` header on every POST that creates a resource or triggers a job.
- Rate limit classes: `auth` (strict), `read`, `write`, `export`, `stream`, `public`. Responses carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset`, and `Retry-After` on 429.
- Streaming: Server-Sent Events with `Last-Event-ID` resume; heartbeat comment every 15 s; per-connection bounded buffer; a slow consumer is disconnected, not buffered without bound.
- Versioning: the path version is stable; breaking changes require `v2`. Deprecations carry `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers and a changelog entry.
- Every endpoint below has: OpenAPI entry, permission check, audit event where it mutates, metric, and a generated contract test (rule in section 0.7 `[API]`).

### B6.2 Authentication and account

| Method and path | Auth | Permission / class | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /auth/signup` | public | auth | Always 202; enumeration-safe; policy and abuse controls. |
| `POST /auth/verify-email` | public | auth | Token in body; single use. |
| `POST /auth/resend-verification` | public | auth | Always 202; rate-limited by IP, email-HMAC. |
| `POST /auth/login` | public | auth | Returns `next: mfa\|passkey\|done`. |
| `POST /auth/login/mfa/totp` | pending | auth | |
| `POST /auth/login/mfa/recovery` | pending | auth | Consumes one code. |
| `POST /auth/login/webauthn/options` | public/pending | auth | |
| `POST /auth/login/webauthn/verify` | public/pending | auth | |
| `POST /auth/logout` | session | auth | Revokes the session. |
| `POST /auth/forgot-password` | public | auth | Always 202. |
| `POST /auth/reset-password` | public | auth | Token + new password; revokes sessions. |
| `POST /auth/reauth` | session | auth | Step-up; returns `step_up_until`. |
| `GET /auth/session` | session | read | User, orgs, csrf token, permissions summary. |
| `POST /auth/invitations/accept` | session or public | auth | Binds membership. |
| `GET /me`, `PATCH /me` | session | PERM-account.self | Profile, locale, timezone, theme. |
| `POST /me/password` | session + reauth | PERM-account.self | |
| `POST /me/email/change`, `POST /me/email/confirm` | session + reauth | PERM-account.self | |
| `GET /me/sessions`, `DELETE /me/sessions/{id}`, `POST /me/sessions/revoke-others` | session | PERM-account.self | |

## B7. Error catalog (RFC 9457 problem types)

`type` URL slug is the lowercase code. User-facing `title`/`detail` are i18n keys; they never reveal whether an account exists, never include internal hostnames, rule names (for visitors) or stack traces.

| Code | HTTP | Title (English key text) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ERR-VAL-001 | 422 | Invalid request body | `errors[]` has JSON-pointer paths. |
| ERR-VAL-002 | 400 | Unknown query parameter | Unknown parameters are rejected. |
| ERR-VAL-003 | 413 | Payload too large | Per-endpoint body cap. |
| ERR-VAL-004 | 415 | Unsupported media type | |
| ERR-VAL-005 | 422 | Value outside allowed range | |
| ERR-AUTH-001 | 401 | Authentication required | |
| ERR-AUTH-002 | 401 | Email or password is incorrect | Identical for unknown email, wrong password. |
| ERR-AUTH-003 | 401 | Verification code is incorrect or expired | |
| ERR-AUTH-004 | 429 | Too many attempts, try again later | With `Retry-After`; does not reveal lock cause. |
| ERR-AUTH-005 | 403 | Email verification required | Only after a correct password. |
| ERR-AUTH-006 | 403 | Multi-factor setup required | Carries redirect to S-030. |
| ERR-AUTH-007 | 401 | Session expired | |
| ERR-AUTH-008 | 403 | Re-authentication required | Step-up; client opens S-032. |
| ERR-AUTH-009 | 400 | Link is invalid or has expired | Verify/reset/invite tokens. |
| ERR-AUTH-010 | 422 | Password does not meet the policy | Lists unmet rules (length, breached, too common). |
| ERR-AUTH-011 | 403 | Account disabled | Generic wording. |
| ERR-AUTH-012 | 401 | API key invalid | No hint about prefix existence. |
| ERR-AUTH-013 | 403 | API key lacks the required scope | |
| ERR-AUTH-014 | 403 | Read-only impersonation session | Any non-GET during impersonation. |
| ERR-AUTH-015 | 403 | Access from this network is not allowed | Admin surface CIDR block (generic). |
| ERR-AUTH-016 | 400 | CSRF validation failed | |
| ERR-AUTH-017 | 409 | Passkey already registered | |
| ERR-AUTH-018 | 400 | Passkey verification failed | |
| ERR-PERM-001 | 403 | You do not have permission for this action | Names the permission ID only to org members. |
| ERR-PERM-002 | 404 | Not found | Used instead of 403 for cross-tenant resources (no existence leak). |
| ERR-PERM-003 | 403 | Not allowed while viewing as a customer | Impersonation sessions are read-only (T-0422). |
| ERR-RATE-001 | 429 | Rate limit exceeded | Class and reset time in headers. |
| ERR-RATE-002 | 429 | Quota exceeded | Plan quota; links to S-085. |
| ERR-TENANT-001 | 403 | Organization is suspended | API keys and writes are refused; read-only export remains available (T-0423). |
| ERR-ANALYTICS-001 | 422 | Time range too large for the requested granularity | Limits per granularity are in the response (T-0442). |
| ERR-ANALYTICS-002 | 504 | Analytics query exceeded its time budget | Narrow the range or filters (T-0442). |
| ERR-CONC-001 | 412 | Resource changed, reload and retry | `If-Match` mismatch. |
| ERR-CONC-002 | 428 | If-Match header required | |
| ERR-IDEMP-001 | 409 | Idempotency key reused with a different request | |
| ERR-ORG-001 | 409 | Organization slug unavailable | |
| ERR-ORG-002 | 403 | Organization suspended | |
| ERR-ORG-003 | 409 | Pending invitation exists | |
| ERR-ORG-004 | 409 | An organization must keep at least one owner | |
| ERR-ORG-005 | 422 | Role not allowed for this action | |
| ERR-DOM-001 | 422 | Domain name is not valid | IDNA/PSL failures. |
| ERR-DOM-002 | 409 | Domain is already protected by another account | Offers the dispute flow. |
| ERR-DOM-003 | 422 | Domain is reserved or not allowed | Platform domain, public suffixes, HDD names. |
| ERR-DOM-004 | 409 | Ownership has not been verified | |
| ERR-DOM-005 | 409 | Domain is not in a state that allows this action | |
| ERR-DOM-006 | 422 | Domain limit reached for your plan | |
| ERR-DOM-007 | 409 | Delegation not detected yet | Carries observed NS. |
| ERR-DNS-001 | 422 | Record is not valid for this type | |
| ERR-DNS-002 | 409 | Conflicting record (CNAME with other data) | |
| ERR-DNS-003 | 422 | Only A, AAAA and CNAME records can be proxied | |
| ERR-DNS-004 | 422 | Mail records cannot be proxied | |
| ERR-DNS-005 | 409 | Change would remove records required for the domain to work | |
| ERR-DNS-006 | 422 | Zone import contains unsupported record types | Lists them. |
| ERR-DNS-007 | 409 | Zone size limit reached | |
| ERR-TLS-001 | 422 | Certificate and key do not match | |
| ERR-TLS-002 | 422 | Certificate does not cover the domain | |
| ERR-TLS-003 | 422 | Certificate chain is incomplete or untrusted | |
| ERR-TLS-004 | 429 | Certificate issuance is rate limited by the authority | Includes next attempt. |
| ERR-TLS-005 | 409 | CAA record forbids issuance | |
| ERR-TLS-006 | 422 | HSTS value is not allowed yet | Staged ramp rule. |
| ERR-ACME-001 | 409 | Certificate order is already in progress for this name | Idempotent re-request returns the existing order. |
| ERR-ACME-002 | 422 | Domain validation failed | Carries the challenge type and a safe, plain-language cause (not the CA's raw text). |
| ERR-ACME-003 | 503 | DNS challenge is waiting for the secondary nameserver | `hidden_primary` only; includes the next check time (T-0396). |
| ERR-ACME-004 | 429 | Certificate authority rate limit reached | Includes `Retry-After` and which limit (duplicate certificate, failed validation, new orders). |
| ERR-ACME-005 | 409 | CAA record forbids this authority | Shows the offending CAA set. |
| ERR-ACME-006 | 502 | Certificate authority is unreachable or returned an error | Transient; retried with backoff. |
| ERR-ACME-007 | 422 | Production issuance is not approved | Staging only until the operator approves (T-0538). |
| ERR-ORIGIN-001 | 422 | Origin address is not allowed | SSRF guard; generic reason class only. |
| ERR-ORIGIN-002 | 422 | Origin port is not allowed | |
| ERR-ORIGIN-003 | 502 | Origin did not respond | Connectivity test result. |
| ERR-ORIGIN-004 | 502 | Origin certificate could not be verified | No downgrade offered silently. |
| ERR-ORIGIN-005 | 422 | Origin points back to this platform | Loop detection. |
| ERR-WAF-001 | 422 | Rule expression is not supported | Diagnostics with position. |
| ERR-WAF-002 | 422 | Rule expression is too large or too complex | |
| ERR-WAF-003 | 422 | Country rules require a GeoIP database | |
| ERR-WAF-004 | 409 | Revision conflict | |
| ERR-WAF-005 | 422 | Exception must have an expiry | |
| ERR-WAF-006 | 409 | Safe mode is active | |
| ERR-WAF-007 | 422 | Change would block your own address | Self-lockout guard; carries preview. |
| ERR-BAN-001 | 404 | IP is not banned | |
| ERR-BAN-002 | 409 | Ban would affect your own address or a never-ban entry | |
| ERR-BAN-003 | 422 | Invalid IP or CIDR | |
| ERR-BAN-004 | 409 | Ban list limit reached | Oldest-expiry eviction explained. |
| ERR-APPEAL-001 | 404 | Ray ID not found or expired | Visitor-facing, generic. |
| ERR-APPEAL-002 | 429 | Too many appeals | |
| ERR-HOOK-001 | 422 | Webhook URL is not allowed | SSRF guard. |
| ERR-HOOK-002 | 502 | Test delivery failed | |
| ERR-KEY-001 | 422 | Scope not permitted for your role | |
| ERR-REPORT-001 | 422 | Report parameters are invalid | |
| ERR-SYS-001 | 503 | Service temporarily unavailable | Maintenance or dependency down. |
| ERR-SYS-002 | 500 | Unexpected error | Carries `request_id` only. |
| ERR-SYS-003 | 503 | Platform is in maintenance mode | |
| ERR-SYS-004 | 503 | Signups are temporarily paused | |
| ERR-PLAT-001 | 403 | Reason is required for this access | Platform support access. |
| ERR-PLAT-002 | 409 | Operation blocked by the never-ban list | |
| ERR-PLAT-003 | 409 | Rule pack rollout already in progress | |
| ERR-PLAT-004 | 422 | Signature verification failed | Upgrade/pack. |
| ERR-LOCAL-001 | 409 | This action is not available in the local runtime profile | For example full nameserver delegation, kernel firewall, XDP, `saas` mode. |
| ERR-LOCAL-002 | 422 | LAN exposure needs the acknowledgement | Names the exact acknowledgement string. |
| ERR-LOCAL-003 | 403 | Request host or origin is not allowed | DNS-rebinding and cross-site defense for the control plane; no detail about allowed names. |
| ERR-LOCAL-004 | 503 | The embedded database is starting or unavailable | Carries a retry hint; `hdd-local doctor` explains. |
| ERR-HOSTING-001 | 422 | A hosting requirement is not met | `errors[]` lists failed checks with remediation keys. |
| ERR-GATE-001 | 401 | Authentication required for this area | Visitor-facing; no information about the protected application. |
| ERR-GATE-002 | 403 | Access to this area is not permitted | Visitor-facing; identical for unknown user and wrong secret. |
| ERR-GATE-003 | 429 | Too many attempts, try again later | Visitor-facing; counts toward credential-stuffing policy. |
| ERR-GATE-005 | 429 | Too many verification attempts | Visitor-facing; returned before any hashing when the per-address bucket or the hashing semaphore is exhausted. |
| ERR-GATE-004 | 409 | This rule would lock out your current session or address | Self-lockout guard (R-19); `acknowledge_self_lockout=true` to override. |
| ERR-SENT-001 | 422 | Model artifact signature or evaluation record is invalid | Platform-facing; the model is not loaded and the previous one stays. |
| ERR-SENT-002 | 409 | Sentinel promotion prerequisites are not met | Names the missing items (shadow days, labeled sample, false-positive budget, held-out evidence). |
| ERR-BYPASS-001 | 409 | This site can still be reached directly; block mode needs a verified lockdown | Offers lockdown instructions, the tunnel option and the typed risk acceptance (step-up, audited). |
| ERR-BYPASS-002 | 401 | Origin authentication is missing or invalid | Origin-side verifier response only; never reveals the key or the expected format. |
| ERR-VKB-001 | 422 | Known-vulnerability entry or exploit signature failed validation | Platform-facing; lint, false-positive gate or signature check failed. |
| ERR-APIDISC-001 | 422 | The API description is invalid or too large | Parser error pointers, no echo of content. |
| ERR-APIDISC-002 | 409 | Enforcement would block recently observed traffic | Preview attached; `acknowledge_preview=true` to proceed. |
| ERR-FLOW-001 | 422 | The business-flow definition is invalid | JSON-pointer paths. |
| ERR-VISITOR-403 | 403 | Access denied (Ray ID) | Block page. No rule detail. |
| ERR-VISITOR-429 | 429 | Too many requests | |
| ERR-VISITOR-502 | 502 | Bad gateway | Branded. |
| ERR-VISITOR-504 | 504 | Gateway timeout | Branded. |
| ERR-VISITOR-421 | 421 | Misdirected request | h2 authority mismatch. |

## B10. Configuration catalog (environment variables; validated at startup; documented in `OPERATIONS.md`, printed by `hddctl preflight`, **no `DEV_MODE` exists**)

Secrets are accepted as `NAME` (value) or `NAME_FILE` (path to a 0600 file) or systemd credentials. Weak or missing required secrets abort startup with a clear error.

| Variable | Default | Required | Validation / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HDD_ENV_NAME | `production` | no | Label only; changes no behavior. |
| HDD_DEPLOYMENT_MODE | `owner_only` | no | `owner_only` or `saas`. |
| HDD_PLATFORM_DOMAIN | none | yes | Registrable domain. |
| HDD_API_BIND | `127.0.0.1:8000` | no | Loopback or private only unless `HDD_API_PUBLIC=true`. |
| HDD_WEB_BIND | `127.0.0.1:3000` | no | Same rule; public surfaces are reached through the proxy. |
| HDD_API_PUBLIC | `false` | no | Opt-in; logs a WARN. |
| HDD_PROXY_BIND_HTTP / HTTPS | `0.0.0.0:80` / `0.0.0.0:443` | no | Host network. |
| HDD_DNS_BIND | `0.0.0.0:53` | no | UDP+TCP. |
| HDD_DATABASE_URL | none | yes | `sslmode=verify-full` or Unix socket. |
| HDD_DATABASE_RO_URL | falls back | no | Read-only roles for proxy/DNS. |
| HDD_REDIS_URL | none | yes | TLS and auth, or Unix socket. |
| HDD_MASTER_KEY | none | yes | 32 bytes base64; escrowed offline. |
| HDD_JWT_SECRET | none | yes | At least 32 bytes; service tokens only. |
| HDD_SESSION_KEY | none | yes | 32 bytes; HMAC for cookie and session IDs. |
| HDD_CSRF_KEY | none | yes | 32 bytes. |
| HDD_CHALLENGE_KEY | none | yes | 32 bytes; rotates with overlap window. |
| HDD_EMAIL_HMAC_KEY | none | yes | 32 bytes; hashes emails in logs/attempt tables. |
| HDD_PEPPER / HDD_PEPPER_KID | none / `1` | yes | 32 bytes; the password pepper, passed to Argon2id as its native keyed `secret` parameter (not an HMAC pre-hash). `HDD_PEPPER_KID` is the id of the current pepper and is stored per user in `users.password_pepper_kid`. |
| HDD_PEPPER_PREV / HDD_PEPPER_PREV_KID | none | during rotation | The previous pepper, accepted for verification only; users are rehashed with the current pepper on their next successful login (T-0526). |
| HDD_ARGON2_M_COST_KIB / T_COST / PARALLELISM | `65536` / `3` / `1` | no | Floors enforced; benchmarked at install (T-0106). |
| HDD_SESSION_IDLE_MINUTES / ABSOLUTE_HOURS | `60` / `12` | no | Platform roles: `15` / `8` fixed minimums. |
| HDD_TRUSTED_PROXIES | empty | no | CIDRs allowed to set XFF (CDN). |
| HDD_NEVER_BAN_CIDRS | empty | no | Plus loopback, platform IPs, origin. |
| HDD_ADMIN_CIDRS | empty | no | Admin surface allowlist. |

## B11. Design system specification

The design system is the source of truth for every pixel. Tokens live in `design/tokens/*.toml`; `cargo xtask ui build` generates `hdd-ui/assets/tokens.css` (custom properties), the Rust constants used by SVG charts, and the contrast report. Components are askama macros in `hdd-ui` with CSS in cascade layers. Nothing in templates uses a literal color, size, font or shadow.

### B11.1 Principles

1. **Calm, honest, expert.** Security tools shout. HDD informs: plain words, exact numbers, clear next action. Never alarmist, never decorative fear.
2. **Show state, not decoration.** Every colored element encodes meaning; every meaning has a second non-color signal (icon, text, shape).
3. **Progressive disclosure.** Maya sees a plain summary; Sara can open the evidence; Dan can copy the API call. Same screen, three depths.
4. **Safe by design.** Dangerous actions look and behave differently: confirmation, preview, undo, scoped time boxes. Safe options are the defaults and the primary buttons.
5. **Fast and light.** Server-rendered, small CSS and JS, no layout shift, works on a 4G phone.
6. **Accessible by construction.** Components encode keyboard behavior, ARIA, focus management, and target size; a screen cannot be assembled from inaccessible parts.
7. **Dark first, light equal.** Both themes are fully designed and tested; `prefers-color-scheme` is honored; user choice persists.

### B11.2 Color tokens (verified contrast; the `xtask contrast-check` fails the build if any pair drops below target)

Targets: body text 4.5:1 (WCAG AA), large text and UI component boundaries 3:1, focus indicator 3:1 against adjacent colors, decorative borders exempt.

### B11.3 Typography

| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--font-sans` | `"Inter", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif` (Inter self-hosted WOFF2, variable, `font-display: swap`, subset to Latin plus Latin-Extended; license OFL recorded) |
| `--font-mono` | `"JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, Consolas, monospace` (self-hosted, OFL) |
| Scale (rem at 16 px root) | 0.75 (caption), 0.8125 (small), 0.875 (body-sm), 1 (body), 1.125 (lead), 1.25 (h4), 1.5 (h3), 1.875 (h2), 2.375 (h1), 3 (display) |
| Line height | 1.5 body, 1.3 headings, 1.2 display, 1.4 mono |
| Weights | 400, 500, 600, 700 |
| Measure | 65ch for prose, tables unconstrained |
| Numerals | `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for all counters, tables, and timestamps |

Text must reflow at 400% zoom and respect user font-size changes (no px font sizes in components). Users can pick "Comfortable" or "Compact" density; compact never reduces target size below 24 CSS px (WCAG 2.5.8) and defaults to 40 px for pointer targets.

| Token | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `--dur-instant` | 80 ms |

Motion only clarifies (state change, origin of overlay). Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` all transitions become instant except opacity fades up to 80 ms, spinners become static progress text, and the live feed never auto-scrolls. Nothing flashes more than three times per second.

### B11.6 Iconography

Single SVG sprite generated by `xtask ui build` from a curated list of permissively licensed icons (ISC/MIT), recorded in `design/LICENSES.md`. Icons are 20 px (default) or 16 px, `stroke: currentColor`, `aria-hidden="true"` when decorative, otherwise paired with visible text or `aria-label`. Required icon set (minimum): shield, shield-check, shield-alert, globe, server, database, lock, key, fingerprint, user, users, mail, bell, search, filter, download, upload, copy, check, x, alert-triangle, alert-octagon, info, help-circle, clock, calendar, refresh, play, pause, stop, trash, edit, plus, minus, chevron-*, arrow-*, external-link, eye, eye-off, settings, sliders, activity, bar-chart, map, route, terminal, code, file-text, git-branch, rewind, undo, flag, bug, radar, ban, unlock, wifi-off, cloud-orange (custom), cloud-grey (custom), sun, moon, monitor.

### B11.7 Layout

- **App frame:** fixed top bar 56 px; left sidebar 240 px expanded / 64 px collapsed; content area scrolls; skip link "Skip to main content" is the first focusable element; landmarks `banner`, `navigation` (labeled), `main`, `complementary`, `contentinfo`.
- **Responsive behavior:** below 1024 px the sidebar becomes a drawer opened by a labeled menu button; tables become cards (stacked key-value) below 640 px only where horizontal scrolling would hide primary data; otherwise tables scroll horizontally inside a focusable region with a visible scroll hint.
- **Page header:** breadcrumbs, title (h1, exactly one per page), status pills, primary action on the right; secondary actions in a menu.
- **Grid:** 12 columns above 1024 px, 4 below; cards use CSS grid `auto-fit` with minimum 280 px.
- **Reading pages (public, docs):** single column 65ch with sticky table of contents above 1024 px.

### B11.8 Component inventory

Every component page in the gallery (T-0047) shows: anatomy, variants, states (default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error, read-only), keyboard map, ARIA contract, do/don't, and the automated a11y result. Components are listed with their contract.

| Component | Contract (summary) |
| --- | --- |
| Button / IconButton | Variants primary, secondary, ghost, danger, link-style. `aria-busy` while loading; icon-only buttons require `aria-label`; never `div` role=button. Disabled buttons keep focusable only when explaining why via `aria-describedby`. |
| Link | Underlined in prose; external links show icon plus `rel="noopener noreferrer"`; `aria-current="page"` in nav. |
| TextInput / Textarea | Visible label always; helper text via `aria-describedby`; error via `aria-invalid` and linked message; never placeholder-as-label; autocomplete tokens set (WCAG 1.3.5). |
| PasswordInput | Show/hide toggle (button, `aria-pressed`), paste allowed (WCAG 3.3.8), strength meter (text + meter role), rule checklist; never reveals by default. |
| OTPInput | Single input with `inputmode="numeric"`, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, `pattern`; not six separate boxes (screen readers and paste). |
| Select / Combobox / MultiSelect | Native `select` for simple cases; ARIA 1.2 combobox with listbox for search; keyboard: arrows, Home/End, type-ahead, Esc; selected tags removable by keyboard. |
| Checkbox / Radio / Switch | Native inputs; switch is a checkbox with `role="switch"`; label click target covers the row; state text ("On"/"Off") not color only. |
| TagInput (IP/CIDR/hostnames) | Validates on commit; paste of lists splits on newline/comma/space; per-tag error; keyboard removal; max count. |
| CopyField / CodeBlock | Read-only monospace with a copy button; announces "Copied" through a polite live region; long values wrap or scroll in a focusable region. |
| FileDropzone | Button-first (works without drag); shows type/size limits; validates client-side for UX and server-side for truth. |
| FormField / ErrorSummary | On submit with errors, focus moves to the summary (`role="alert"` once) with links to fields. |
| Card / StatCard | StatCard: label, value (tabular), delta with text, optional sparkline; the whole card is not a link unless it is one control. |
| Badge / StatusDot / SeverityPill | Always icon + text; `title` is never the only description. |
| Tooltip / Popover | Tooltip: description only, never required to operate; shown on focus and hover; dismissible with Esc; persistent hover (WCAG 1.4.13). Popover: focus management, Esc, return focus. |
| Menu / Dropdown | `button` + `menu` pattern with roving focus; typeahead; `aria-haspopup`. |
| Modal / Drawer / ConfirmDialog | Native `<dialog>` with focus trap, labelled by heading, returns focus, inert background; ConfirmDialog supports type-to-confirm (user types the exact resource name), a visible consequences list, and a default focus on the safe action. |
| Toast | `role="status"` (polite) or `role="alert"` (errors only); minimum 8 s, pauses on hover/focus, never the only place an error is shown; has an Undo action where reversible. |
| Banner / Alert | Variants info, success, warning, danger; `role="status"` or `alert`; dismissible only for non-critical. |
| Tabs | Roving tabindex; `aria-selected`; panels labelled; deep-linkable via URL (not JS-only). |
| Breadcrumbs | `nav` with `aria-label`; last item `aria-current`. |
| Pagination (cursor) | Prev/next with counts; keyboard; URL state. |
| DataTable | Semantic `table`; sortable headers as buttons with `aria-sort`; column visibility menu; density toggle; row selection with `aria-checked`; sticky header; virtualized only for live feeds above 500 rows (keeping row semantics via `aria-rowcount`/`aria-rowindex`); bulk action bar; empty state; filter chips from URL; CSV export. |
| KeyValueList | `dl` semantics. |
| Timeline | Ordered list with timestamps (`<time>`), status icons plus text. |
| Stepper / Wizard | Ordered steps with `aria-current="step"`; each step is a URL; back/next preserve input; progress persisted server-side; leave-guard for unsaved changes. |
| Skeleton / Spinner / ProgressBar | Skeletons only for loads over 300 ms; `aria-busy` region; progress has `role="progressbar"` with `aria-valuenow` or indeterminate text. |
| EmptyState / ErrorState | Illustration optional (decorative SVG); explains why empty, what to do next with a primary action; error state shows request ID and retry. |
| CommandPalette | `role="dialog"` + combobox listbox; opened by Ctrl/Cmd+K; results grouped; shows only permitted actions; recent items; Esc closes. |
| ThemeToggle / LocaleSwitcher / DensityToggle | Persist to account and cookie; no flash of wrong theme (inline-free: theme attribute set by a nonce script that is size-capped and CSP-allowed, or by server from cookie). |
| NotificationBell | Count in text for screen readers; opens a popover list with mark-all-read; polite live region for new items. |
| RayIDChip | Monospace, copy button, link to event; format validated. |
| IPChip | IP with country flag (decorative, plus text code), ASN label, actions menu (ban, allow, lookup, copy); IPv6 shown with /64 key note. |
| CountdownBadge | Remaining ban time updating each second only when visible; static text for reduced motion and screen readers (`aria-live="off"`, updated every 30 s). |
| PayloadViewer | Shows redacted evidence with the matched span highlighted using background + underline (not color only), always HTML-escaped, `white-space: pre-wrap`, 512-byte cap indicator; never rendered as markup. |
| ReadinessRing | SVG ring with textual score and list below; announces "Protection readiness 74 out of 100"; footnote "Measures configuration completeness, not security." |
| CloudToggle | Orange/Grey toggle button pair with explicit text "Proxied" / "DNS only", icon, and an explanatory popover; changing triggers consequence text. |
| NameserverCard | Two copy fields, status poller (`aria-live="polite"`), last checked time, next check time. |
| VerificationPoller | Server-driven status with next-check countdown; manual "Check now" rate-limited. |
| LiveFeed (SSE) | List/table with pause/resume (button), buffered count "12 new events", never auto-scrolls while focus is inside, announces batches politely at most every 10 s. |
| ChartKit | Server-rendered SVG with `role="img"` and an accessible data table alternative (toggle "View as table"); direct labels; patterns for series; tooltip island is optional enhancement. |
| WorldMap | SVG choropleth with ranked list alternative; keyboard-focusable countries in the list; legend with numbers. |
| RuleBuilder | Rows of condition fields; add/remove; AND/OR groups with explicit group labels; keyboard reorder via move up/down buttons (WCAG 2.5.7); live validation messages from the server; test panel. |
| DiffViewer | Side-by-side and unified; changes announced as "added/removed" text, not color only. |
| MarkdownRender | Sanitized (`ammonia`), headings anchor links, code blocks with copy; external images blocked. |
| Avatar | Initials only (no external avatar fetching); decorative. |
| Kbd | `<kbd>` styling; shortcuts listed in help overlay. |

### B11.9 Interaction patterns

1. **Forms.** Single column; labels above; required fields marked in text ("required") not asterisk-only; validate on blur and submit; server is the source of truth; errors preserve input; never clear password fields except on success or explicit failure; disable the submit only while in flight; prevent double submit (idempotency key).
2. **Destructive actions.** Use ConfirmDialog with consequences list; type-to-confirm for domain removal, org deletion, global changes; offer undo toast where technically reversible (ban, rule delete within 30 s), otherwise explain irreversibility.
3. **Self-lockout guard.** Any action whose effect would match the current session's IP (ban, deny, geo-block, rule match, access list) shows a blocking warning with the exact rule and a "Run as dry-run first" link.
4. **Empty/loading/error/offline.** Every data region defines all four; the offline state is a banner with retry; list views never show a spinner longer than 300 ms without a skeleton.
5. **Time.** Show relative time with absolute time in `<time datetime>` and `title`; always UTC offset visible in tooltips; user time zone from profile.
6. **Numbers.** Locale formatting; large numbers abbreviated only in cards, exact in tables; units explicit (req/s, MB).
7. **Wizards.** Resumable; each step has "Why we ask"; never lose input on back; show what changes where (HDD vs the user's DNS provider) with distinct visual treatment ("Do this at your DNS provider" boxes).
8. **Live data.** Pause control; "N new" indicator; no scroll hijack; rate-limited announcements.
9. **Search and filters.** Filters reflect in URL; saved views; clear-all; empty-result state suggests loosening filters.
10. **Notifications.** Toasts for transient; Notification center for durable; email for out-of-band; severity maps to channels in alert rules.
11. **Help.** Contextual "Learn more" links to docs pages; consistent help placement (WCAG 3.2.6).
12. **Honest data.** Unknown values display "Unknown" with the reason, never zero.

### B11.10 Data visualization rules

1. Choose the simplest form that answers the question: line for time series, bar for category comparison, stacked bar for composition over time, ranked horizontal bar for top-N, heatmap for hour-by-day, choropleth only with a ranked table alongside.
2. Axes labeled with units; zero baseline for bars; time axis in user time zone; gaps shown as gaps, not interpolated zeros.
3. Direct labels over legends where feasible; legend order matches visual order; limit to 8 series (then "Other").
4. Color-blind-safe palette (B11.2) plus patterns for fills; severity uses icon + label.
5. Every chart has a text summary ("Blocked requests peaked at 14:10 with 412") and a "View as table" toggle.
6. Interaction is progressive: tooltips and crosshair enhance; all information is available without them.
7. Charts are server-rendered SVG so they render without JavaScript and print cleanly; no animation by default.
8. Never chart fabricated or interpolated data; sparse data shows the sparse state.

### B11.11 Accessibility contract (summary of WCAG 2.2 AA obligations the components encode)

| Criterion | Rule in HDD |
| --- | --- |
| 1.1.1 / 1.3.x | Text alternatives; semantic structure; reading order equals DOM order; orientation not locked. |
| 1.4.3 / 1.4.11 | Contrast per B11.2; control boundaries 3:1. |
| 1.4.4 / 1.4.10 | 200% text resize; reflow at 320 CSS px without two-dimensional scrolling (data tables exempt, with scroll regions). |
| 1.4.12 / 1.4.13 | Text spacing overrides survive; hover/focus content dismissible, hoverable, persistent. |
| 2.1.x | All functionality by keyboard; no traps; shortcuts can be turned off or require modifier. |
| 2.4.1 / 2.4.3 / 2.4.7 | Skip link; logical focus order; visible focus on every interactive element. |
| 2.4.11 | Focus not obscured: sticky headers and banners use `scroll-padding`; toasts never cover focused controls. |
| 2.5.7 | Drag-and-drop reorder always has move up/down buttons. |
| 2.5.8 | Targets at least 24 CSS px (defaults 40). |
| 3.2.6 | Consistent help location. |
| 3.3.1 / 3.3.3 / 3.3.4 | Errors identified in text, suggestions given, reversible or confirmed for destructive. |
| 3.3.7 | Redundant entry avoided: wizard keeps entered values; DNS scan reuses domain. |
| 3.3.8 | Accessible authentication: paste allowed in password fields, password managers supported, passkeys offered, no cognitive tests (the proof-of-work challenge is automatic). |
| 4.1.2 / 4.1.3 | Names, roles, values; status messages via live regions. |

Automated checks (axe oracle) catch a subset; each screen also has a recorded keyboard-walkthrough test and, for the 12 critical flows, a screen-reader checklist run manually by the operator or a recorded exception (T-0069).

### B11.12 Voice and tone

- Plain words; short sentences; active voice; second person. "Your domain is protected in monitor mode. Nothing is blocked yet." not "WAF is operating in non-blocking observation state."
- Say what happened, why it matters, what to do. Errors blame the situation, not the user.
- Numbers over adjectives. "412 requests blocked in the last hour" not "many attacks".
- Security terms get a one-line explanation on first use with a docs link.
- No fear language, no emojis in product UI, no humor in errors, no exclamation marks except success confirmations used sparingly.
- Every string is an i18n key in `i18n/en/*.ftl`; keys are semantic (`domain-add-step2-title`), never sentences.
