### B12.2 Detailed specifications of critical screens

#### S-042 Add-domain wizard

Eight resumable steps; URL `/app/o/{org}/domains/new?step=n`; the draft `sites` row is created at step 1; leaving shows a leave-guard only when unsaved fields exist.

1. **Enter domain.** Field accepts `example.org`, `https://example.org/path` (stripped), `www.example.org` (offers apex), Unicode (shows punycode). Validation: IDNA, registrable domain via the public-suffix list, not the platform domain, not reserved, not already claimed (dispute link), plan quota (`ERR-DOM-006`). Bulk add via multi-line paste (max 20).
2. **Scan existing DNS.** Async job with progress text; results grouped: web (A/AAAA/CNAME), mail (MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC), other (TXT/SRV/CAA/NS), unknown. Shows the current nameservers and provider guess. Offers "Import from zone file" and "Add manually". Errors: scan blocked by resolver outage shows partial results with a retry.
3. **Choose how to connect.** Cards: Full nameserver delegation (recommended), Keep my DNS provider (CNAME/A), Subdomain only. Each card lists what changes, what stays, rollback time, and prerequisites. Recommendation logic is deterministic: apex wanted and provider unknown gives full; provider supports ALIAS/CNAME flattening gives partial.
4. **Review records.** Full mode: imported records with proxy toggles (web records default orange, mail and SRV and unknown grey), parity banner, unsupported types needing acknowledgment, origin-leak warnings ("This MX record exposes your origin IP 203.0.113.10"). Partial mode: the exact records to create (CNAME or A, verification TXT, optional `_acme-challenge` CNAME) in "Do this at your DNS provider" boxes with copy buttons.
5. **Prove ownership.** TXT or HTTP file; live status; "Check now" (rate-limited). Full mode can defer proof until delegation is detected because controlling DNS is itself proof only if the registrar NS points to HDD (the platform still requires TXT first in `saas` mode).
6. **Origin.** Fields: address (hostname or IP), port, scheme, Host header (defaults to domain), SNI name, TLS verification mode, health path. "Test connection" shows DNS result, connect, TLS, status, and clear remedies; SSRF guard errors explain without echoing internal details.
7. **TLS and protection level.** Certificate plan: pre-issue via DNS-01 (full mode, or partial with the CNAME) or issue on first request (warning). Preset cards: Monitor first (default), Balanced, Strict, Vulnerable-Origin Shield; each says what it logs and bans.
8. **Go live.** Checklist of verified facts, preview commands (`curl --resolve`, hosts-file snippet, preview URL), final warnings (DS record, TTLs), rollback instructions shown before the button. After activation, a delegation or CNAME status poller runs until detected; the page then shows the first requests arriving.

States: draft resume list on S-041; failure at any step keeps previous inputs; network error shows retry.

#### S-044 Protection readiness

Score 0 to 100 with ring and the footnote. Groups and example checks (weights sum to 100; exact weights in T-0172):
- **Traffic** (20): traffic flows through HDD (last proxied request within 24 h), delegation or CNAME verified, no grey web records that expose the same hostnames.
- **Encryption** (15): valid certificate with more than one quarter lifetime remaining, HTTPS redirect on, origin verification mode strict, HSTS enabled (partial credit by max-age).
- **Origin** (20): lockdown applied, secret header verified, origin IP not found in own DNS/headers/mail, origin health check passing.
- **Detection** (25): WAF in block mode (monitor gives partial), SQLi shield enabled, all hard categories on, auth endpoints declared, outbound filter on.
- **Abuse controls** (10): rate limits on auth endpoints, challenge configured, scanner policy on.
- **Operations** (10): alert channel tested, MFA required for org, DNS backup exported, appeals enabled.
Each check shows `Pass`, `Partial`, `Fail` or `Unknown (reason)`, a plain "why it matters", and a fix link. Unknown never scores as pass.

#### S-057 Vulnerable-Origin Shield

Regions: (1) explainer card using `shield-title/body/limit`; (2) master toggle with strictness `Balanced` or `Paranoid` and consequence text; (3) **Ban behavior** panel: "Ban on first clear attack" (on by default), TTL ladder editor (1 h, 6 h, 24 h, 7 d), cross-site handling explanation, CGNAT option "challenge instead of ban"; (4) **Declared login and form endpoints** table (path, method, kind, detected or declared, strict) with auto-detected suggestions; (5) **SQL injection** panel listing subtypes (tautology, comment termination, UNION, stacked, time-based, error-based, out-of-band, schema discovery, evasion) each with an enable toggle (default on, cannot all be disabled in Paranoid) and counters; (6) **Learned parameter shapes** (opt-in) with enforce toggle in log or block; (7) **Try a payload** box: textarea + vector selector + field type; submit calls the inspect API and shows verdict, matched subtype, ban-would-apply, no request is sent to the origin; includes quick fills of the six canonical payloads; (8) **Outbound leak protection** link; (9) **Limits** statement with link to S-003.

#### S-059 Rule builder

Header: name, description, priority, scope (path pattern and methods), expiry (required for `allow` rules). Conditions: rows of `[field] [operator] [value]` joined by AND within a group and OR between groups; fields: URI path, query, any parameter name/value, header, cookie, method, client IP/CIDR, country, ASN, user agent, body contains, JSON path, request size; operators: equals, contains, starts/ends with, matches regex (restricted subset with diagnostics), in list, in CIDR, greater/less than. Actions: block, ban, challenge, log, allow. Preview panel: human-readable sentence ("Block when the path starts with /admin and the country is not NL"), validation messages from the server with source positions, sample tester (paste a request or URL) calling `/rules/test`, link to dry-run. Self-lockout warning if the rule would match the current IP. Save creates a revision with the author and note.

#### S-065 Live threat monitor

Table columns: time, Ray ID chip, IP chip (country, ASN), domain, category + subtype, action, rule, vector/field, redacted payload excerpt (escaped, 120 characters, expand in drawer), status. Controls: Pause/Resume, "N new events", filters (category, action, severity, IP, rule, vector, country), density, column visibility, saved views, export. SSE connection status indicator in text ("Live", "Reconnecting in 4 s", "Paused"). Row Enter opens S-066 in a drawer (focus returns to row). Stored-XSS payloads render escaped. Bulk selection supports ban and exception creation. Virtualization applies above 500 rows with `aria-rowcount`.

#### S-067 IP jail

Columns: IP/CIDR, reason, rule and subtype, created, expires with countdown, hits since ban, scope (domain, org, platform), source (auto or manual). Actions: Unban, extend, convert to allowlist exception (with reason), add manual ban (form with self-lockout guard and collateral-risk hint: estimated shared-address risk from rDNS/ASN class and recent distinct sessions). Unban shows "Effective within 2 seconds" and then a live verification status (L7, kernel). Empty state: "No active bans".

#### S-140 Block page (visitor)

Server-rendered by the proxy from a compiled template; no external requests; inline critical CSS with a nonce (the data-plane CSP allows only that nonce); dark/light via `prefers-color-scheme`; elements: tenant logo (if configured), title, body, Ray ID with copy button (progressive enhancement), "Report a mistaken block" link (if appeals enabled), footer "Protected by Hack Dev Defence" (configurable off on paid plans). For `Accept: application/json` returns `{error:"access_denied", ray_id}`. Status 403. Content never includes which rule fired.

#### S-102 Tenant detail (admin)

Header with org name, plan, status, created; tabs: Overview (usage vs quota), Domains (state, WAF mode, abuse flags), Members (roles, last active, MFA state), Abuse (reports and actions), Notes, Audit (filtered). Actions: change plan (step-up), suspend/unsuspend (reason required; customer email preview), impersonate (reason, duration), export tenant summary. Every action shows the audit event that will be written.

#### S-100 Admin overview

Cards: edge health (proxy/DNS up, config revision, p99 added latency), control health (API/web/worker, queue depth), data stores (Postgres/Redis), certificates expiring within a quarter lifetime, ban set size and kernel enforcement, shield state, attack summary last hour (top categories, top ASNs), abuse queue, signups (24 h), pending upgrades. All numbers come from real metrics; missing sources display "Unknown (reason)".

#### S-110/S-111 Infra and services

Nodes table: role, version, build commit, last heartbeat, config revision, drift indicator; services list with readiness probes and last restart; queues with depth, oldest job age, failure counts and retry actions (with confirmation).

#### S-131 Access gate

Two columns on wide screens: the rule list (path pattern, methods, policy chip, on-fail behavior, hits in 24 h, enabled toggle) and a detail editor. The template picker offers WordPress admin, phpMyAdmin and Adminer, Spring actuator, generic `/admin`, `/server-status`, `/.env` and `/.git` denial, API documentation pages. Creating a rule shows the **self-lockout preview** ("Your current address would be allowed / blocked / asked to sign in") before saving (R-19). Credentials are created with a one-time reveal; the screen never shows a stored secret. Signed links show their expiry and are revocable.

#### S-132 API discovery and schemas

Top tiles: endpoints total, approved, shadow (seen but not in any approved spec), schema coverage. Table columns: method, path template, state chip, calls (7 d), authenticated share, schema status. Row drawer: observed parameter shapes (types and length bounds only; never values), the proposed schema, approve or block actions. The enforcement panel offers `off`, `monitor`, `block`; switching to `block` first runs the preview and requires acknowledging any would-have-blocked traffic (`ERR-APIDISC-002`).

#### S-133 Business flows

Flow cards show kind, matched endpoints, active signals (velocity, time-to-complete, honey field, sequence, distinct-credential ratio, response-ratio), mode, and a sparkline of triggers. A flow opens a form with conditions and limits in plain language, plus **Simulate**, which replays recent events and lists the actions that would have fired. Defaults ship in `monitor`.

#### S-134 Coverage map

Grouped accordions per standard. Each row: category, status chip (Covered, Partial, Signal only, Not covered) with text as well as color, what is detected, how it is tested (AC and ATK IDs linking to the evidence summary), and limits. A fixed section at the end, "What HDD does not cover", is never collapsed. The page shows the date and commit of the data it was generated from.

#### S-135/S-136 Runtime, hosting and first-run setup

S-135 is a status page, not a control panel: every number is a real metric. S-136 (hosted) lists each hosting check with pass, fail or unknown (reason) and a remediation link to the exact `docs/HOSTING.md` section; it never claims uptime it cannot measure. S-136 (local `/setup`) is a four-step flow: enter the bootstrap token, create the platform owner (strong password, MFA enrollment), choose the trust option for the local certificate authority (install into the OS store with consent, or use the browser exception instructions, or HTTP-only on loopback), and run a self-test that reports its own results.

(The remaining screens follow the same structure; their task blocks in Part D specify fields, validations, states and tests in detail.)

# PART C: SECURITY ARCHITECTURE

## C1. Defense in depth

HDD protects the origin even when the origin is vulnerable by stacking independent layers. A failure in one layer must not disable the others, and each layer states how it fails.

| Layer | Threat addressed | Mechanism | Fails | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L0 Upstream scrubbing | Volumetric floods larger than the VPS uplink | Provider service (documented, escalation-tested, never claimed beyond contract) | Cannot be fixed locally; alert and DNS failover | AC-25 |
| L1 Early drop | Cheap floods, banned sources, invalid packets | XDP program (`hdd-xdp`) with nftables `raw` fallback | To `XDP_PASS`; kernel baseline remains | AC-26 |
| L2 Stack tuning | SYN floods, state exhaustion | SYN cookies, backlog sizing, NOTRACK for 53/80/443, conntrack sizing, `rp_filter` | Default kernel behavior | AC-29 |
| L3 Amplification-proofing | Reflection through HDD's DNS | No recursion, minimal `ANY`, RRL, cookies, TC=1 | Refuses | AC-28 |
| L4 DNS survivability | Loss of the VPS | External secondary, hidden-primary topology | Secondary keeps answering | AC-21, AC-28 |
| L5 Protocol hardening | Request smuggling, h2 floods, slow attacks, parser abuse | Strict HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 front end with hard limits | Rejects the request/connection | AC-14 |
| L6 Jail | Known attackers | L7 jail (platform, org, site), kernel set for proxied ports, XDP map | Local cache keeps working if Redis is down | AC-08, AC-34, AC-51 |
| L7 Behavior | Floods, brute force, scrapers, scanners | Sliding-window rate limits, bot scoring, proof-of-work challenge, credential-stuffing detection, campaign detection | Local limiter if Redis is down | AC-11, AC-44, AC-48 |
| L8 Request inspection | Injection, XSS, traversal, RCE, upload abuse, protocol/API abuse | Normalizer, hard and soft signatures, structural tokenizers, positive-security hints, virtual patches | **Never fails open** (R-26) | AC-06, AC-07, AC-09, AC-38, AC-39 |
| L9 Response inspection | Data leaks from vulnerable code | Outbound filter (DB errors, traces, secrets, versions), header policy | Passes with `partial_scan` tag beyond the window (documented limit) | AC-10 |
| L10 Origin protection | Bypass of HDD, origin discovery | Secret header, mTLS option, firewall allowlist, no origin data in DNS | Origin refuses non-HDD traffic when lockdown is applied | AC-18 |
| L11 Detection and response | Silent compromise, bad rules | Events, alerts, auto-rollback, revisions, forensics, heartbeat | Local queue; alert via heartbeat absence | AC-13, AC-16, AC-20 |
| L12 Exposure management | Unpatched components | Inventory, feeds, SLAs, virtual patches with expiry | Items stay open (R-11) | AC-30, AC-31 |
| L13 Self-protection | Attacks on HDD itself | Admin-plane isolation, MFA, hardened identity, supply-chain checks, signed updates | Locked down | AC-01, AC-33, AC-35, AC-42 |
| L14 Sensitive paths, API surface and business flows | Exposed admin areas, shadow or over-permissive APIs, abuse of valid business functions | Access gate (C19.2), API discovery and positive security (C19.3), business-flow signals (C19.4) | Gate fails closed; API and flow controls start in `monitor` and never ban on schema errors alone | AC-57 |

---

## C2. Request lifecycle (data-plane pipeline)

Each stage is a separately testable function with a time budget, a metric, and a defined failure behavior. Any stage can short-circuit with a response. Budgets are initial and re-baselined at the P18 gate.

| # | Stage | Input to output | Budget | On error or overload |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Accept and connection limits | socket to connection (per-IP caps, global caps) | 10 µs | Drop; `MET-hdd_proxy_shed_total` |
| 1 | TLS handshake | ClientHello to session; SNI to certificate | handshake | Unknown or absent SNI: `unrecognized_name` alert or failure |
| 2 | HTTP framing validation | bytes to parsed request | 50 µs | 400/431/413/501; connection closed on smuggling shapes |
| 3 | Host and route resolution | Host + SNI to site snapshot | 5 µs | Branded 404 (never a default tenant); h2 authority mismatch: 421 |
| 4 | Client IP resolution | peer + headers to `ClientIp` | 2 µs | Peer IP if peer not trusted; strip spoofable headers |
| 5 | Safe-mode check | flag to pass-through | 1 µs | n/a |
| 6 | Jail and allowlist | `ClientIp` to jail verdict | 5 µs (local), 1 ms (Redis fallback) | Local ban cache used; branded 403 with Ray ID |
| 7 | Reputation and geo policy | `ClientIp` to policy action | 10 µs | Allow if lists unavailable (documented); log |
| 8 | Reserved paths | `/__hdd/*`, ACME, verification | 20 µs | Handled by data plane, never forwarded |
| 8a | Access gate (C19.2) | site gate rules to allow, challenge or deny | 20 µs p99 for paths up to 2 KiB (longer paths are decided as gated without full canonicalization); gate sessions come from an in-process cache (5 to 10 s, invalidated over the `Bus`), Redis only on a miss | Fails closed: deny with `ERR-GATE-002` |
| 9 | Rate limiter and business-flow signals | key to allow/429/ban; flow signals (C19.4) | 5 µs p99 in-process; 1 ms p99 with Redis (counters are batched; monitor and challenge decisions never wait on the store, T-0333) | In-process limiter (the `Limiter` trait falls back to `MemoryKv` semantics) |
| 10 | Challenge and clearance | cookie + site mode to pass/challenge | 10 µs | Challenge page |
| 11 | Body acquisition | stream to bounded buffer (prefix) | per policy | `over_limit_policy` (inspect_prefix default) |
| 12 | Normalization and extraction | request to `Vec<Vector>` with raw/decoded/canonical views | 100 to 400 µs | Over budget: `over_limit_policy` |
| 12a | Flow field signals (C19.4 phase B) | declared fields to flow signals | 30 µs | Skipped with a counter; never delays the response |
| 13 | Detection | vectors to matches | p50 under 1 ms | Budget exceeded: block with 503 (never silently pass) unless mode is `monitor` |
| 14 | Decision | matches + policy + mode + exceptions to `Verdict` | 20 µs | n/a |
| 15 | Enforcement | `Verdict` to response, ban intent, event | 100 µs | Event queue full: drop event, count, still enforce |
| 16 | Upstream request build | request to origin request (strip/set headers, secret header) | 20 µs | n/a |
| 17 | Origin exchange | pool, health, timeouts, no redirects | origin | Branded 502/504; serve-stale when enabled |
| 18 | Response processing | origin response to client response | 100 µs CPU + hold window (origin body-wait during the hold is origin time, C14.9) | Outbound modes; header policy |
| 18a | Flow outcome recording (C19.4 phase C) | response status or declared marker to counters | asynchronous | Dropped with a counter; never delays the response |
| 19 | Emission | event, metrics, logs | async | Never awaited on the hot path |

### C2.1 The `Verdict` contract (`hdd-waf-core`)

```
Verdict {
  action: Pass | Block | Challenge | RateLimit | Log
  mode_applied: Off | Monitor | Log | Block
  category: Category            // sqli, xss, ... (B8 list in Appendix E7)
  subtype: Option<Subtype>      // tautology, comment_termination, union, ...
  rule_id: RuleId, rule_version: u32
  hardness: Hard | Soft | Custom | VirtualPatch
  severity: Critical | Error | Warning | Notice
  score: u16, threshold: u16
  vector: Vector                // path, query, form, json, xml, multipart, cookie, header, graphql, ws
  field: FieldRef               // name only; never the value
  field_kind: FieldKind         // password, username, email, numeric_id, search, free_text, header, filename, unknown
  evidence: Evidence            // canonical snippet <= 512 bytes after redaction, with match span
  ban: Option<BanIntent>        // reason, scope, ttl_step_hint, cross_site: bool, explain: PolicyBranch
  config_revision: u64
  truncated: bool, partial: bool
}
```

`BanIntent` is a *proposal*; the proxy's ban policy engine (C6) decides whether it becomes a ban, applying cross-site context, never-ban, allowlists and the TTL ladder. `hdd-waf-core` never performs I/O.

### C2.2 Fail-closed rules

1. An inspection error, panic caught at the task boundary, or budget overrun yields: `Block` (503 with Ray ID) in `block` mode; `Pass` plus a critical event in `monitor`/`log` modes. Never a silent pass in `block` mode.
2. Redis down: local ban cache + local limiter. Postgres down: serve from snapshot, queue events with a bounded disk spill.
3. Snapshot compile failure on update: keep the last good snapshot, alert, and mark the revision `failed`.
4. Config bus gap: resync from Postgres immediately.

---

## C3. Vulnerable-Origin Shield (doctrine)

### C3.1 Premise

Assume the origin application is exploitable and that its developers will not patch quickly. HDD must still prevent the attack from reaching the application, remove the attacker from the network path, and hide evidence of the vulnerability from the attacker. The shield is a **profile of HDD settings plus extra mechanisms**, not a separate engine.

### C3.2 Honest limits (must appear in `S-003`, `S-057` and docs)

1. Signature and structure based detection can be evaded by techniques not yet in the rules.
2. The shield cannot see attacks that do not traverse HDD (direct-to-origin traffic), so origin lockdown is part of the profile.
3. It cannot detect logic flaws (authorization bugs, business logic) except through heuristics in log mode.
4. Second-order attacks (stored now, used later) are mitigated only on the write path and by response inspection.
5. A virtual patch or the shield never marks a vulnerability fixed.

### C3.3 Mechanisms (V1 to V16)

| ID | Mechanism | Behavior | Tasks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| V1 | Ban on first clear attack | Any **hard** signature hit in `block` mode returns 403 and bans the client IP (outside cross-site subresource context) | T-0273, T-0317 |
| V2 | Declared and detected auth endpoints | Login, signup, reset, API auth paths get strict inspection, tighter rate limits, credential-stuffing detection, failure-response learning | T-0225, T-0274, T-0343 |
| V3 | Field-kind awareness | Parameter names map to field kinds (password, username, email, numeric id, search, free text) with per-kind policy (C4.6) | T-0251 |
| V4 | Learned parameter shapes | Opt-in learning mode observes legitimate traffic (type, charset, max length) per path and parameter; enforcement flags deviations | T-0272 |
| V5 | Outbound leak control | Database error strings, stack traces, secrets and version banners in responses are masked or blocked | T-0408, T-0409 |
| V6 | Write-path hardening | Bodies of POST/PUT/PATCH are always inspected (no prefix skipping below a configurable minimum), with stricter rules on fields likely to be stored (comments, profile, names) to blunt second-order injection and stored XSS | T-0276, T-0287 |
| V7 | Time-based attack detection | Parameter-correlated origin latency anomalies raise events; optional tarpit | T-0277 |
| V8 | Method and content-type hardening | Only declared methods per path; JSON endpoints require JSON content type; unexpected content types in login forms flagged | T-0298, T-0302 |
| V9 | Tripwires | Honeypot paths and parameters (`/.env`, `/phpmyadmin`, decoy login) ban on touch outside cross-site context | T-0233, T-0309 |
| V10 | Virtual patches | Scoped mitigations for specific CVEs with evidence and expiry | T-0310, T-0485 |
| V11 | Admin path restriction | Optional allowlist for `/admin`, `/wp-admin`, `/manager`, other declared admin paths | T-0232 |
| V12 | Upload quarantine | Executable and webshell uploads blocked; archive and image bombs rejected | T-0297 |
| V13 | Success-after-attack tripwire | In `monitor` mode, a 2xx/3xx login success following a request that matched hard SQLi raises a critical "possible authentication bypass" event | T-0274 |
| V14 | Origin lockdown | Direct-to-origin traffic is refused; secret header enforced | T-0405, T-0406 |
| V15 | Attack-diversity ban | One IP triggering three or more distinct attack categories within ten minutes is banned even if each was soft | T-0317 |
| V16 | Campaign detection | Many IPs hitting one endpoint with one attack signature raises the site to elevated protection (challenge for new clients on that endpoint) | T-0325 |

### C3.4 Presets

| Setting | Monitor first | Balanced | Strict | Vulnerable-Origin Shield (Balanced) | Vulnerable-Origin Shield (Paranoid) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| WAF mode | monitor | block | block | block | block |
| Paranoia level | 1 | 1 | 2 | 2 | 3 |
| Soft threshold | 5 | 5 | 4 | 4 | 3 |
| Ban on first hard hit | records `would_ban` | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| Soft-score block bans | no | after 3 in 10 min | after 2 in 10 min | after 2 in 10 min | on first |
| H2 comment-breakout in password fields | soft | soft | hard | soft (4) | hard |
| Auth endpoint strictness | normal | normal | strict | strict | strict plus rate 5/min/IP |
| Rate limit default | 60/10 s | 60/10 s | 40/10 s | 40/10 s | 30/10 s |
| Scanner tools | log | block + ban | block + ban | block + ban | block + ban |
| Outbound filter | monitor | monitor | block | block | block |
| Learned shapes | off | off | log | log | enforce |
| Challenge on anomalies | off | off | on | on | on |
| Attack-diversity ban | off | on | on | on | on |
| Recommended for | first week | most sites | login-heavy sites | known-weak or legacy apps | known-exploitable apps while a fix is pending |

Presets are data (`waf_policies` documents), shown in full on S-057/S-055, and diffable. Choosing a preset never hides what it changes.

### C3.5 Proof obligations (acceptance)

1. **AC-38 Vulnerable-origin proof (lab).** For each Vuln-Lab endpoint class (login SQLi, search SQLi, numeric-ID SQLi, reflected XSS, LFI, command injection, SSRF fetcher, upload, deserialization): (a) direct exploit succeeds against the Vuln-Lab (Class A proof, non-destructive); (b) the same exploit through HDD in `block` mode with the shield fails (403) and the client IP is banned; (c) a legitimate request on the same endpoint through HDD still succeeds.
2. **AC-39 SQLi ban matrix.** Cross product of the six mandated payloads and variants against every vector in C4.2 and each field kind: 100% `would_block` with category `sqli` and 100% bans in live enforcement outside cross-site context; benign suite 0 false positives.
3. **Oracle campaign (lab).** sqlmap (levels 1 to 3, risk 1 to 2, default tampers plus a published tamper list) through HDD: in `block` mode no data extraction succeeds and the source is banned within the first hard hit; in `monitor` mode, at least 95% of injection-bearing requests are flagged `would_block` (report the exact figure and the un-flagged request classes).

---

## C4. SQL injection doctrine

### C4.1 Goals

1. Every payload in the **mandated set** (Appendix E1.1) is a hard hit with category `sqli`, in every vector and every field kind except the documented password-field exception, regardless of case, whitespace, comment placement or encoding.
2. A hard hit in `block` mode returns 403 and bans the client IP (progressive TTL), unless the request carries cross-site subresource context (C6.5).
3. Legitimate input containing apostrophes, SQL words in prose, code samples and punctuation does not trigger (benign suite, zero false positives).
4. The detector is explainable: subtype, rule ID, evidence span, and policy branch are recorded.

The **mandated set** is the six payloads supplied by the operator:

| # | Payload | Expected tokens (conceptual) | Hard family |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| M1 | `' OR 1=1--` | quote, OR, 1, =, 1, comment | H1 tautology + H2 comment breakout |
| M2 | `' OR '1'='1` | quote, OR, string, =, unterminated string | H1 tautology |
| M3 | `admin' --` | identifier, quote, comment | H2 comment breakout (auth bypass) |
| M4 | `admin' #` | identifier, quote, hash comment | H2 |
| M5 | `admin'/*` | identifier, quote, comment-open | H2 |
| M6 | `' or 1=1 LIMIT 1 --` | quote, or, 1, =, 1, LIMIT, 1, comment | H1 + H2 |

(The v4.1 specification referred to seven payloads while listing six; this edition fixes the mandated set at these six plus the variant families below and records the discrepancy in `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` as `DEV-V5-003`.)

### C4.2 Input surfaces (vectors)

Every one of these is extracted, normalized and inspected with the same detector set, each with its own vector label:

1. URL path segments (decoded per segment), including matrix parameters (`;jsessionid=`).
2. Query string keys and values (duplicates inspected individually and concatenated).
3. `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` bodies (keys, values).
4. `multipart/form-data` text parts, part headers, filenames.
5. JSON (keys and every string leaf; numbers and booleans converted to strings for the numeric-context check; arrays and nested objects up to depth 32), including NoSQL operator keys.
6. XML text nodes, attributes, CDATA (no entity resolution).
7. GraphQL query text and `variables`.
8. Cookies (names and values).
9. Request headers: `User-Agent`, `Referer`, `Origin`, `X-Forwarded-For` (when untrusted it is already stripped; when trusted each hop is inspected), `Accept-Language`, `Content-Type` parameters, custom configured headers, and any header value not on a documented safe list.
10. WebSocket handshake and (opt-in) text frames.
11. Content under `Content-Encoding` (bounded decompression) and chunk-reassembled bodies.

### C4.3 Normalization pipeline (shared by all detectors; `hdd-waf-core::normalize`)

Three views per string (v4.1 rule retained and extended):

1. `raw`: bytes as received, lossily decoded for display only.
2. `decoded`: iterate to fixed point (maximum 3 layers) of: percent-decoding, `%uXXXX`, `+` to space (in query/form), HTML entities (named, decimal, hex, with or without trailing semicolon), JSON `\uXXXX` and `\xNN`, backslash escapes (`\'`), overlong UTF-8 rejected (flag `evasion.overlong_utf8`), invalid UTF-8 handled per policy (flag `evasion.invalid_utf8`), NFKC normalization, null-byte removal (flag `evasion.null_byte`), case folding. **Quote folding:** U+02BC, U+2018, U+2019, U+201B, U+FF07, U+00B4, U+2032 map to `'`; U+201C, U+201D, U+FF02 to `"`; U+FF1D to `=`; U+FF0D and U+2010-U+2015 to `-` (so fullwidth/lookalike payloads fold into ASCII). **Wide-byte (GBK-style) sequences** `%bf%27`, `%df%27`, `%a1%27`... flagged `evasion.multibyte_quote` and also decoded as `'`. Comment tokens (`--`, `#`, `/*`) remain visible because they are signals.
3. `canonical`: `decoded` plus: MySQL versioned comments unwrapped (`/*!50000 union*/` becomes ` union `), inline comments `/**/` replaced by a single space (their presence is recorded as a flag), whitespace variants (`%09 %0a %0b %0c %0d %a0` and Unicode spaces) collapsed to one space, adjacent string concatenations joined (`'un'+'ion'`, `'un' 'ion'`, `CONCAT('un','ion')` where trivially evaluable), `CHAR(39)`, `CHR(39)`, `0x27` evaluated to their literal characters in suspected-SQL context, `${lower:x}`-style lookups unwrapped (shared with JNDI detection), repeated whitespace/punctuation noise bounded.

Rules: the normalizer is **idempotent**, **panic-free**, and **size-bounded** (output at most 4x input, hard cap 1 MiB per string; truncated strings are flagged and handled by `over_limit_policy`). Detectors run on `decoded` and `canonical` and take the union of matches. Evidence snippets come from `decoded` (closest to what the attacker sent).

### C4.4 Detection layers

| Layer | Purpose | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D0 Prefilter | Aho-Corasick over SQL-relevant tokens; strings with none skip D1 to D3 | Tokens: `'`, `"`, `` ` ``, `--`, `#`, `/*`, `;`, `union`, `select`, `insert`, `update`, `delete`, `drop`, `exec`, `sleep(`, `benchmark(`, `waitfor`, `information_schema`, `0x`, `char(`, `or `, `and `, `\|\|`, `&&`, `xp_`, `sp_`, etc. |
| D1 Hard signature set | Linear-time regex automata for H1 to H8 (C4.5) | Each rule has an ID, subtype, examples, counter-examples |
| D2 Tokenizer and fingerprints | Own SQL tokenizer producing token classes; evaluated under three starting contexts (none, in single quote, in double quote; plus backtick for MySQL) | Fingerprint database built from labelled corpora; unknown sequences are scored softly |
| D3 Semantic evaluator | Evaluates tautologies by comparing literal operands after normalization (`'1'='1'`, `1<2`, `2>1`, `'a' LIKE 'a'`, `1 IS NOT NULL`, `NOT 0`, `true`) and recognizes quote break-out followed by boolean/comment/terminator | This is what makes M1 to M6 robust to spacing/case/encoding |
| D4 Context policy | Applies field-kind rules (C4.6) | Reduces false positives in passwords, names, prose |
| D5 Behavioral | Repeated soft hits, attack diversity, success-after-attack, latency correlation | Feeds ban policy |
| D6 Outbound | Database error strings in responses | P21 |

### C4.5 Hard signature families

Each family lists intent and canonical examples (fixtures hold the full sets, Appendix E1). Matching is case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant (any run of whitespace, comments, `+`, or `%`-encoded spaces), and applied after normalization.

**H1 Tautology / always-true predicate.** A boolean connector (`or`, `and`, `xor`, `||`, `&&`, or an opening/closing parenthesis sequence preceding them) followed by a comparison whose operands are literals or identical identifiers and which evaluates to true (or is trivially true: `1`, `true`, `'x'`).
Examples: `' OR 1=1--`, `' OR '1'='1`, `" or ""="`, `' or 'a'='a`, `1' or '1'='1`, `') or ('1'='1`, `')) or (('1'='1`, `' || '1'='1`, `' OR 1=1 LIMIT 1 --`, `or 1=1`, `or 2>1`, `' or 'x' like 'x`, `' or 1 --`, `' OR TRUE--`, `' or 1 in (1)--`, `' or 1 between 0 and 2--`.
Notes: bare `or 1=1` with no quote/parenthesis break-out is hard only in numeric contexts or when preceded by a SQL-ish token; otherwise soft 4.

**H2 Quote break-out followed by comment or terminator.** A quote/paren-closing token that closes a context, then a comment starter or statement terminator, with an identifier, string, number or `)` immediately before the quote.
Examples: `admin'--`, `admin' --`, `admin' #`, `admin'/*`, `admin')--`, `admin"--`, `' --`, `'--`, `') --`, `'; --`, `1'#`, `admin' -- -`, `admin'%23`.
Counter-examples (must not match as hard): `O'Brien`, `rock 'n' roll`, `it's -- fine` (quote not directly followed by a comment starter), `'Hello' -- he said`. **Deterministic `#` rule:** a `#` directly after a closing quote is a hard H2 match in every field kind except `password` (soft 4 under Balanced), because MySQL ignores everything after `#` and `admin'#x` is as dangerous as `admin'# `. The one exception: `'#<digit>` (for example `l'#1`, `I'#1 fan`) is **soft 2** when the field kind is `free_text` or `search` (numbering in prose), and stays hard in `username`, `email`, `numeric_id`, `unknown` kinds and on declared auth endpoints. No rule is "borderline": every boundary case lives in `tests/fixtures/sqli/h2-boundary.txt` (listed in E1.11) with its field kind and expected hardness, and the unit tests read that file.
In password fields H2 is **soft 4** (Balanced) or hard (Paranoid) because legitimate passwords may contain such sequences (C4.6).

**H3 UNION-based extraction.** `union` followed by optional `all`/`distinct` then `select`, with arbitrary comment/whitespace between; or an `ORDER BY`/`GROUP BY` ordinal probe after a break-out; `select` list with `null,null` padding or SQL metadata functions.
Examples: `' UNION SELECT NULL,NULL--`, `1 UNION ALL SELECT username,password FROM users`, `' ORDER BY 5--`, `-1 union/**/select 1,@@version,3`.

**H4 Stacked queries and dangerous statements.** `;` followed by a DDL/DML/administrative keyword; known dangerous procedures.
Examples: `'; DROP TABLE users--`, `1; UPDATE users SET`, `; EXEC xp_cmdshell('...')`, `; shutdown --`, `'; INSERT INTO`, `; DECLARE @q`, `; COPY ... TO PROGRAM`.

**H5 Blind, time-based, error-based and out-of-band functions.** Function-call syntax of: `sleep`, `benchmark`, `pg_sleep`, `waitfor delay`, `dbms_pipe.receive_message`, `dbms_lock.sleep`, `randomblob` (large), `extractvalue`, `updatexml`, `exp(~`, `floor(rand`, `utl_inaddr`, `utl_http`, `xp_dirtree`, `xp_fileexist`, `load_file`, `into outfile`, `into dumpfile`, `lo_import`, `pg_read_file`, `openrowset`, `opendatasource`, boolean-extraction shapes like `if(ascii(substring(...)))`, `case when ... then ... else ... end` with `sleep`.
Examples: `1 AND SLEEP(5)`, `'; WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'--`, `' AND (SELECT 1 FROM (SELECT SLEEP(5))a)--`, `' || pg_sleep(5)--`.

**H6 Schema and metadata discovery in SQL context.** `information_schema`, `pg_catalog`, `pg_tables`, `sysobjects`, `syscolumns`, `sys.tables`, `sqlite_master`, `all_tables`, `user_tables`, `mysql.user`, `@@version`, `version()`, `database()`, `current_user`, `@@datadir`, only when accompanied by SQL syntax (select/from/union/concat) so prose does not trigger.

**H7 Authentication-bypass idioms.** `admin' or '1'='1'--`, `' or ''='`, `'='`, `' or username like '%admin%'--`, `' having 1=1--`, `' group by x having 1=1--`, `admin' and 1=1--`. Largely covered by H1/H2; listed so each has an explicit fixture and subtype `auth_bypass`.

**H8 Evasion constructs in SQL context.** Versioned comments with SQL keywords, hex/CHAR/CHR construction of quotes or keywords near SQL tokens, scientific-notation keyword glue (`1e0union`), `/*!50000select*/`, `%00` inside keywords, concatenation of keyword parts, nested comment tricks, mixed-case keyword with comment-as-space.

### C4.6 Context policy (field kinds)

Field kind is inferred from parameter name (case-insensitive tokens), declared mappings in S-057, learned shapes, and header/cookie vector.

| Field kind | Name hints | Policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `password` | `pass`, `passwd`, `pwd`, `password`, `secret`, `pin` | H1 (with break-out), H3, H4, H5, H6 hard. H2 soft 4 (Balanced) or hard (Paranoid). All other soft signals disabled. |
| `username` / `email` | `user`, `login`, `uname`, `email`, `mail` | All hard families. Apostrophes inside email local parts and names allowed unless followed by SQL syntax. |
| `numeric_id` | `id`, `*_id`, `uid`, `pid`, `page`, `limit`, `offset`, `num`, `qty`, `count` or learned numeric | Any quote, comment, or SQL keyword is at least soft 4; any H-family is hard. |
| `search` | `q`, `s`, `search`, `query`, `keyword`, `term` | H1, H3, H4, H5, H6, H7 hard; H2 hard only when preceded by an identifier/number and followed immediately by a comment; soft signals halved for natural-language-looking input (long, high word ratio, no SQL punctuation). |
| `free_text` | `comment`, `message`, `body`, `description`, `bio`, `note` | Same as search, plus stored-content hardening (V6): `<script`, SQL stacked patterns scored harder. |
| `filename` | multipart filename | H3, H4, H5 hard. |
| `header` / `cookie` | | All hard families. |
| `unknown` | | Treated as `search`. |

### C4.7 Soft signals (additive; weights default; scoring in `docs/SCORING.md`)

| Signal | Weight |
| --- | --- |
| Quote or comment character in a `numeric_id` field | 3 |
| `--`, `#`, `/*` in a non-prose field | 2 |
| `select` and `from` both present, SQL-looking | 3 |
| `insert into`, `update ... set`, `delete from` shapes | 3 |
| `;` followed by SQL keyword (not in H4 list) | 2 |
| Boolean operator adjacent to a quote | 2 |
| `order by <n>` / `group by <n>` after break-out | 2 |
| SQL function-call syntax (`concat(`, `substring(`, `ascii(`, `char(`, `hex(`, `ifnull(`) each, capped | 2 |
| `null,null,...` padding | 3 |
| `@@` system variables | 3 |
| Long hex literal near SQL tokens | 1 |
| Quote/paren imbalance beyond threshold | 1 |
| `like '%'` patterns | 1 |

### C4.8 Evasion catalog the detector must handle (each has fixtures)

1. Case: `SeLeCt`, `oR`. 2. Whitespace: tabs, newlines, `/**/`, `%0a`, `+`, non-breaking space. 3. Comments: `--`, `-- -`, `#`, `/* */`, `/*!`, nested. 4. Encoding: single, double, triple URL encoding; `%u0027`; HTML entities; JSON escapes; mixed. 5. Unicode: fullwidth and lookalike quotes; right-single-quote U+2019; U+02BC modifier letter apostrophe. 6. Wide-byte: `%bf%27`. 7. Numeric: `1e0`, hex numbers, `0b1`. 8. Concatenation: `'a'+'b'`, `CONCAT`, `||`, adjacent literals. 9. Hex/char construction. 10. Parameter pollution: payload split across duplicate params or across array parameters `a[]=...`. 11. Content-type confusion: JSON payload in a form or vice versa; wrong content type with correct body. 12. Method override headers. 13. Chunked and padded bodies placing the payload after `inspect_body_max_bytes` (policy handles it). 14. Multipart tricks: unusual boundaries, duplicate Content-Disposition, `filename*`. 15. HTTP/2 header casing/dups. 16. Path-based injection: `/item/1'or'1'='1`. 17. Cookie-borne injection. 18. Header-borne injection (`User-Agent`, `Referer`, `X-Forwarded-For`). 19. Second-order: stored value later reused (write-path hardening + outbound). 20. Out-of-band via DNS exfil functions.

### C4.9 False-positive controls

1. The benign suite (Appendix E2) is run on every detector change; **zero** matches allowed (R-23).
2. Counter-example lists are part of every rule's test file.
3. Prose heuristics: a string with at least 5 words, sentence punctuation, and no SQL operators is treated as prose for soft signals; hard families still apply.
4. Names and addresses (apostrophes, hyphens, `#` as number sign in addresses like `Apt #4`) are explicit counter-examples; `#` is a comment signal only after a quote.
5. Developer-oriented sites (Q&A, docs) can set the `code_friendly` site option that lowers soft weights in `free_text` and requires a break-out context for H1 and H2 (hard families that need no break-out remain).
6. A per-rule, per-path exception (S-064) is the only supported way to remove a detection locally, and it requires an expiry.

### C4.10 Ban policy for SQLi (decision table; full policy engine in C6)

| Situation | Response | Ban |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mode `off` | pass | none |
| Mode `monitor` or `log`, hard hit | pass; event with `would_block=true` and `would_ban=true` | none |
| Mode `block`, hard hit, normal browsing context | 403 with Ray ID | **Yes**: IP key (IPv4 /32, IPv6 /64), ladder step by offence count; kernel set; global-jail evaluation |
| Mode `block`, hard hit, `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site\|same-site` with subresource `Sec-Fetch-Dest`, or cross-origin `Referer` | 403 with Ray ID | **No** (anti-poisoning); counted in `cross_site` counter; three in 60 s from one IP escalates to a rate-limit ban |
| Mode `block`, soft score at or above threshold | 403 | After 3 within 10 min (Balanced) or immediately (Paranoid) |
| Hard hit from a never-ban IP | 403 | **No**; critical alert "never-ban IP attempted an attack" |
| Hard hit from a tenant-allowlisted IP (`skip_inspection=false`) | pass; event `would_block` | none |
| Hard hit from a tenant-allowlisted IP with `skip_inspection=true` | pass; not inspected | none (documented risk) |
| Hard hit within a Vuln-Lab or acceptance run | 403 | Yes, with TTL 60 s (test bans) |

### C4.11 Auth-endpoint behavior

For declared or detected authentication endpoints (`auth_endpoints`): every parameter is inspected (no prefix skipping), the strict profile applies, rate limits use the auth class (Balanced default 10/min per IP per path, Paranoid 5/min), failures feed credential-stuffing detection (P17), and the V13 tripwire applies in `monitor` mode. Responses to blocked login attempts are identical to other blocks (no hint that the endpoint is special).

### C4.12 Telemetry and evidence

Every hard hit stores: Ray ID, site, client IP key, subtype, rule ID/version, vector, field name, field kind, canonical evidence window (up to 512 B, redacted), policy branch, ban ID, config revision. Metrics: `MET-hdd_sqli_hard_hits_total{subtype,vector,field_kind}`, `MET-hdd_sqli_bans_total`, `MET-hdd_sqli_cross_site_nobans_total`. The UI (S-054, S-057, S-065, S-066) shows these without the raw payload beyond the redacted evidence.

### C4.13 Test obligations

1. Fixture files: `tests/fixtures/sqli/core.txt` (the six mandated payloads + at least 300 variants), `tests/fixtures/sqli/evasion.txt`, `tests/fixtures/sqli/by-dialect/*.txt` (MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MSSQL, Oracle, SQLite, DB2/H2 where applicable), `heldout/sqli/*` (never used for tuning), `tests/fixtures/benign-sql-prose.txt` (400+).
2. Unit tests per rule (positive, negative, counter-example); proptests (normalizer idempotence, detection invariance under encodings and whitespace permutations of the mandated set); fuzz target `waf_inspect`.
3. Vector matrix test: every mandated payload through every vector in C4.2 using the inspect API and the in-process pipeline.
4. Live enforcement subset (inspect-first gate) and the lab campaigns in C3.5.
5. Mutation testing score on `hdd-waf-core` at least 80% (Appendix E4).

## C5. Attack coverage matrix (390 classes)

Every row is a requirement. `cargo xtask attack-matrix check` (T-0313) fails if a row lacks (a) at least one fixture file under `tests/fixtures/<group>/`, (b) at least one automated test that references the `ATK-nnn` ID, or (c) a mapped task. A row may be marked `limit` (known limitation) instead of detected, but then it must appear in `SECURITY.md` and the S-003 page with the reason.

**Action codes.** `BB` block and ban (hard signature, ban policy of C6 applies); `B` block without automatic ban (ban only through repetition rules); `S` soft score contribution; `C` challenge (proof of work); `L` log and alert only; `R` protocol-level rejection (400/413/414/421/431/501) with connection handling; `T` tarpit option; `P` posture finding (scanner/readiness, no runtime action); `Q` quota or limit enforced at the data plane. **PL** is the paranoia level at which the rule becomes active (1 default; 2 to 4 progressively stricter). **Ref** gives CWE and OWASP mapping (Top 10 2021 `A0x`, API Top 10 2023 `APIx`) to be rechecked against the current editions at build time.

Group acceptance: AG-01 AC-07, AC-38, AC-39; AG-02 to AG-07 AC-07, AC-09, AC-49; AG-08 AC-14; AG-09 AC-11, AC-35, AC-44; AG-10 AC-50; AG-11 AC-48; AG-12 AC-11, AC-14, AC-44; AG-13 AC-03, AC-28; AG-14 AC-26, AC-29; AG-15 AC-09, AC-31; AG-16 AC-10, AC-32; AG-17 AC-01, AC-35, AC-36, AC-42; AG-18 AC-09, AC-31, AC-61; AG-19 AC-14, AC-61, AC-62; AG-20 AC-61, AC-62; AG-21 AC-61, AC-62.

## C6. Ban, jail and appeal doctrine

### C6.1 What a ban is

A ban is a time-limited denial for one **IP key** at three possible scopes, enforced in up to four places.

| Scope | Meaning | Created by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Site | One domain denies the key | Detection on that domain; manual |
| Org | All of the org's domains deny the key | Manual; org-level policy "propagate hard-hit bans to all my domains" (default on) |
| Platform | Every domain on the installation denies the key | Platform admin; automatic global jail (C6.7) |

| Enforcement point | Mechanism | Latency budget |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L7 local cache | `ArcSwap` snapshot + `moka` cache in each proxy node, checked at pipeline stage 6 | effective within 2 s of creation across nodes (initial target 100 ms) |
| Redis | `hdd:banned_ips` zset + detail hash; pub/sub `hdd:events:ban` with revision numbers | write under 5 ms |
| Kernel | nftables set with native timeout, rule applies to TCP 80/443 and UDP 443 only | within 2 s |
| XDP | LPM-trie map (same ban stream) | within 2 s |

Postgres `ip_bans` is the durable source of truth; all other copies reconcile from it (host agent every 30 s; proxies on revision gap).

### C6.2 IP keys

IPv4 `/32`; IPv6 `/64` by default (configurable per site: `/56`, `/48`, or `/128`); API accepts either the address or the key. Bans on IPv6 /64 show the member address that triggered it. Shared-address hints (CGNAT, mobile carriers, university, corporate NAT, Tor exits, public proxies) come from ASN class data and observed distinct session counts, and are displayed in the ban dialog and the IP jail table.

### C6.3 Ban reasons and the TTL ladder

Reasons: `waf_hard_hit`, `waf_score`, `honeypot`, `rate_limit`, `credential_stuffing`, `scanner`, `manual`, `global_jail`, `reputation`, `campaign`, `attack_diversity`.

Progressive TTL by **offence count per org and IP key** within a decay window (default 30 days of quiet resets the counter):

| Offence | Default TTL | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1st | 1 hour | Hard hits and honeypot hits ban on first occurrence |
| 2nd | 6 hours | |
| 3rd | 24 hours | |
| 4th and later | 7 days (cap) | Cap is configurable down, never above 30 days without operator approval |
| Test bans (acceptance, Vuln-Lab) | 60 seconds | Dead-man TTL |
| Rate-limit bans | 10 minutes first, then ladder | Softer first step |

The ladder is per site configurable (`ban_ttl_ladder`) and shown on S-057/S-067.

### C6.4 Ban policy engine (single place that turns intents into bans)

Inputs: `BanIntent` (from detection, rate limiter, honeypot, shield), `ClientIp`, request browsing context, site policy, allowlists, never-ban list, offence counters, platform policy. Output: `Ban { scope, key, ttl, reason, evidence }` or `NoBan { reason }`. Decision table:

1. IP in platform never-ban list or org never-ban: `NoBan(never_ban)`, event severity critical, alert (a trusted address attempted an attack).
2. IP in org allowlist with `skip_inspection=false`: inspection ran; verdict recorded as `would_block`; `NoBan(allowlisted)`.
3. Mode not `block`: `NoBan(mode)`, record `would_ban`.
4. Cross-site subresource context (C6.5): block the request, `NoBan(cross_site)`, increment `cross_site` counter; if the counter reaches 3 within 60 s for the same key, convert to a `rate_limit` ban.
5. Otherwise create a ban at the scope implied by the site/org policy with the ladder TTL, set `evidence`, emit audit `AUD-ban.created`, publish to Redis and the host agent, evaluate global-jail promotion (C6.7).
6. Self-protection: a ban whose key matches the **acting admin's session IP** is refused for manual bans (`ERR-BAN-002`) unless `acknowledge_self_ban=true`; automatic bans of the acceptance runner are expected and carry the 60 s TTL.

### C6.5 Ban-poisoning resistance (cross-site context)

A detection or honeypot hit creates a ban only when the request lacks cross-site browser context. Cross-site context means: `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site` or `same-site` **and** `Sec-Fetch-Dest` is a subresource destination (`image`, `script`, `style`, `iframe`, `frame`, `font`, `audio`, `video`, `track`, `object`, `embed`, `manifest`, `worker`, `sharedworker`, `serviceworker`, `report`, `xslt`), or the `Referer` origin differs from the site origin on a subresource-style request. Such requests are blocked (403 with Ray ID), recorded, counted, and **not** banned (configurable alternative: challenge, or a 60 second ban). Forging headers only avoids the instant ban; the rate limiter's auto-ban still applies, and top-level navigations (`Sec-Fetch-Dest: document`) with attack payloads are banned. Requests with no `Sec-Fetch-*` headers (tools, scanners, curl) are treated as no browser context and ban normally. Tests: AC-34.

### C6.6 Collateral-damage controls

1. Per-site option **challenge-instead-of-ban for shared addresses**: if the IP's ASN is flagged as mobile/CGNAT/corporate or the address has had more than N distinct sessions with legitimate traffic in 24 h, soft-score blocks challenge rather than ban; hard hits still ban unless the option "never hard-ban shared addresses" is on (then 5-minute bans).
2. Ban preview on manual ban and access-list changes (S-063/S-067): who else probably shares the address.
3. Appeals (C6.8).
4. Mass-ban anomaly alert: more than `max(50, 5%)` of the active ban set created within 5 minutes triggers a critical alert and an "investigate possible poisoning" banner.
5. Ban-set cap (default 100,000 per node) with oldest-expiry eviction and a metric; eviction never removes manual or platform-wide bans.

### C6.7 Platform-wide (global) jail

Automatic promotion: the same IP key receiving **hard-hit bans on three or more distinct orgs within one hour** (not counting orgs that share an owner) is promoted to a platform ban at the ladder TTL, because it is scanning the platform's customers. Promotion is on by default in `saas` mode, off in `owner_only`, and every promoted ban is explainable (list of site-level bans as evidence) and appealable. Platform admins can add, extend or remove global bans (S-106) and manage the never-ban list (S-109), with a guard that rejects entries colliding with `test_runner.public_ip`.

### C6.8 Appeals

1. The block page offers "Report a mistaken block" if the site enabled appeals (default on).
2. The appeal form requires the Ray ID, accepts an optional contact email and a note (500 chars), and uses a light proof-of-work; rate limit 3 per hour per IP key and 10 per day per site.
3. The server verifies the Ray ID exists and belongs to the same site and the same IP key (visitors cannot appeal other people's bans); the response is identical whether verification succeeds or not (no oracle).
4. The owner sees appeals in S-069 with evidence and four actions: unban, allowlist for N days (max 30), create a scoped exception for the rule, decline with a reason. Auto-expiry after 14 days.
5. Contact emails are encrypted at rest and deleted when the appeal is resolved or expires.
6. Appeal flows never reveal rule names or detection details to the visitor.

### C6.9 Campaign and evasion defenses

1. **Campaign detector:** many distinct IP keys sending the same attack signature (rule + endpoint) within 10 minutes (default 20 keys) opens a `campaign_cluster`, raises the site to elevated protection for that endpoint (challenge new clients), and alerts.
2. **Fingerprint-linked bans:** after a hard-hit ban, the request's header-order hash and UA hash are remembered for the ban duration; new IPs presenting the same hashes together with the same attack signature are challenged first, then banned on a second hit (fingerprints are never used alone to ban).
3. **Ban evasion via IPv6 rotation:** /64 key by default; optional /56 escalation after repeated bans within a /56.
4. **Residential proxy rotation:** handled by campaign detection and challenge, not by per-IP bans alone.

### C6.10 Unban

`DELETE /bans/{ip}` clears Redis, local caches (via pub/sub), the kernel set, and the XDP map, then a verification probe confirms L7 and kernel state; target at most 2 s. Unban of a non-banned key returns 404. Every unban records who and why. Dead-man: acceptance bans have a 60 s TTL regardless.

---

## C7. Challenge, bot and reputation doctrine

### C7.1 Principles

1. No third-party CAPTCHA, no tracking, no cognitive puzzles (WCAG 3.3.8). The challenge is an automatic proof of work plus lightweight signals.
2. Challenge is a **response option** everywhere a block would be too harsh (shared addresses, soft scores, bot suspicion, under-attack mode, signup/contact abuse).
3. Bot management is policy: the site owner picks per-class actions (allow, log, challenge, block). Verified search engines are allowed by default.

### C7.2 Proof-of-work design (`hdd-challenge`)

1. The server issues a token: `{v, site_id, ip_bucket, ua_hash, issued_at, expires_at (60 s), difficulty_bits, nonce}` signed with HMAC-SHA-256 under `HDD_CHALLENGE_KEY` (rotation with overlap).
2. The client computes the smallest counter such that `SHA-256(nonce || counter)` has at least `difficulty_bits` leading zero bits, in a Web Worker if available, with progress text and a cancel button; no data leaves the page beyond the solution.
3. The server verifies signature, expiry, one-time use (`hdd:chal:nonce:{nonce}`), difficulty, then issues a **clearance cookie** `__Host-hdd_cl` (`Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/`) containing `{v, site_id, ip_bucket, ua_hash, exp, hmac}` valid for 30 minutes (configurable 5 minutes to 24 hours).
4. `ip_bucket` is the IPv4 /24 or IPv6 /56 of the client to tolerate carrier-grade address changes; `ua_hash` binds to the user agent string.
5. Difficulty is adaptive and comes from **one table** (T-0337 calibrates it; T-0324 and E4.6 cite it): tier `baseline` 14 bits (about tens of milliseconds on a laptop), tier `appeal` 14 bits, tier `elevated` 18 bits (under elevated protection or `under_attack`), tier `automation` 20 to 22 bits (suspected automation), never above a cap that would exceed 10 s on a mid-range phone, measured by a built-in calibration. Pass-rate and solve-time histograms drive tuning (metrics).
6. **Accessibility:** automatic; screen reader announcements ("Checking your browser. This usually takes a few seconds."); reduced-motion spinner replaced by text; `noscript` explains the requirement and offers the appeal path; keyboard-complete.
7. **Abuse resistance:** replay is blocked by nonce use; clearance cookies are not transferable across IP buckets or user agents; clearance does not bypass inspection or bans, only the challenge prompt.

### C7.3 Bot scoring features

Each feature adds to a 0 to 100 score and is logged with the decision.

| Feature | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| Known scanner/tool UA | Immediate class `scanner` (policy: block and ban) |
| Missing or inconsistent headers (`Accept`, `Accept-Language`, `Accept-Encoding`, `Sec-Fetch-*` on browser UAs) | Weighted |
| Header order and casing fingerprint vs UA family | Weighted |
| HTTP/2 SETTINGS fingerprint vs UA family | Needs frame sniffer; documented limits |
| TLS fingerprint (JA3/JA4) vs UA family and against known automation families | Spike-first (T-0342); optional |
| No cookie support after challenge, missing clearance | Weighted |
| Request timing and rhythm (constant intervals) | Weighted |
| Path diversity and 404 ratio | Weighted |
| Honeypot touch | Immediate class `malicious` |
| Reputation (local score, feeds) | Weighted |
| ASN class (datacenter, hosting) | Weighted, policy-dependent |

Classes: `human_likely`, `unknown`, `automation_suspected`, `scanner`, `malicious`, `verified_bot`. Default policy per class is in S-062; defaults: verified bots allow, scanner and malicious block (and ban), automation challenge, unknown allow with log.

### C7.4 Verified bots

Forward-confirmed reverse DNS (PTR then A/AAAA matching the original IP, domain suffix match for the claimed crawler) plus optionally published IP ranges (fetched through the egress allowlist, signed or checksummed). Cache results with TTL; fail closed (treat as unverified) when DNS fails; a UA claiming Googlebot (and similar) that fails verification is class `automation_suspected` and challenged.

### C7.5 Reputation sources

1. Local reputation: score built from the installation's own events (hard hits, bans, honeypots) with exponential decay (half-life default 7 days).
2. Tor exit list, public proxy/VPN lists, datacenter ASN lists, and threat feeds (operator-enabled, signed or pinned, size-bounded, expiry per entry); policy per site: allow, challenge, block. Defaults: allow for Tor and VPN, challenge for flagged datacenter ASNs only on auth endpoints.
3. All feeds go through the egress client; entries expire; every use is explainable in the event.

### C7.6 Credential-stuffing and brute-force logic

1. Per-IP distinct-username counter on auth endpoints (HMAC'd usernames; sliding window 10 minutes): more than 5 distinct usernames with failures from one IP triggers challenge, more than 15 triggers a ban.
2. Per-username failure counter across IPs (HMAC keyed per site): more than 10 failures in 10 minutes from at least 3 IPs flags a distributed attack on that account: step-up challenge for logins to that username (the site owner is alerted; HDD cannot lock the origin's account).
3. Failure detection uses learned response patterns per auth endpoint (status codes, redirect targets, size classes) with an owner override; unknown patterns reduce confidence and are reported.
4. Responses are never altered by HDD for real users except challenge/429/403 pages.

---

## C8. Data protection and privacy

| Data | Where | Retention | Protection |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Passwords | `users.password_hash` | until change/delete | Argon2id with pepper; never logged; breached-password check at set time |
| Sessions | `user_sessions`, Redis | idle 60 min / absolute 12 h (platform staff 15 min / 8 h) | opaque IDs hashed at rest; rotated on auth change |
| TOTP secrets, recovery codes | `mfa_*` | until removed | secret encrypted (AES-256-GCM envelope), codes Argon2id-hashed |
| API keys | `api_keys` | until revoked | hash only, prefix visible |
| TLS private keys, ACME keys | `certificates`, `acme_accounts` | lifetime | envelope encryption; decrypted only in proxy memory |
| SMTP and webhook secrets, provider tokens | encrypted columns | lifetime | envelope encryption; write-only in UI |
| Request evidence | `waf_events.matched_payload` | `events_retention_days` (default 30) | at most 512 bytes, redacted (Authorization, cookies, password/token-like values), HTML-escaped on display |
| Client IPs | events, bans | with the event/ban | optional truncation (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /48) per org; full IP kept only for active bans |
| Email addresses | users, invitations, appeals | account lifetime / short | normalized; HMAC in attempt tables; encrypted in appeals and mail outbox |
| Audit log | `audit_log` | `audit_retention_days` (default 400, floor 180) | hash chain; no secrets or payloads |
| Backups | encrypted archives | per schedule | AES-256-GCM, key escrowed offline; restore drills |
| Logs | JSON on disk | 14 days default | redaction filter; no bodies; no tokens |

**Subject rights.** Users can export their data and request deletion (S-090) with a 14-day grace period; orgs can export events and audit logs; deletion removes personal data but retains hash-chained audit entries with identifiers replaced by irreversible tokens. **No tracking:** the public site and app set only essential cookies (session, CSRF, theme, locale); no third-party scripts, fonts, or analytics. **Subprocessors** (SMTP relay, CA, DNS secondary, GeoIP provider) are listed on S-013 from the live profile. **Data minimization** applies to all analytics (rollups store aggregates, not request content).

---

## C9. Hardening baseline (carried forward from v4.1 section 8 and extended; implement all of it)

### C9.1 Admin plane isolation and identity hardening

1. API and web bind to loopback or a private interface; public surfaces are reached only through the HDD proxy (dogfood) or an explicit reverse proxy; the admin surface is never public by default: SSH tunnel/WireGuard, or a routed hostname with `admin_cidrs` **and** MFA, plus step-up for mutations.
2. Session cookie `__Host-hdd_session` (no `Domain` attribute, `Path=/`, `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Lax`, Strict on admin) accepted only on the same-origin `/api/v1/*` mounts of `app` and `admin` (B2.1); the `api` host accepts bearer API keys only and never sets or reads cookies; CSRF token on every mutation; strict CSP with nonces; HSTS (`max-age` 2 years, `includeSubDomains`, preload only after operator approval; the local profile sends none or `max-age=300`, C18.6); `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`; `Permissions-Policy` denying unused features; `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin`; `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin`; frame-ancestors `none`; all output escaped; HTMX runs with `allowEval=false`, `allowScriptTags=false`, `selfRequestsOnly=true`, no inline handlers.
3. Login rate limiting with progressive backoff keyed by IP, account-HMAC, and IP-account pair; lockout messaging identical for existing and non-existing accounts; breached-password rejection; MFA mandatory for platform roles; passkeys preferred.
4. An SSH-tunnel break-glass path always exists, so a proxy outage never locks out administration. `hddctl admin mfa-reset` is the only MFA reset for platform staff and writes an audit event.

### C9.2 Anti-self-harm

Never-ban list (admin CIDRs, loopback, platform IPs, origin IPs) plus DB allowlist; the runner IP is deliberately excluded (section 2.4). Bans only on the resolved client IP. Ban-set size cap with oldest-expiry eviction. Rule dry-run against known-good probes before activation. Per-domain monitor-first rollout. Progressive ban TTL, capped.

### C9.3 Client IP and header spoofing

Client IP is the TCP peer unless the peer is in `HDD_TRUSTED_PROXIES`/`upstream_cdn.trusted_cidrs`, then `X-Forwarded-For` is parsed right to left to the first untrusted entry. Default trusts nothing. HDD **strips** inbound `X-Forwarded-*`, `Forwarded`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Original-URL`, `X-Rewrite-URL`, and `HDD-*` headers from untrusted peers before setting its own. Real client IP preservation requires proxy and DNS to bind directly on the host network; Docker NAT or the userland proxy is forbidden for 53/80/443 (AC-22).

### C9.4 IPv6 and shared addresses

IPv6 bans and rate limits key on /64 (configurable); per-domain challenge-instead-of-ban for shared addresses; collateral risk shown in the UI.

### C9.5 WAF self-DoS defenses

Global memory and CPU inspection budgets; regex size limits and linear-time engines only; decompression ratio and size caps; JSON depth 32; multipart part and size limits; per-IP connection caps; header and body limits; header-read and idle timeouts; request-smuggling rejection; bounded event queue with drop counters and per-IP aggregation. `over_limit_policy` for bodies larger than `inspect_body_max_bytes`: `inspect_prefix` (default; inspect the first N bytes, tag `truncated`), `block`, or `pass`; the choice is surfaced in metrics and in the UI with a warning for `pass`.

### C9.6 HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 attack surface

Mitigate Rapid Reset (stream-reset rate limits), CONTINUATION flood (header-block size cap), HPACK bombs (dynamic table and decoded size caps), SETTINGS/PING/empty-frame floods, h2-to-h1 downgrade smuggling (reject pseudo-header, `Transfer-Encoding` and CRLF anomalies), h2c upgrade (disabled), absolute-form and obs-fold request lines, chunk-extension abuse. Each has a raw-socket test (AC-14).

### C9.7 Internal trust

Services talk over a private network with authenticated, encrypted channels (mTLS from `hddctl pki`, or Unix sockets on one host). The proxy's dogfood path to `hdd-web` and `hdd-api` uses Unix domain sockets by default (`origin_kind=platform_internal`, section 2.9), with permissions limited to the service users. Redis and Postgres are never published. DB roles are least privilege (proxy and DNS read-only on config tables). Tenant isolation uses Postgres row-level security keyed on `org_id`.

### C9.8 Secrets at rest

TLS private keys and ACME account keys encrypted with AES-256-GCM using an envelope scheme (`HDD_MASTER_KEY` wraps per-key data keys). The master key is escrowed offline by the operator (documented in `OPERATIONS.md`; a restore drill proves a backup restores with the escrowed key); key rotation is tested; an external KMS hook is documented.

### C9.9 Privacy of stored events

`matched_payload` at most 512 bytes with redaction of `Authorization`, cookies, password-like and token-like values before storage; optional IP truncation; configurable retention with automatic partition drop; request bodies are never logged in full.

### C9.10 Supply chain

`Cargo.lock` committed; `cargo deny`/`audit`/`vet` clean or exceptions documented with expiry; digest-pinned images; SBOM; `cargo-auditable` binaries; checksums and `cosign` signatures on release artifacts; secret scanning in `xtask verify`; vendored front-end files (HTMX, axe-core, fonts) with recorded checksums and licenses.

### C9.11 Audit

Every mutation logged with actor, source IP, request ID; hash-chained `audit_log` with `hddctl audit verify`; the UI shows the verification state.

### C9.12 Origin protection

Per-domain secret origin header (`HDD-Origin-Auth`) and/or mTLS; origin firewall allowlist of HDD IPs only; strict origin certificate verification; SSRF guard on origin URLs; if the origin IP was ever exposed in DNS history, mail headers or CT-visible names, assume it is known: the firewall allowlist is then the only real protection and re-IPing the origin is recommended in `ORIGIN-HARDENING.md`.

### C9.13 Domain ownership

Before onboarding a hostname, require a DNS TXT or HTTP proof of control (waived only for domains listed in the profile in `owner_only` mode), so a tenant cannot claim someone else's domain and dangling records cannot be hijacked. Periodic re-verification; a domain failing re-verification for 7 days is moved to `pending_verification` and traffic continues for 14 more days with warnings before pause.

### C9.14 Certificate hygiene

Budget ACME issuance against the CA's current rate limits (duplicate-certificate and failed-validation limits included, verified at build time), pre-check CAA, monitor Certificate Transparency for unexpected issuance for managed names, run own expiry monitoring (do not depend on CA reminder emails). Renewal at one third of lifetime remaining or when ARI says so; alert at one quarter remaining.

| Subsystem | S (spoofing) | T (tampering) | R (repudiation) | I (information disclosure) | D (denial of service) | E (elevation) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Public site | Look-alike phishing of the brand: publish security.txt, HSTS preload plan | Content tampering: signed releases, read-only FS | n/a | No tracking; no secrets in pages | Rate limits, caching headers | n/a |
| Signup and login | Credential stuffing, fake accounts: rate limits, PoW, breached passwords | Token tampering: HMAC and hashed tokens | Audit of auth events | Enumeration: uniform responses, timing equalization | Email bombing: per-recipient limits | Role escalation: server-side RBAC |
| Sessions and API keys | Session theft: cookie flags, rotation, binding | CSRF: tokens, SameSite, origin checks | Session audit | Key leakage: hashed, shown once | Key flood: per-key limits | Scope abuse: intersection rule |
| Tenant isolation | Forged org IDs: membership check | Cross-tenant write: RLS + checks | Audit | BOLA: 404 on foreign IDs, RLS tests | Noisy neighbor: quotas, per-tenant budgets | Platform bypass: `SECURITY DEFINER` + reason + audit |
| Domain onboarding | Claim someone else's domain: ownership proof, periodic re-verification | Zone import tampering: parity and acknowledgment | Audit | Origin IP exposure analysis | Onboarding spam: quotas | n/a |
| DNS server | Spoofed source queries: RRL, cookies | Zone content tampering: API-only writes, versions | Zone version history | AXFR refusal, no origin data in answers | Floods: RRL, caps, secondary | n/a |
| Proxy and TLS | Fake SNI: refuse unknown | Smuggling: strict framing | Ray ID and events | Header stripping, error masking | Slowloris, h2 floods, budgets | Header spoofing: untrusted-peer stripping |
| WAF engine | Header spoofing for allowlist bypass: IP resolution rules | Rule tampering: signed packs, revisions | Event and audit trail | Evidence redaction, escaping | ReDoS: linear engines, budgets | Exception abuse: expiry and audit |
| Ban system | Ban poisoning: cross-site rule | Ban list tampering: authz, audit | Ban evidence | Appeal oracle prevention | Mass-ban attack: alerts, caps | Unban abuse: permissions, audit |
| Challenge | Replay: nonce, binding | Token forgery: HMAC | Stats | Timing | Solve farms: adaptive difficulty | n/a |
| Admin panel | Phishing staff: passkeys, step-up | CSRF: tokens | Platform audit | Impersonation read-only | Admin brute force: CIDR, lockout | Role escalation: platform matrix tests |
| Workers and mail | Mail spoofing of platform: SPF, DKIM, DMARC | Template injection: safe templating | Mail outbox log | PII minimization | Queue flooding: bounds | n/a |
| Webhooks and integrations | Forged callbacks: HMAC signatures | Replay: timestamp and nonce | Delivery log | SSRF: guard | Slow endpoints: timeouts | n/a |
| Host agent and XDP | Unauthorized commands: Unix socket permissions, signed messages | Rule tampering: capability drop | Audit | n/a | Detach timer protects against lockout | Capability minimization |
| Updates and supply chain | Rogue mirror: signature checks | Dependency compromise: deny/audit/vet | Release provenance | SBOM | Bad release: staged swap + rollback | Build isolation |
| Backups | n/a | Backup tampering: authenticated encryption | Backup log | Encrypted, key escrow | Restore drills | n/a |
