## C20. Machine-learning-assisted detection: Sentinel (new in v5.2)

### C20.1 Premise and honest limits

Signatures and tokenizers catch what is known. **Sentinel** adds learned components that look for what is *unusual*, to shrink the window in which a new technique works. It is not a replacement for the deterministic engine, it is not a guarantee, it can be evaded, and it produces false positives. The deterministic engine stays authoritative (rule R-33). Product text says "machine-learning-assisted" and "advisory" and cites held-out measurements; it never says "AI-powered protection" (section 4.2).

### C20.2 Layers

| Layer | Runs | Latency | May it block alone? | Learns from | If it fails |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Deterministic engine (C4, C5) | in-process | p50 under 1 ms | yes (hard signatures) | rules and fixtures | blocks per R-26 |
| B. Per-site baseline (benign profile per path template and parameter) | in-process | within the Sentinel budget | no | this site's accepted traffic | skipped, counter |
| C. Global attack-shape classifier | in-process | within the Sentinel budget | only in `block` mode and only under the corroboration rules of C20.5 | offline corpora, fixtures, synthetic mutations | skipped, counter |
| D. Session-sequence model (bounded) | in-process | within the Sentinel budget | no | this site's sessions | skipped, counter |
| E. Analyst (optional language model) | asynchronous, **never on the request path** | seconds | never | none (no training on tenant data) | disabled, nothing changes |

The Sentinel budget is 200 µs p99 per request in total. A cheap prefilter (shape novelty, entropy, view mismatch, token-class anomalies) decides whether the models run at all, so most requests pay a few microseconds.

### C20.3 Features and privacy

Features come from the three normalized views and the SQL, HTML and shell tokenizers: hashed token n-grams (2^18 buckets, used only inside the in-memory scoring and never stored), token-class sequences, character-class ratios, entropy, nesting depth, encoding-layer count, disagreement between the raw, decoded and canonical views, length z-scores per (template, parameter), keyword density, header order and set, and content-type versus body-shape agreement. Features are computed in memory and discarded; only the top contributing features, expressed as feature **classes** (never hashed content buckets), and the redacted evidence snippet (at most 512 bytes, passed through the redaction library of T-0253 with a pattern set for credentials, tokens and personal data) are stored for flagged events; sequence-model state is kept in memory and in a per-site snapshot for at most 24 hours. Opt-in sharing sends aggregate class counts only, with a minimum population of 50 distinct clients per cell and added noise, so rare values of small tenants cannot be recovered. No raw request bodies are kept for training, and no tenant data leaves the platform for model improvement unless the tenant opts in (aggregate features only, T-0598 notes).

### C20.4 Models

- **Per-site baseline.** Bounded memory per (path template, parameter): length distribution (t-digest), character-class histogram, token-class bigram counts (count-min sketch), plus a site-wide isolation forest over aggregated features. Cold start: no influence before 10,000 requests and 7 days.
- **Global attack-shape classifier.** Gradient-boosted trees or a small character-level convolutional network exported to an inference-only runtime (T-0581). Trained offline (`cargo xtask ml train`) on public corpora with licenses recorded, HDD fixtures and a synthetic mutation generator; calibrated at an operating point with a benign false-positive rate of at most 0.01% of requests. Evaluation includes **leave-one-family-out** runs (train without a whole attack family, test on it) so claims about *unseen* techniques are measured, not assumed.
- **Session-sequence model.** A bounded first-order model of path-template transitions that scores implausible sequences (for example a login page followed directly by a data-export endpoint at machine speed); advisory only.

### C20.5 Influence policy (the bounds)

| Mode | Effect | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `off` | nothing runs | |
| `shadow` | scores and findings are recorded, **no effect on any response** | yes, for every new site and every new model |
| `assist` | adds a **soft score** capped at 3 points and **never enough to cross the block threshold**: the total with the deterministic score is clamped to threshold minus 1, and the request is escalated to a proof-of-work challenge on non-authentication GET requests instead; Sentinel alone can therefore never turn a deterministic `pass` into a `block` | owner opt-in |
| `block` | may block alone only when classifier probability is at least 0.99, the vector lies in a field kind where the baseline is mature, and the model's measured false-positive budget is met | owner opt-in, per site, step-up |

Rules that apply in every mode: (1) a learned component **never bans alone**: a ban always requires a deterministic signal in the same request; repeated high-confidence Sentinel findings from one identity may only raise that identity's challenge level and priority for human review, never create a ban; (2) no ban in cross-site subresource context (C6.5) and none for password fields; (3) hard-signature doctrine is unchanged; (4) a Sentinel failure, timeout or oversized input is skipped with `MET-hdd_sentinel_fallback_total` and the deterministic verdict stands; (5) every finding stores the top five features in plain language ("parameter far longer than usual for this endpoint; rare character mix") and is labeled advisory; (6) promotion from `shadow` needs at least 14 days, an owner review of the 100 highest-scoring findings, a baseline-replay false-positive rate within budget, and a measured detection uplift on the held-out novel set; (7) a spike in appeals or owner "mark as normal" labels, counted only from distinct cleared or verified clients with a capped weight per client, or drift beyond a threshold, auto-demotes the site to `shadow`, raises an alert that says the spike may itself be an attack, and requires owner confirmation to re-promote; (8) `hddctl sentinel off` is the break-glass.

### C20.6 Training and lifecycle

Reproducible pipeline with pinned data hashes, a fixed split protocol, calibration, model cards (`docs/ml/`), signed artifacts and staged rollout (shadow canary, then stable) exactly like rule packs, with rollback. Baselines are per site and never leave it. Global models update through signed packs.

### C20.7 Threat model of the learned components

| Threat | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Evasion by mimicry, padding, homoglyphs, token insertion | Deterministic layer first; adversarial augmentation in training; robustness suite with a measured evasion rate (T-0585); Sentinel is never the only control |
| Poisoning of the baseline by an attacker | Baselines learn only from requests that passed the deterministic engine and came from cleared clients or established sessions; trimmed, rate-limited, per-identity-capped updates; flagged requests are quarantined from learning |
| Model extraction by probing | Scores are never returned to clients; per-identity probing is rate limited |
| Prompt injection into the analyst | Analyst input is structured data marked untrusted; no tools, no write access, schema-validated output, human approval, dry-run before any rule exists |
| Drift and stale models | Age and drift metrics; auto-demotion; scheduled retraining |
| Resource exhaustion | Prefilter, hard CPU budget, bounded memory per template, global cap |

### C20.8 The analyst (optional language model)

Off by default (`HDD_ANALYST_MODE=off`). When enabled it summarizes campaigns, explains a blocked event in plain language, ranks the triage queue and drafts a candidate rule or exception **as a diff for a human**. It receives only redacted evidence (at most 512 bytes) and features inside a structured, labeled-untrusted field, never secrets, cookies or other tenants' data. It runs through the egress client to an allowlisted endpoint or a local model on loopback, with cost caps. Its output is validated against a schema, never applied automatically, and any proposed rule is replayed through the dry-run harness (T-0229) before an owner can approve it.

## C21. Bypass Guard: closing and verifying the direct path to the origin (new in v5.2)

### C21.1 Premise and honest limits

HDD cannot configure the origin host. What it can do is (a) remove the direct path in tunnel mode when the origin's inbound ports are closed and that closure has been verified from outside, (b) make direct requests rejected by every deployed verifier by requiring a signed per-request authentication (the signing key is shared with the verifier, so a compromised verifier host can forge), (c) **verify continuously** from outside and from inside, and (d) **refuse to call a site protected** until verification passes (rule R-34). It cannot protect an origin whose host is compromised, whose signing key is stolen, or whose neighbors share its network.

### C21.2 Ways around HDD, and the control for each

| Bypass path | Control |
| --- | --- |
| Direct connection to the origin IP | Signed origin authentication, firewall allowlist, or tunnel (C21.3); active probes from outside |
| Origin IP leaked by history (old DNS, certificate transparency, mail headers, other subdomains) | Exposure scan (T-0165, T-0407), re-IP assistant, signed authentication makes a known IP useless |
| Another hostname or virtual host on the same origin | Verifier rejects unsigned requests for every host; probe tries every name found |
| Other ports and services (alternate web ports, admin consoles, databases, SSH, FTP) | Port probe of the origin's own address from outside; firewall generator closes everything but HDD's egress set |
| IPv6 or HTTP/3 side doors | Probe covers IPv6 and UDP 443; generator covers both families |
| Grey-cloud (unproxied) DNS records that expose the origin | Hard blocker in the go-live gate and a continuous check |
| Wildcard or forgotten subdomains, staging and dev names | Dangling and unproxied-name scan; wildcard policy |
| Another proxy or CDN in front of the origin | Detected by the echo canary; warns |
| SSRF from a neighboring service to the origin's private address | Signed authentication still required; network segmentation guidance |
| Host or SNI confusion at HDD to reach another tenant or an internal route | Host and SNI consistency (T-0355), neutral 404, no default tenant |
| Spoofed forwarding headers | Stripped inbound; signature covers method, host, path and query |
| Replay of a captured signed request | Timestamp window (30 s) and nonce cache at the verifier |

### C21.3 Controls

1. **Signed origin authentication (default).** HDD adds `HDD-Origin-Auth: v1;<kid>;<unix-ts>;<nonce>;<sig>` with `sig = HMAC-SHA-256(key, canonical)` where `canonical` is newline-terminated, length-prefixed fields: version, `kid`, uppercase method, lowercase host without port, port, the raw request-target bytes as forwarded, SHA-256 of the body (or the literal `nobody`; for streamed bodies the signature covers `Content-Length` or `chunked` and states that the body is not covered), `ts`, `nonce`, `ray_id`, and the marker `via=tunnel|direct`; test vectors fix every byte. The origin must be reached over TLS or the tunnel so a signed request cannot be altered in transit. The verifier rejects unknown `kid`, timestamp skew over 30 s, replayed nonces and bad signatures, with a generic 403 that reveals nothing. Nonces are retained for at least twice the skew window; a full cache fails closed; multi-instance origins use a shared nonce store or sticky routing, and the wizard says so. Origins need a clock within 5 s (NTP); a skewed clock returns the same generic 403 and a heartbeat reason code. The verifier in signed mode **rejects the static header of T-0361**. Keys rotate with overlap. Key handling: one key per site, scoped per `kid`, shown once to a user holding `PERM-bypass.key_view`, held in HDD envelope-encrypted and in the proxy's memory only (zeroized on rotation); rotation retires the old key only after every verifier instance has acknowledged the new one, or after a rolling probe confirms every origin target accepts it. The wizard generates verifier modules or snippets for nginx, Apache, Caddy, HAProxy, Node (Express, Fastify), Python (WSGI/ASGI), PHP (`auto_prepend_file`), Java (servlet filter) and .NET middleware, each a short, reviewed, tested file. The static secret header of T-0361 remains available for simple setups, is marked weaker, and caps the lockdown state at `applied_unverified`.
2. **Mutual TLS** (T-0383) as an alternative or in addition.
3. **Tunnel mode (`hdd-tunnel`).** A small connector on the origin dials out to HDD over mutually authenticated TLS and carries the requests; the origin host closes all inbound web ports. With inbound ports closed there is no listener to connect to directly. The connector dials one configured `host:port` only (not a range), enrollment tokens are single-use, bound to the site, valid for 15 minutes and confirmed by a fingerprint shown on both sides, and origins that trust loopback peers (admin paths, `/server-status`, metrics) are flagged by the wizard because tunnel traffic arrives from the connector; verifiers use the `via=tunnel` marker rather than the peer address.
4. **Network allowlist.** Generators for nftables, iptables, ufw, and the main cloud firewalls that allow only HDD's published egress addresses (T-0405) and deny the rest. Removed addresses expire automatically after the overlap and the probe verifies the old set is closed. If HDD's egress range is shared infrastructure, co-tenants of that range can reach the origin; a firewall-only setup is therefore never eligible for `verified` without signed authentication or the tunnel.
5. **Origin-side tripwire.** The verifier counts unsigned or invalid requests and reports them to HDD in a signed heartbeat (through the tunnel or an HTTPS callback). The verifier distinguishes a **bypass attempt** (an unsigned or invalid request that was rejected: informational, aggregated by rate, never changes the state) from a **confirmed bypass** (site content served without a valid signature, or a successful direct probe: a `bypass_events` row, a critical alert and `bypass_detected`). The heartbeat is signed with its own key, separate from the origin-authentication key.
6. **Active verification** every hour (configurable) from at least two vantage points outside HDD's network (the operator's runner, an operator-configured probe, or a bring-your-own-probe token page): direct connections to the origin address on the common web ports, the configured ports and the top-100 web ports (rate-limited, each probed address and name first proven to belong to the site's owner by a DNS or HTTP challenge, resolved once and pinned, never a private, loopback, link-local or cloud-metadata range, with a per-target cost cap and every probe target written to the audit log), with and without SNI and with different `Host` values, over IPv4, IPv6 and UDP 443, plus every historic and certificate-transparency name found. Results are classified `blocked`, `site_content` (matched by the echo canary token or a content hash), `exposed_service` (any non-HDD service that answers, such as an admin console, database or default virtual host) and `inconclusive`; `site_content` and `exposed_service` both fail verification. At least one vantage is HDD-operated with rotating, unpublished addresses, owner-run probes sign their results with a per-probe key and nonce, and a probe whose results never vary is treated as suspect. Before any result counts, an **origin-address check** shows that a request to the probed address reaches the same origin as the proxied path (a unique token seen on both); otherwise the state stays `applied_unverified`.
7. **DNS hygiene.** Every hostname of a protected site is proxied, no unproxied record shares the origin address, wildcards are explicit.
8. **The gate (R-34).** See C21.4.

### C21.4 States and the go-live gate

States: `unprotected`, `lockdown_instructed`, `applied_unverified`, `verified`, `degraded`, `bypass_detected`. `protection_state()` maps the six states to the surface labels: `verified` → `protected` (shown with date and vantage count); `applied_unverified` and `lockdown_instructed` → `unverified`; `degraded` → `monitoring` (verification overdue or a vantage outage); `bypass_detected` and `unprotected` → `bypassable`. A site already in `block` mode that becomes `degraded` keeps blocking (never weaker than before) but shows `monitoring`; at `bypass_detected` it keeps blocking, raises the incident and cannot be promoted or have its protections relaxed. A risk acceptance shows `bypassable` until the state is `verified`, at which point the acceptance is cleared and the label follows the state. `degraded` begins only after 24 hours without a valid verification and never from a single outage. In the local profile `verified` means tunnel mode with a verified closed inbound plus at least one owner-attested vantage; without any vantage, `block` mode needs the typed risk acceptance. A site cannot enter `block` mode or show "protected" in any surface unless it is `verified`; the owner may override only with a typed risk acceptance, which shows "bypassable" in readiness, the dashboard and reports. In tunnel mode with a verified closed inbound (and, outside the local profile, at least two independent vantages including one HDD-operated), the state is `verified` and the surfaces say "no direct path found from N vantage points on <date>", never "cannot be bypassed". `bypass_detected` raises a critical alert, offers one-click key rotation and a tightening wizard, blocks promotion to `block` mode, and is shown on S-138 until two consecutive clean verifications; attempts alone never keep the state pinned.

### C21.5 What the guard cannot do

A stolen signing key lets an attacker forge requests until rotation; keys are stored with web-server-only permissions and rotated on suspicion. A compromised origin host is outside HDD. Services on the same host that are not HTTP are covered only by the port probe and firewall advice. Shared hosting cannot close ports and is flagged as `weak` in the wizard.

## C22. Known-vulnerability coverage and additional hardening (new in v5.2)

### C22.1 What "all well-known vulnerabilities" can honestly mean

No product can contain every vulnerability ever found. HDD instead provides (a) a **Known-Vulnerability Knowledge Base (VKB)** that tracks named CVEs (CISA KEV first, then high-EPSS and high-severity items), vulnerability classes (OWASP, CWE, CAPEC) and misconfiguration classes; (b) a **pipeline** that turns request-visible exploit shapes into tested, signed, staged rules within a stated time; (c) the **attack matrix** (C5, now ATK-001 to ATK-390) and the coverage map (E15) that show what exists, what is tested and what is not covered; and (d) **per-site relevance**, so a site running a product gets that product's rules prioritized and enabled.

### C22.2 The VKB

Entry fields: key (CVE, GHSA, OSV or class id), kind, product and version range (purl/CPE), CWE and CAPEC, severity, KEV flag, EPSS, **request-visible** (does an exploit leave a pattern in the request or response HDD can see), rule reference, status (`candidate`, `monitor`, `block`, `retired`, `not_applicable`), source and license, lab-tested date. Sources: CISA KEV, NVD, OSV, GitHub advisories, vendor advisories, Exploit-DB metadata, CWE and CAPEC, and community detection templates (for example the Nuclei templates, MIT-licensed) with each license recorded and reviewed before use. Feeds are fetched only by the worker through the egress client and verified (T-0481); unsigned community templates are pinned by commit, diff-reviewed and converted only with a human approval, because a hostile upstream change is a supply-chain risk.

### C22.3 Pipeline and service levels

Ingest, classify request-visibility, find or derive the pattern (own research, community template, rule-set patterns), convert to HDD rule format, lint (ReDoS, budget), measure false positives against the benign corpora, prove against a vulnerable container in the lab where one exists, sign, roll out in stages (1%, 10%, 100% of opted-in sites) with auto-rollback, and retire when the component is patched across the fleet and aged. **Targets (measured, not promised):** a request-visible KEV entry becomes a `candidate` within 24 hours and, where a pattern can be derived, a `monitor` rule within 72 hours. An emergency channel (two-person approval, offline signing key, `monitor` start, 24-hour expiry) pushes a signed rule to 95% of a test fleet within 10 minutes and, in production, within a measured time that is reported; `hddctl vkb apply` works offline with serial numbers and expiry. A virtual patch never marks the vulnerability resolved (R-11).

### C22.4 Matrix expansion

Four new attack groups: **AG-18** named vulnerabilities (ATK-301 to ATK-340), **AG-19** modern techniques and evasion (ATK-341 to ATK-360), **AG-20** AI-system and modern-stack exposure (ATK-361 to ATK-370), **AG-21** additional techniques from the independent review (ATK-371 to ATK-390). Rows whose action is `P`, `L` or `Q` are mitigations or posture items, not detections, and are labeled so in the coverage map. CVE-specific rows use pattern *shapes*; the exact CVE list is refreshed from the KEV catalog at build time and monthly thereafter.

### C22.5 Additional hardening added in v5.2

| Measure | What it closes | Task |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Stack-aware normalization profiles (PHP, Java, .NET, Node, Python, Ruby, nginx, Apache, IIS) | Parser differentials: HDD and the origin disagree on what a request means | T-0593 |
| Parser-differential rejection (duplicate JSON keys, comments and big numbers, multipart edge cases, charset confusion such as `ibm037` or UTF-7, content-type switching) | WAF bypass by representation | T-0597 |
| Bounded rolling-window inspection of padded requests (scanning beyond the prefix within a budget, chunk-split and multipart-split payload reassembly) | Narrows padding past the inspect limit and payload splitting | T-0597 |
| Cache poisoning and deception guard (unkeyed header stripping, path-delimiter normalization, `Vary` enforcement, cache-poisoned DoS shapes) | ATK-155, ATK-156 and variants | T-0598 |
| Honeytokens (decoy credentials, API keys and records placed in responses and files; per-session issuance; use in a first-party context from another client bans, other contexts raise a critical event) | Attackers using stolen data | T-0598 |
| Webshell interaction detection and origin integrity watch | Post-exploitation on the origin | T-0598 |
| AI-endpoint protections (prompt-injection signals, token-cost quotas, exposed model and MCP endpoints) | LLM-backed apps | T-0598 |
| Script-integrity monitor and generated CSP / Trusted Types | Skimmers, third-party script tampering | T-0412, T-0598 |
| Signed origin authentication and tunnel | Bypass | T-0588, T-0589 |

<!-- PART:D -->
# PART D: THE 599 TASKS

How to use this part: execute phases in order; inside a phase follow the task order unless the `deps` allow earlier work (section 0.8). Each task block states its objective, concrete steps, deliverables, acceptance criteria, tests and notes. Sizes: S, M, L, XL. Owners: `ux`, `ui`, `api`, `waf`, `dp` (data plane), `dns`, `infra`, `qa`, `sec`, `docs`, `ops`. Phase gates require a gate report in the Appendix E5 format with pasted real output.

<!-- PHASE:P00 -->
## PHASE P00: Bootstrap and governance (T-0001 to T-0010) · milestone M0 · gate G00

Requirement prefix `GOV`. Goal: the agent can be resumed from files alone, the workspace builds and verifies itself, the live profile is validated, and safety libraries exist before any feature work. This is the only phase that precedes UX work, because the persistent state files and the egress guard are preconditions for everything else.

Gate G00 passes when: `docs/SPEC.md` and its split exist with a matching checksum; `AGENTS.md` is at most 150 lines; `cargo check --workspace` and `cargo xtask verify` are green; `hddctl preflight --profile-only` reports honestly (including real failures); the egress guard tests pass; the capability matrix is generated; the first response of section 9 has been delivered and the operator's answers are recorded or marked open.

### T-0001 · Save the specification verbatim, split it, and index every task
`P00` `[DOC][OPS]` · deps: none · size: S · owner: docs
**Objective.** Make the specification durable and cheaply loadable: one verbatim copy, one split copy, one index from task ID to file and line.
**Steps.**
1. Create the repository skeleton directories from section 7 (empty directories get a `.gitkeep`); do not create code yet. The skeleton is `.gitkeep` files only; the first real code arrives with T-0004.
2. Copy this entire document byte-for-byte to `docs/SPEC.md`; compute SHA-256 and write it to `docs/SPEC.sha256` with the date.
3. Write the one-off bootstrap splitter as a short POSIX `awk` command recorded in `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` as `DEV-V5-000` (the sole permitted non-Rust script; it is deleted by T-0005).
4. Split at every `<!-- PART:<id> -->` and `<!-- PHASE:<id> -->` marker into `docs/spec/<id>.md`, keeping the marker as the first line of each file; the preamble before the first marker goes to `docs/spec/00-preamble.md`.
5. Generate `docs/spec/INDEX.md`: a table of every `### T-nnnn` heading with columns task ID, title, phase, file, start line, tags, size, deps.
6. Verify losslessness: concatenating `docs/spec/*.md` in order must reproduce `docs/SPEC.md` exactly (compare SHA-256).
7. Add a README section "Reading the spec" explaining the loading strategy of section 0.1.
8. Commit with message `docs: add verbatim spec v5 and split index` and trailer `Task: T-0001`.
**Deliverables.**
- `docs/SPEC.md`, `docs/SPEC.sha256`
- `docs/spec/*.md` (about 50 files) and `docs/spec/INDEX.md`
- `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` containing `DEV-V5-000`
- `README.md` stub with the reading instructions
**Acceptance.**
- A1: SHA-256 of concatenated split files equals the SHA-256 of `docs/SPEC.md`.
- A2: `INDEX.md` lists exactly 599 task rows with no duplicates and no gaps from T-0001 to T-0599.
- A3: every phase P00 to P34 has a split file whose first line is its marker.
- A4: no file in `docs/spec/` exceeds 3,000 lines (splitting at phase markers keeps phases manageable; if a phase exceeds it, the splitter adds sub-splits at task boundaries and the index records them).
- A5: the commit contains only files under `docs/`, `README.md` and the `.gitkeep` files of the skeleton; no source code and no build files.
**Tests.**
- Shell-free check run once by hand and later replaced by `cargo xtask spec check` (T-0005).
- The index row count is compared with `grep -c '^### T-' docs/SPEC.md`.
**Notes.** From T-0005 on, `cargo xtask spec split` regenerates the same files deterministically; CI compares them with the committed copy.

### T-0002 · Create the state files and the deviation log
`P00` `[DOC]` · deps: T-0001 · size: S · owner: docs
**Objective.** Give every future session the same three entry points and a place to record deviations, so no knowledge lives in chat.
**Steps.**
1. Write `AGENTS.md` (at most 150 lines): non-negotiable rules digest (R-01 to R-30 one line each), the commands (`cargo xtask verify`, `ui verify`, `acceptance`), current phase and task pointer, where things live, the session start ritual of section 0.1, and the stop conditions (STOP #1, STOP #2, approvals).
2. Write `STATUS.md` with sections: Current phase and milestone; Task table (ID, title, state, evidence link, commit); Open risks; Open questions (seeded from Appendix E8); UNVERIFIED list (ID, reason code, what the operator must supply); Last gate report summary.

4. Create `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` with the table header (ID, deviation, reason, date, approver) and pre-seed `DEV-V5-000` to `DEV-V5-003` (`DEV-V5-000` splitter script; `DEV-V5-001` Vuln-Lab exception to "no dummy origin"; `DEV-V5-002` rust-share definition; `DEV-V5-003` mandated SQLi set discrepancy) with the reasons from sections 0.1, 2.8, 5 and C4.1; `DEV-V5-004` (YAML to TOML fallback) and `DEV-V5-005` (UI stack choice) are added only if T-0006 or T-0071 trigger them.

7. Link all state files from `README.md`.
8. Run a manual review: simulate a new session and confirm the files alone answer "what is next".
**Deliverables.**

**Tests.**

### T-0003 · Environment discovery with read-only commands
`P00` `[OPS]` · deps: T-0002 · size: S · owner: infra
**Objective.** Record what the builder, VPS (when reachable) and runner can and cannot do, and state what degrades.
**Steps.**
1. On the builder, record the operating system and architecture (Windows, macOS or Linux; PowerShell equivalents of the commands below on Windows) and run read-only commands: `rustc -V`, `cargo -V`, nightly and `bpf-linker` presence, `docker -v` and compose, `dig -v`, `delv -v`, `openssl version`, `ssh -V`, `nft --version`, `iptables -V`, kernel version, `/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux` presence, virtualization (`systemd-detect-virt`), CPU, RAM, disk.
2. Record browser readiness: Chromium path (`/opt/pw-browsers/chromium` in cloud sessions), headless launch test, fonts installed; confirm Node is **not** required.
3. If `deploy_mode: ssh`, run the same read-only commands on the VPS through the configured SSH account and add NIC driver, link speed (`ethtool`), XDP native/generic support (read-only probe), ability to bind 53/80/443 (checked with `ss -ltn` and capability inspection, not by binding), NTP sync (`timedatectl`).
4. Test outbound connectivity **only** to hosts on the egress allowlist; record failures as `environment_unsupported` rather than trying other hosts.
5. For each missing tool, write what degrades (for example "no nightly toolchain: XDP crate cannot build, AC-26 becomes UNVERIFIED(environment_unsupported)"). Status words: a missing optional tool (`dig`, `delv`, `openssl`, a nightly toolchain) is `UNVERIFIED(tool_unavailable)`, a capability the platform cannot offer (Docker on this builder, `nft`, binding port 53) is `UNVERIFIED(environment_unsupported)`, and FAIL is reserved for a check that ran and failed; reason codes belong to UNVERIFIED, so `FAIL(environment_unsupported)` is never written.
6. Save full logs under git-ignored `acceptance-env/` with SHA-256 and write the summary to `docs/ENV.md` with command, output tail (last 5 lines), and status per item.
7. Add the degradation list to `STATUS.md` UNVERIFIED section.
8. Decide and record the **build track**: *Track H* (Linux builder with Docker: testcontainers) or *Track L* (no Docker: the embedded PostgreSQL and in-process stores of `hdd-local`, started by `cargo xtask db up` once T-0563 lands). Until T-0563, a Track L builder uses a locally installed PostgreSQL if present, otherwise marks the database-dependent checks UNVERIFIED(`environment_unsupported`) and continues with the tasks that do not need it.
9. Commit `docs/ENV.md`.
**Deliverables.**
- `docs/ENV.md` (table of items, commands, tails, status)
- `acceptance-env/*.log` (ignored) with `SHA256SUMS`
- STATUS.md update
**Acceptance.**
- A1: every item listed in R-05 has a row with a status of PASS, FAIL or UNVERIFIED(reason).
- A2: no command in the discovery set writes outside the scratch directories or changes system state.
- A3: degradation statements exist for every non-PASS row.
- A4: outbound checks touched only allowlisted hosts (verified from the egress client log once T-0009 exists; before that, a manual list is included).
- A5: secrets and key paths are not printed in any output.
**Tests.**
- Re-run the discovery script twice; outputs must be identical except timestamps.
- A review confirms that no command used `sudo` or modified configuration.
**Notes.** Discovery is repeated at the start of P11 (VPS) and P28 (lab) with the same checklist.

### T-0004 · Cargo workspace, lints, toolchain and dependency policy
`P00` `[OPS][SEC]` · deps: T-0002 · size: M · owner: infra
**Objective.** Create the workspace so that unsafe code, unwraps and panics are build failures from the first commit.
**Steps.**
1. Create `Cargo.toml` with `[workspace]` listing every crate from section 7 (each with a minimal `lib.rs` or `main.rs` that compiles), `resolver = "2"`, shared `[workspace.package]` and `[workspace.dependencies]` (no versions asserted from memory; read them from the registry at the time).
2. Add `[workspace.lints]`: deny `unsafe_code`, `clippy::unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `indexing_slicing`, `todo`, `unimplemented`, `dbg_macro`, `print_stdout` (allowed in CLI crates via crate-level override), `missing_docs` for public items; `warnings` denied in CI.
3. Add `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` to every crate except `hdd-xdp-ebpf`, which is excluded from the default workspace build (separate target and toolchain) and documented in an ADR stub.
4. Pin the toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml` (stable) with `rustfmt` and `clippy` components; record MSRV.
5. Write `deny.toml`: licenses allowlist (permissive plus MPL-2.0/OpenSSL-style exceptions decided in the ADR), bans for yanked crates, advisories from RustSec, duplicate-version warnings, sources restricted to crates.io.
6. Add `rustfmt.toml`, `clippy.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml` (no network flags that weaken TLS), and a `lab/vulnlab` workspace member that is excluded from `default-members` and has its own lint override only for the intentional-vulnerability modules, still with `forbid(unsafe_code)`.
7. Run `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.
8. Commit the lockfile (`Cargo.lock`).
**Deliverables.**
- `Cargo.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `deny.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `clippy.toml`, `.cargo/config.toml`
- one `Cargo.toml` and one source file per crate listed in section 7
- `Cargo.lock`
**Acceptance.**
- A1: `cargo check --workspace` succeeds on the builder.
- A2: adding a `.unwrap()` in a non-test file makes `cargo clippy` fail (demonstrated in a test commit then reverted).
- A3: `cargo deny check` runs (exceptions documented with expiry).
- A4: `hdd-vulnlab` does not appear in `cargo tree -p hdd-proxy -e normal` or any shipped binary's graph.
- A5: all crates carry `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` except `hdd-xdp-ebpf` (checked by a grep rule in `xtask`).
**Tests.**
- A CI script (later `xtask verify`) asserts the lint table is present and unchanged.
- A compile-fail test under `crates/hdd-common/tests/` (using `trybuild` if vetted) confirms `unsafe` is rejected.
**Notes.** Do not add crates "for later". Each dependency is added by the task that uses it, with the vetting evidence in the ADR or the commit body (R-08).

`P00` `[OPS][QA][DOC]` · deps: T-0004 · size: L · owner: infra
**Objective.** One command (`cargo xtask verify`) that enforces the rules mechanically, plus the spec and task tools that replace the bootstrap script.

Implement the xtask binary with `clap` subcommands: `verify`, `spec split|check|show <T-id>`, `tasks index|order`, `gen-secrets`, `claims-lint`, `rust-share`, `matrix check`, `attack-matrix check`, `contrast-check`, `i18n check`, `routes check` (stubs return success with a note until their tasks land, each tracked in STATUS as `stub`).

### T-0009 · Egress client, SSRF guard, target allowlist and kill switch
`P00` `[SEC][DP]` · deps: T-0004, T-0006 · size: L · owner: sec
**Objective.** Build the single outbound path that makes the safety envelope enforceable in code.
**Steps.**
1. Implement `hdd-common::egress::Client` over `hyper` + `rustls`: allowlist matching by scheme, host (exact or suffix), port and optional path prefix; connect/total timeouts; maximum response size; redirects disabled by default (opt-in per call with re-validation of each hop); TLS verification always on.
2. Implement DNS pinning: resolve, validate, connect to the validated address, never re-resolve silently; the resolver is a trait so unit tests can drive rebinding sequences.
3. Implement the **SSRF-guarded variant** `UserUrlClient` enforcing section 2.9: public unicast only, rejected ranges (loopback, RFC 1918, CGNAT, link-local incl. metadata, multicast, unspecified, documentation, IPv6 ULA, IPv4-mapped forms, platform addresses), port allowlist, no redirects, re-validation on every connect.
4. Implement `TargetGuard` for acceptance and scanning tools: derives the allowed target set from the profile (`test_hostname`, `sandbox_hostname`, and lab addresses in lab mode) and aborts on any other target.
5. Implement the kill switch: a file path watched by a cheap poller; all long-running tools check it and abort within one second.
6. Log every denied egress attempt as a structured event (destination, reason, caller) with rate limiting of the logs themselves.
7. Add an xtask grep rule that fails if `reqwest::Client::new`, `hyper::Client` construction, or `std::net::TcpStream::connect` appears outside `egress`, tests, and listed exceptions (R-22).
8. Write the module documentation and an `OPERATIONS.md` section describing allowlist entries and how to request additions.
**Deliverables.**
- `crates/hdd-common/src/egress/{client,ssrf,target,killswitch}.rs`
- xtask grep rule; docs
- test suite with real local HTTP/TLS servers and a real local DNS responder
**Acceptance.**
- A1: a request to a host not on the allowlist is denied before any socket is opened (proved by an unused-listener test).
- A2: a hostname that first resolves to a public address and then to `127.0.0.1` is rejected at connect time.
- A3: a redirect from an allowed host to `http://169.254.169.254/` is not followed.
- A4: `TargetGuard` rejects any target outside the derived set, including via CNAME to another host.
- A5: touching the kill-switch file aborts a running sample tool within 1 s.
**Tests.**
- Unit: range classification table for IPv4/IPv6 including mapped and compressed forms (property test: classification invariant under textual representation).

### T-0010 · Capability matrix, requirement tooling and gate G00
`P00` `[DOC][QA]` · deps: T-0005, T-0008, T-0009 · size: M · owner: docs

<!-- PHASE:P01 -->
## PHASE P01: UX research, personas, information architecture, journeys (T-0011 to T-0028) · milestone M1 · gate G01

Requirement prefix `UXR`. Goal: turn the product definition of Part B into reviewed repository documents and decisions before any pixel is designed, so that design and build start from agreed principles, flows and constraints. Deliverables live in `docs/UX/` and are written for the operator to review. No shipped UI exists yet; these are design inputs, not prototypes.

Constraints: no scraping or browsing outside the egress allowlist; "pattern review" uses only operator-supplied screenshots, public documentation fetched through the egress client if the operator allowlists it, or first principles (and is labeled accordingly). All text follows the voice rules of B11.12.

Gate G01 passes when: the UX charter, personas, information architecture, journeys, states, accessibility and i18n plans, security-UX review and the review pack exist in `docs/UX/` and link to each other; `xtask ux check` reports zero orphan screens or journeys; the open operator decisions each have a default and an owner; and `docs/gates/G01.md` exists in the E5.1 format with the pasted command output. G01 is a light gate: the operator is shown the pack, but design sign-off is the heavier gate G03.

### T-0011 · Product principles, success measures and UX charter
`P01` `[DOC]` · deps: T-0010 · size: S · owner: ux
**Objective.** Fix the principles every design decision is judged against, and the measures that tell us whether the UX works.
**Steps.**
1. Write `docs/UX/CHARTER.md` containing the seven design principles of B11.1 with one concrete "we will" and "we will not" example each.
2. Define the experience measures: time to first domain in monitor mode, completion rate of the add-domain wizard, number of support-worthy errors per 100 sessions, false-positive appeal rate, time to unban, accessibility defects open, and how each is measured honestly in a self-hosted product (local counters, no third-party analytics).
3. Define the "honesty tests": five questions every screen must pass (Does it show real data? Does it state limits? Is anything claimed untested? Is the safe option default? Can the user undo?).
4. Write a decision log format for UX decisions (`docs/UX/decisions/UXD-nnn.md`) and record the first three: dark-first theming, server-rendered UI, no third-party analytics.
5. Map every principle to enforcement mechanisms (a lint, a checklist, or a test) so principles are not decorative.
6. Add the charter to `AGENTS.md` pointers.
7. Review the charter against the claims policy (section 4) and fix any drift.
8. Commit.
**Deliverables.**
- `docs/UX/CHARTER.md`, `docs/UX/MEASURES.md`
- `docs/UX/decisions/UXD-001..003.md`
**Acceptance.**
- A1: each principle has an enforcement mechanism listed.
- A2: each measure names its data source and its privacy treatment.
- A3: the honesty tests are phrased as yes/no questions.
- A4: claims-lint passes on the new documents.
- A5: the charter fits on four printed pages.
**Tests.**
- `cargo xtask verify` (claims-lint, link check for relative links).
**Notes.** The measures feed T-0139 (overview KPIs for operators) only where they are legitimately collectable.

### T-0025 · Security UX: dangerous actions, lockout prevention, honest warnings
`P01` `[DOC][SEC]` · deps: T-0017 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Make it hard to hurt yourself with a security product.
**Steps.**
1. Catalog every dangerous action (domain removal, DNS delete, NS change guidance, block-mode switch, ban, access-list deny, geo-block, rule with broad scope, safe mode, origin lockdown, API key creation, MFA removal, org deletion, global changes).
2. For each define: risk, safeguard (preview, dry-run, typed confirmation, time box, step-up), undo path, audit event, and the copy.
3. Define the self-lockout guard algorithm requirements (detect acting IP, session, admin CIDR collisions; where the check runs; how it is displayed).
4. Define the preview ("what would change") patterns for DNS, rules, access lists and policies.
5. Define typed-confirmation rules (exact resource name; case-sensitive; paste allowed).
6. Define the time-box pattern (auto-revert timer visible; extend explicitly).
7. Define the honest-limits placements (shield, virtual patches, readiness, block mode collateral).
8. Define the abuse cases of the UI itself (clickjacking, CSRF, UI redress, confused deputy in impersonation) and requirements that counter them.
**Deliverables.**
- `docs/UX/SECURITY-UX.md`, `docs/UX/dangerous-actions.md`
**Acceptance.**
- A1: at least 20 dangerous actions are cataloged with all fields.
- A2: the self-lockout guard has testable requirements.
- A3: each time-boxed feature specifies the revert behavior if the browser closes.
- A4: abuse cases link to ATK-285 to ATK-300.
- A5: copy for each confirmation exists as i18n keys.
**Tests.**
- Implemented as acceptance criteria in T-0327 (self-lockout), T-0235, T-0094 and others.
**Notes.** R-19 and R-28 are enforced here.

<!-- PHASE:P02 -->
## PHASE P02: Design system (T-0029 to T-0052) · milestone M1 · gate G02

Requirement prefix `DSN`. Goal: a complete, tokenized, accessible component library (`hdd-ui`) plus design documentation, built before any product screen. Components are Rust structs (typed props) that render askama partials with scoped CSS classes prefixed `hdd-`; no component accepts raw HTML except through a `SafeHtml` newtype produced only by the template engine or the sanitizer. All tokens come from `design/tokens/*.toml`.

Conventions for every component task in this phase:
- Props struct in `crates/hdd-ui/src/components/<name>.rs`, partial in `crates/hdd-ui/templates/components/<name>.html`, CSS in `crates/hdd-ui/css/components/<name>.css` (cascade layer `components`), snapshot tests with `insta`, unit tests for prop validation (for example icon-only buttons without a label do not compile or return an error).
- Class naming: `hdd-<component>`, modifiers `hdd-<component>--<variant>`, state via ARIA or data attributes (`aria-busy`, `aria-invalid`, `data-state`).
- Every component documents its keyboard map and ARIA contract in `docs/UX/components/<name>.md` (generated from doc comments).
- Visual states shown in the gallery: default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled, loading, error, read-only where relevant, in dark and light.

Gate G02 passes when: the contrast check, token build and CSS budget checks pass; every component renders in the static gallery in both themes; the axe oracle reports no serious or critical findings on the gallery; keyboard maps are documented; the operator has seen screenshots of the gallery.

### T-0029 · Brand foundations: name, logo mark, wordmark, favicons
`P02` `[UI][DOC]` · deps: T-0011 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Establish a simple, ownable identity that works at 16 px and in forced-colors mode, without third-party fonts or raster-only assets.
**Steps.**
1. Write `design/brand/BRAND.md`: name usage ("Hack Dev Defence", short form "HDD"), tone, clear-space rules, minimum sizes, do/don't, and the operator-ownership note (the operator may replace the mark; nothing else depends on its shape).
2. Design the mark as a hand-authored SVG: a shield outline with a stylized request-path notch, using only `currentColor` and one accent via CSS variable so it adapts to themes and forced colors; provide 16, 24, 32, 64 px optical variants.
3. Create the wordmark lockups (horizontal, stacked, icon-only) as SVG with text converted to paths or using the self-hosted font with `font-display` fallback; record how to regenerate them.
4. Generate the favicon set from the SVG by an `xtask ui build` step: `favicon.svg` (with `prefers-color-scheme` handling), `favicon.ico` fallback (16/32/48), `apple-touch-icon.png` (180), maskable PWA icons (192/512) for P32, and a monochrome `safari-pinned-tab.svg`.
5. Create an Open Graph card template rendered at build time (1200x630) as a static asset with the tagline; no raster tools outside Rust (use the `image` crate or render SVG with `resvg` if vetted).
6. Define email header and footer branding that works without remote images (inline CID or text fallback).
7. Add `design/LICENSES.md` stating the mark is original and listing licenses of anything reused.
8. Add the brand name and logo path as profile fields (`branding.product_name`, `branding.logo_path`) consumed by templates, so the operator can rebrand without code changes.
**Deliverables.**
- `design/brand/*.svg`, `design/brand/BRAND.md`, `design/LICENSES.md`
- `xtask ui build` favicon and OG generation
- tests rendering the mark in light, dark and forced-colors mockups
**Acceptance.**
- A1: the mark is legible at 16 px (visual check recorded) and uses no raster data.
- A2: favicon set is generated reproducibly (hash stable across two builds).
- A3: replacing `branding.logo_path` changes the logo everywhere through the template layer without code edits.
- A4: the mark meets 3:1 contrast against both theme backgrounds.
- A5: no external fonts or remote assets are referenced.
**Tests.**
- Snapshot test of the SVG sprite output; build-reproducibility test; contrast test of the mark colors via the token checker.
**Notes.** The operator can supply a real logo later; nothing here blocks on it (UXD default recorded in T-0028).

### T-0030 · Color tokens, themes and the contrast checker
`P02` `[UI][QA]` · deps: T-0029 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Implement the color system of B11.2 as data, generate CSS, and make contrast regressions impossible.
**Steps.**
1. Create `design/tokens/color.toml` with dark and light sets exactly as specified in B11.2, plus semantic aliases (`surface`, `surface-raised`, `text`, `text-muted`, `border`, `border-control`, `accent`, `danger`, `warning`, `success`, `info`, `focus`, `link`).
2. Add the severity palette (critical, high, medium, low, info) and the 8-color chart series for both themes, plus selection and hover tints.
3. Implement `xtask contrast-check` (WCAG relative-luminance formula) that evaluates a declared list of foreground/background pairs with targets (4.5, 3.0) and fails the build if any pair falls short; the pair list lives in `design/tokens/contrast-pairs.toml`.
4. Generate `tokens.css` with `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, `:root[data-theme="light"]`, and `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` defaults for `data-theme="system"`, plus `@media (forced-colors: active)` overrides mapping to system colors.
5. Generate a Rust module with the series colors for the SVG chart kit so charts and CSS never drift.
6. Add a report `acceptance-ui/contrast.json` listing every pair with ratio and pass/fail, included in gate reports.
7. Define the rules for adding colors: new tokens require a pair entry and a use case; ad-hoc hex values in CSS or templates fail a lint (`xtask ui lint`).
8. Document color usage guidance (never color alone; severity always with icon and text).
**Deliverables.**
- `design/tokens/color.toml`, `design/tokens/contrast-pairs.toml`
- generated `crates/hdd-ui/assets/tokens.css` and `src/tokens.rs`
- `xtask contrast-check`, `xtask ui lint` (hex literal ban)
**Acceptance.**
- A1: all pairs in B11.2 meet their targets; the report is generated.
- A2: changing one token to a failing value makes `xtask contrast-check` fail (demonstrated).
- A3: forced-colors CSS uses only system colors.
- A4: a hex literal in a component stylesheet fails `xtask ui lint`.
- A5: dark and light CSS is generated from the same source of truth with no manual duplication.
**Tests.**
- Unit tests for the luminance and ratio functions against reference values; golden test for generated CSS.
**Notes.** Contrast numbers quoted in B11.2 were computed with this formula and must match the checker output.

### T-0031 · Typography tokens and self-hosted fonts
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0030 · size: S · owner: ux
**Objective.** Deliver readable, fast typography with no third-party requests.
**Steps.**
1. Select the sans and mono fonts per B11.3 (Inter and JetBrains Mono under the SIL Open Font License) and record the licenses, versions and checksums in `design/LICENSES.md`.
2. Subset to Latin and Latin-Extended with a Rust-based or vetted tool run by `xtask ui build` (no Python in the pipeline); produce WOFF2 files and verify sizes meet the budget (target at most 60 KB for the sans variable subset, 40 KB for mono regular).
3. Define `@font-face` with `font-display: swap`, `unicode-range`, and preload hints for the critical weight only.
4. Create `design/tokens/type.toml` (scale, line heights, weights, tracking) and generate CSS custom properties; define utility classes for headings `h1`..`h6` and `text-*` roles.
5. Define fallbacks (`system-ui` stacks) with `size-adjust` to limit layout shift when swapping.
6. Define tabular numerals and `font-feature-settings` for tables and counters; define slashed zero for mono where useful.
7. Verify rendering at 200% and 400% zoom and with user stylesheets overriding line height and letter spacing (WCAG 1.4.12).
8. Document how to add a script/locale-specific font later without touching components.
**Deliverables.**
- `crates/hdd-ui/assets/fonts/*.woff2`, `design/tokens/type.toml`, generated `typography.css`
- font license records
**Acceptance.**
- A1: no request leaves the origin for fonts (verified in the browser harness network log).
- A2: font assets meet the size budgets.
- A3: layout shift from font swap is under 0.02 CLS in the gallery page test.
- A4: text spacing override test passes (no clipped text).
- A5: license texts are bundled and referenced from the `/legal` area.
**Tests.**
- Browser test measuring CLS and network requests on the gallery; text-spacing override test using injected CSS.
**Notes.** If subsetting tooling is not available in Rust, record an ADR allowing a pinned build-time tool and keep generated fonts in the repo.

### T-0032 · Spacing, size, radius, elevation, z-index tokens and the token build pipeline
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0030 · size: S · owner: ux
**Objective.** Finish the token set and make `xtask ui build` the only producer of generated design assets.
**Steps.**
1. Create `design/tokens/space.toml`, `size.toml`, `radius.toml`, `elevation.toml`, `zindex.toml`, `breakpoint.toml` with the values of B11.4.
2. Implement the generator that emits custom properties, container-query-friendly breakpoint constants, and Rust constants for server-side layout calculations (chart sizes).
3. Provide logical-property utilities (`margin-inline`, `padding-block`) to support RTL.
4. Define elevation per theme (dark relies on surface tint plus border; light uses shadow) and test that popovers remain distinguishable in forced colors (outline).
5. Implement a token documentation page generator for the gallery (T-0047).
6. Create `xtask ui build` orchestration: tokens, fonts, sprite, CSS bundle, JS bundle, hash-named outputs, and the asset manifest (`assets.json`) with SRI hashes.
7. Make the build deterministic and cached (skip when inputs unchanged).
8. Add budget reporting (CSS and JS gzip sizes) with thresholds from Part A.

- documentation of token usage

- A3: a token removed from TOML but used in CSS fails the build (unknown token lint).
- A4: logical properties are used in the generated utilities.
- A5: budgets are reported even when passing.
**Tests.**

### T-0033 · Motion tokens and reduced-motion behavior
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0032 · size: S · owner: ux
**Objective.** Make motion purposeful and safe.
**Steps.**
1. Create `design/tokens/motion.toml` with durations and easings from B11.5 and generate CSS properties.
2. Write the global reduced-motion layer: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` sets transition and animation durations to 0 except opacity fades up to 80 ms, disables parallax and auto-scrolling, replaces spinners with static text.
3. Define which components animate and how: dialog open/close, drawer slide, toast enter/exit, accordion, readiness ring fill, skeleton shimmer (static under reduced motion), chart draw (none by default).
4. Ban flashing content: no element changes luminance more than three times per second (lint on keyframes and review).
5. Provide a user preference "Reduce motion" in the profile that overrides the system setting in both directions where permitted.
6. Add a motion test utility in the harness to emulate reduced motion and assert computed durations.
7. Document performance rules (animate only `opacity` and `transform`, avoid layout thrash).
8. Add motion usage to the component docs.
**Deliverables.**
- `design/tokens/motion.toml`, `motion.css`, harness helper
**Acceptance.**
- A1: with reduced motion emulated, no transition duration exceeds 80 ms in the gallery (assert on computed styles).
- A2: skeletons and spinners have static equivalents.
- A3: a keyframe lint rejects animations that animate layout properties.
- A4: the profile preference overrides correctly.
- A5: no animation starts on page load without user action except permitted progress indicators.
**Tests.**
- Browser tests emulating `prefers-reduced-motion`; CSS lint unit tests.
**Notes.** Reduced-motion users must lose nothing functionally.

### T-0034 · Icon system and SVG sprite pipeline
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0032 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Provide a consistent, accessible, license-clean icon set without runtime requests per icon.
**Steps.**
1. Choose a permissively licensed icon set (ISC or MIT; record the license text and version in `design/LICENSES.md` and an ADR) and vendor only the icons needed.
2. Draw the custom icons needed that do not exist: `cloud-orange` (proxied), `cloud-grey` (DNS only), `ray-id`, `ban-ip`, `shield-sql`, `nameserver`, with the same grid and stroke.
3. Implement `xtask ui build` sprite generation: one SVG with `<symbol>` entries, ids `i-<name>`, normalized viewBox 24, stroke `currentColor`, optimized with a Rust-based minifier.
4. Create the `Icon` component (name enum generated from the sprite so unknown icons fail to compile), size variants 16 and 20, `aria-hidden` default, with an optional accessible label that switches to `role="img"`.
5. Provide RTL mirroring flags for directional icons.
6. Generate an icon gallery for the design system with names and usage notes.
7. Add a lint that rejects inline `<svg>` in templates except via the component and chart kit.
8. Budget: the sprite must be at most 25 KB gzip; unused icons are tree-shaken by a usage scan.

- ADR for the icon set

- A2: every icon in the required list of B11.6 exists.
- A3: the sprite meets the size budget after tree shaking.
- A4: icon-only buttons require a label (type-level or runtime error).
- A5: custom cloud icons are distinguishable without color (shape/pattern).
**Tests.**
- Compile-fail test for unknown icon; snapshot test of sprite; unit test for RTL mirroring list.
**Notes.** The cloud icons also appear in documentation; keep the source SVGs.

### T-0035 · CSS architecture, cascade layers and the stylesheet bundler
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0032 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Establish maintainable CSS with predictable specificity and enforceable limits.
**Steps.**
1. Define the layer order: `reset, tokens, base, layout, components, patterns, utilities, overrides` and document what belongs where.
2. Write the reset/base styles: box-sizing, margin reset, `color-scheme`, focus-visible default, `prefers-reduced-motion`, forced-colors, selection, scrollbar styling with fallback, `hidden` attribute behavior, `[inert]`.
3. Define naming (`hdd-` prefix, BEM-lite) and the rule that components never style other components' internals.
4. Implement bundling with `lightningcss` inside `xtask`: imports resolved, nesting lowered, minified, source maps for development builds only (never shipped), vendor prefixes per browser targets (documented), unused CSS report.
5. Split bundles: `core.css` (tokens, base, layout, components used on every page) and per-surface bundles (`public.css`, `app.css`, `admin.css`) loaded conditionally to keep the budget.
6. Implement a CSS size and rule-count budget check: core+surface at most 60 KB gzip, hand-written CSS at most 12,000 lines (DEV-V5-002).
7. Add a CSS lint: no `!important` outside `overrides`, no inline styles in templates, no ID selectors, no hex literals, no px font sizes in components.
8. Document browser support targets (last two major versions of Chromium, Firefox, Safari) and progressive enhancement rules.
**Deliverables.**
- `crates/hdd-ui/css/{reset,base,layout,utilities}.css`, layer manifest, bundler in xtask, lint
**Acceptance.**
- A1: bundles are produced with hashed names and listed in `assets.json`.
- A2: CSP can run with `style-src 'self'` (no inline styles anywhere; verified by T-0075 tests later and a static scan now).
- A3: lint violations fail `xtask ui verify`.
- A4: size budgets are reported and enforced.
- A5: unused CSS report exists and is reviewed at gate.
**Tests.**
- Unit tests for the lint rules; golden tests for bundle output; budget test with an artificially large stylesheet.
**Notes.** The CSS cap in DEV-V5-002 includes only hand-written CSS, not generated tokens.

### T-0037 · Buttons, links and icon buttons
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0034, T-0035 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Implement the foundational interactive controls with complete states.
**Steps.**

Define the `Button` props: label (i18n key), variant (primary, secondary, ghost, danger, link), size (compact 32, default 40, large 48), icon (optional, leading/trailing), loading, disabled (with reason), full-width, `type` (submit/button/reset), `form`, and `aria-*` passthrough limited to an allowlist.

### T-0038 · Text inputs, textarea, labels, help and error summary
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0037 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Build accessible form text controls and the form-level error pattern.
**Steps.**
1. Implement `FormField` (label, optional hint, control slot, error message, `aria-describedby` wiring, required text marker), `TextInput` (types text, email, url, search, tel, number with `inputmode`), `Textarea` with character counter (polite, debounced announcements), and read-only/disabled states.
2. Enforce `autocomplete` tokens in props (enum) to satisfy WCAG 1.3.5 and support password managers.
3. Implement `ErrorSummary` that lists errors with in-page links to fields, receives focus on submit failure, and uses `role="alert"` once.
4. Implement inline validation display (on blur and on submit) driven by server responses (field path to message), never client-only truth.
5. Implement input groups (prefix/suffix such as `https://`, `.example.com`), clear button, and copy-on-focus for read-only values.
6. Implement size variants and density rules.
7. Document patterns: never placeholder-as-label, optional vs required text, long-help disclosure.
8. Implement unit tests for ID generation (stable, unique) and association correctness.
**Deliverables.**
- `components/form_field.rs`, `text_input.rs`, `textarea.rs`, `error_summary.rs`, templates, CSS, docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: label, hint and error are programmatically associated (axe label and aria rules pass).
- A2: the error summary receives focus and links work with keyboard.
- A3: every input type has the correct `inputmode` and `autocomplete`.
- A4: error text uses text plus icon, not color alone.
- A5: read-only inputs are focusable and copyable.
**Tests.**
- Snapshot tests; browser tests for focus movement; axe on a form gallery page; unit tests for ID uniqueness across fragments.
**Notes.** HTMX partial swaps must keep IDs stable to avoid breaking `aria-describedby` references.

### T-0039 · Selection controls: checkbox, radio, switch, select, segmented control
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0038 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Provide accessible selection controls built on native elements.
**Steps.**
1. Implement `Checkbox` and `CheckboxGroup` (fieldset/legend), indeterminate state via `aria-checked="mixed"` for parent selections, and large click areas.
2. Implement `Radio` and `RadioCards` (card-style options for integration mode and presets, each with title, description, badge, and disabled-reason) using real radio inputs and a visible focus ring around the card.
3. Implement `Switch` as `input[type=checkbox][role=switch]` with visible "On/Off" text and support for confirm-before-toggle for dangerous settings.
4. Implement `Select` using a native `select` styled consistently, with option groups and a disabled placeholder pattern.
5. Implement `SegmentedControl` (radio group semantics) for mode choices (monitor/log/block).
6. Provide consequence text slots (`aria-describedby`) for security-relevant options.
7. Ensure touch target sizing and spacing in groups.
8. Document keyboard maps (Space toggles, arrows within radio groups).
**Deliverables.**
- component code, templates, CSS, docs, snapshot tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: groups expose legend and role relationships (axe).
- A2: RadioCards are fully keyboard-operable and announce description.
- A3: the switch exposes state text and is not color-dependent.
- A4: indeterminate checkboxes announce mixed state.
- A5: all controls pass the 24 px minimum target and the 40 px default.
**Tests.**
- Snapshot tests; keyboard traversal tests; forced-colors screenshot test.
**Notes.** The mode selector uses SegmentedControl plus a consequences panel, not a dropdown.

### T-0040 · Advanced inputs: password, OTP, tag input, copy field, file dropzone, restricted regex input
`P02` `[UI][SEC]` · deps: T-0038 · size: L · owner: ux
**Objective.** Implement the security-sensitive inputs with accessible, safe behavior.
**Steps.**
1. `PasswordInput`: show/hide button (`aria-pressed`), paste always allowed, `autocomplete` `current-password`/`new-password`, strength meter (`role="meter"` with text label), rule checklist (length, not breached, not common), and a note that no composition rules are required; the meter receives its verdict from the server estimator (T-0106) via HTMX with debounce, never from client heuristics alone.
2. `OtpInput`: single input, `inputmode="numeric"`, `autocomplete="one-time-code"`, `pattern`, auto-submit option off by default, accessible hint about the code source.
3. `TagInput` for IPs/CIDRs/hostnames: commit on Enter/comma/space/paste, per-tag validation messages, removal by keyboard (Backspace/Delete on focused tag), max count, accessible list semantics, and a textual summary ("3 values") for screen readers.
4. `CopyField` with copy button, success announcement via polite live region, fallback selection if Clipboard API unavailable.
5. `FileDropzone`: button-first, drag-and-drop optional, type/size hints, client-side checks for UX, progress, error states, and server authority; limit multiple files by prop.
6. `RegexInput`: monospace input with the server-validated restricted syntax (no lookaround/backreference), inline diagnostics list with positions, never executes the regex client-side.
7. Add secret-value handling: values never rendered into the DOM unless the user reveals them, `autocomplete="off"` where appropriate, and no logging in HTMX events.
8. Document threat considerations (shoulder surfing, clipboard, autofill) per input.
**Deliverables.**
- component code, templates, CSS, islands JS (copy, password toggle; each under budget), docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: password paste is possible and password managers can fill (autocomplete tokens verified).
- A2: the strength meter's text and role are announced and not color-only.
- A3: tag input is fully keyboard-operable and announces additions/removals.
- A4: copy success is announced politely and the secret value is not duplicated in hidden DOM.
- A5: regex diagnostics come from the server and include positions.
**Tests.**
- Browser tests for each input (keyboard flows, paste, announcements); axe; unit tests for tag parsing of messy pasted lists.
**Notes.** Client JS for these inputs is progressive enhancement; core submission works without it.

### T-0041 · Feedback components: toast, banner, inline message, progress, spinner, skeleton, empty and error states
`P02` `[UI]` · deps: T-0037 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Make system feedback consistent, polite and non-blocking.
**Steps.**
1. `Toast` stack with polite/assertive regions, minimum 8 s display, pause on hover and focus, undo action slot, dismiss button, queue limit of 3 visible, and server-driven creation through the `HX-Trigger` contract (T-0084).
2. `Banner`/`Alert` variants (info, success, warning, danger), optional action, dismissible only for non-critical, `role` mapping.
3. `InlineMessage` for field/section feedback with icon+text.
4. `ProgressBar` (determinate/indeterminate), `Spinner` (with text), and `Skeleton` (text, card, table row) with reduced-motion variants and a delayed-appearance rule (show after 300 ms).
5. `EmptyState` (title, explanation, primary action, secondary link, decorative illustration slot) and `ErrorState` (message, request ID chip, retry action).
6. `OfflineBanner` pattern placeholder for connectivity loss.
7. Document usage rules: toasts never carry the only copy of an error; banners for persistent states; skeleton thresholds.
8. Provide server helpers to build these from `Problem` responses (RFC 9457) consistently.
**Deliverables.**
- components, CSS, docs, snapshot tests, `Problem`-to-UI helpers
**Acceptance.**
- A1: toasts do not steal focus and are announced once.
- A2: banners expose correct roles and meet contrast in both themes.
- A3: skeletons are static under reduced motion.
- A4: the error state shows the request ID and a retry control that works without JS via a link or form.
- A5: no component uses color alone to convey state.
**Tests.**
- Browser tests for announcement behavior (via accessibility tree snapshot), delayed skeleton test, axe.
**Notes.** The toast contract fields are documented for T-0084.

### T-0042 · Overlays: dialog, drawer, confirm dialog, popover, tooltip, dropdown menu
`P02` `[UI][SEC]` · deps: T-0041 · size: L · owner: ux
**Objective.** Implement overlays with correct focus management and safe confirmation patterns.
**Steps.**
1. `Dialog` built on native `<dialog>` with `showModal()`: labelled by heading, `aria-describedby` for body, focus moves to the first meaningful element or the safe action, `Escape` closes, focus returns to the invoker, background inert; no-JS fallback navigates to a full page route.
2. `Drawer` (side panel) with the same semantics, used by event detail (S-066) and navigation on small screens; deep-linkable by URL.
3. `ConfirmDialog` with consequences list, optional type-to-confirm (exact resource name, paste allowed), default focus on the safe action, destructive button disabled until confirmed, and optional "Run as dry-run first" link for self-lockout cases.
4. `Popover` (non-modal) with focus management and Esc, `aria-expanded` on the trigger.
5. `Tooltip` for supplemental description only (never required), shown on hover and focus, dismissible, hoverable, persistent (WCAG 1.4.13), referenced via `aria-describedby`.
6. `Menu` (button + menu) with roving tabindex, type-ahead, `aria-haspopup`, `Home/End`, and close on Tab.
7. Implement stacking rules (z-index tokens) and scroll locking without layout shift (scrollbar-gutter).
8. Document anti-patterns (modal inside modal, autoplay dialogs, hover-only tooltips).
**Deliverables.**
- components, CSS, small island JS modules for popover/menu positioning (CSS anchor positioning when available, JS fallback), docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: focus is trapped inside modals and returns on close (browser test).
- A2: type-to-confirm requires the exact name and blocks the destructive action otherwise.
- A3: tooltips satisfy 1.4.13 (dismissible, hoverable, persistent).
- A4: menus support full keyboard navigation and Escape.
- A5: dialogs work without JavaScript through route fallbacks for critical flows.
**Tests.**
- Browser tests for focus management and keyboard; axe; unit tests for type-to-confirm logic server-side.
**Notes.** ConfirmDialog is the only component allowed to render destructive primary buttons.

### T-0045 · Security-domain components: Ray ID, IP chip, countdown, payload viewer, readiness ring, cloud toggle, nameserver card, verification poller
`P02` `[UI][SEC]` · deps: T-0044 · size: L · owner: ux
**Objective.** Build the product-specific components with strict safety properties.
**Steps.**
1. `RayIdChip`: validates the `16hex-HDD1` format, monospace, copy button, link to event; invalid values render as plain text.
2. `IpChip`: IP with textual country code and optional flag (decorative), ASN label, actions menu (ban, allow, lookup, copy), IPv6 /64 key note, and collateral-risk badge slot.
3. `CountdownBadge`: server-rendered remaining time with a small island updating every second only when visible; static text for reduced motion and screen readers (updates announced no more than every 30 s).
4. `PayloadViewer`: renders redacted evidence as escaped text in a `pre`, highlights the matched span using background plus underline, indicates the 512-byte cap, never interprets HTML, and offers copy of the escaped text.
5. `ReadinessRing`: SVG ring with textual score, status text and list; the aria label announces "Protection readiness N out of 100"; includes the footnote slot.
6. `CloudToggle`: two-state control labeled "Proxied" and "DNS only" with icons and a consequence popover; server confirms and shows the resulting answer set.
7. `NameserverCard` and `VerificationPoller`: copy fields, status text, last/next check times, polite live region, manual "Check now" respecting rate limits.
8. Write abuse-case tests: HTML/JS payloads in `PayloadViewer`, extremely long unbroken strings, bidirectional control characters (rendered visibly and neutralized), and homoglyph hostnames (punycode shown alongside).
**Deliverables.**
- components, CSS, small islands, docs, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: XSS payloads in `PayloadViewer` never execute and render as escaped text (browser test with CSP violation trap).
- A2: bidi control characters are visibly neutralized.
- A3: readiness ring's text alternative contains the score and footnote.
- A4: the cloud toggle has a non-color distinction and a consequence description.
- A5: poller announcements are polite and rate-limited.
**Tests.**
- Browser tests with hostile strings; snapshot tests; axe; fuzz target for the escaping function.
**Notes.** This component set is the main defense against stored XSS from attacker-controlled event data (ATK-297).

<!-- PHASE:P03 -->
## PHASE P03: Screen design and clickable design prototypes (T-0053 to T-0070) · milestone M1 · gate G03

Requirement prefix `SCR`. Goal: design every screen of B12 with the design system, validate flows and states, review accessibility and content, and obtain the operator's sign-off before building the product. Prototypes are **design artifacts** under `design/prototypes/`: static HTML generated from the real components by `xtask ui prototype build`, with visibly labeled synthetic example data. They are never shipped, never served from the product, never used by the acceptance suite, and are excluded from `cargo xtask release` (R-16).

Phase gate G03 passes when: all 143 screens have prototype pages in all required states; heuristic and accessibility reviews have recorded fixes; the claims-lint passes; and the operator has reviewed screenshots and recorded sign-off or a list of changes (UNVERIFIED(`human_step_pending`) until then, which blocks only the build of the affected screens).

### T-0053 · Prototype tooling and policy
`P03` `[UI][QA]` · deps: T-0052 · size: M · owner: ux
**Objective.** Build a safe way to produce clickable prototypes from real components, with guards that prevent shipping them.
**Steps.**
1. Implement `xtask ui prototype build` that renders prototype pages from Rust fixtures (`design/prototypes/src/*.rs`) into static HTML under `target/prototypes/` using `hdd-ui` components and the same CSS bundles.
2. Mark every prototype page with a fixed banner "Design artifact. Example data. Not the product." styled with a dedicated token, and add `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`.
3. Define the synthetic data policy: reserved names only (`example.org`, `.invalid`, RFC 5737 addresses), obviously fake brand names, no real personal data.
4. Implement link wiring between prototype pages so flows are clickable (static links plus minimal state through URL fragments); no JavaScript beyond the shipped islands.
5. Add a guard in `xtask release` and in CI: the shipped crates and asset manifests must not include prototype content (path and content scans), and `hdd-web` has no dependency on the prototype crate.
6. Add a guard in claims-lint to scan prototypes too (copy must still be honest).
7. Implement an index page listing all prototypes by surface/screen ID/state with links and statuses (draft, reviewed, approved).
8. Document the workflow and the review process.
**Deliverables.**
- `xtask ui prototype`, `design/prototypes/` skeleton, index generator, release guard
**Acceptance.**
- A1: prototype build fails if a fixture contains a non-reserved domain or a routable IP.
- A2: `cargo xtask release --dry-run` fails if prototype files are present in shipped inputs (demonstrated by a test).
- A3: every page shows the design-artifact banner and `noindex`.
- A4: the index lists screens with state variants.
- A5: prototype CSS/JS equals shipped bundles (hash equality), proving fidelity.
**Tests.**
- Unit tests for reserved-name validation; release-guard test; link checker over the prototype set.
**Notes.** Interaction fidelity is deliberately low (no real backend), but visual and semantic fidelity is high.
