`P21` `[DP][UI][API]` · deps: T-0408, T-0362, T-0363, T-0222 · size: L · owner: dp
**Objective.** Apply the leak engine safely to live responses and let owners control it.
**Steps.**
1. Implement the response-phase stage (pipeline stage 17): eligibility rules — only `GET/POST/...` responses with status 2xx/4xx/5xx and text-like content types (`text/*`, `application/json`, `application/xml`, `application/javascript` configurable), `Content-Encoding` of identity/gzip/br/deflate/zstd decompressed in a bounded streaming decoder (decompression bomb limits: decompressed size ≤ 10 MiB and ratio ≤ 20:1 per Appendix E4), skip for `Range`/`206`, WebSocket upgrades, server-sent events, gRPC, `Content-Length` > the large-body threshold (stream through, tag `skipped_large`), and per-path exclusions.
2. Implement the **hold window**: buffer up to the first 64 KiB of the decompressed body (configurable 16–256 KiB) before releasing headers; bodies larger than the window are scanned over the prefix and tagged `partial_scan`; the proxy documents the latency effect (added time to first byte bounded by origin send time of the first window, with a 250 ms hold timeout after which streaming proceeds and the response is tagged `scan_timeout`).
3. Implement modes: `off`, `monitor` (record events, pass body), `block` (high-confidence findings replace the response with the branded 500 `S-143`-style page and record a `critical` `data_leak` event; medium findings are masked or recorded per policy, see below), plus `mask` (replace only the matched span with a fixed marker when the content type is JSON/text and the replacement preserves syntactic validity; otherwise fall back to block). Masking is limited to database error and path patterns; secrets always block.
4. Recompute `Content-Length`, strip `Content-Encoding` only when the body had to be rewritten (recompress is not attempted; document the cost), keep `ETag`/`Last-Modified` semantics sane (drop the strong `ETag` on rewritten bodies), preserve `Vary`, never touch HEAD or 304 responses.
5. Implement the **fail-safe**: scanner errors or panics fall back to pass-through with a metric and an alert (the outbound filter fails open for availability by design because it is a secondary control; this is documented and the opposite of the request-side rule R-26; the readiness page states it).
6. Implement `S-097` backend: mode, exclusions (path + method + content type), pattern pack version, per-category toggles (database errors, stack traces, secrets, source code, directory listings, paths), confidence thresholds, test tool ("scan a pasted response" using the pure engine with redaction), event table, and the canary `leak.txt` verification button that runs the AC-10 probe via the pilot path.
7. Record events with ray id, path template, category, confidence, mode, action, response status, `partial_scan`, and the redacted snippet (≤ 512 B), applying the 30-day default retention; send `critical` findings to notifications (owner may opt out of snippet storage).
8. Emit metrics: scanned bytes, hold latency histogram, findings by category/action, skipped reasons, timeouts, masking successes/failures.
9. Write tests: origins returning each pattern in plain/gzip/br/chunked/HTTP2, boundary-spanning patterns, large bodies, binary data (images, PDFs, zips) untouched, streaming responses untouched, SSE untouched, HEAD/304 untouched, JSON validity after masking, monitor vs block behavior, exclusions, panic injection.
**Deliverables.**
- proxy stage, S-097 backend and screen wiring, metrics, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: AC-10 canary leak is blocked in `block` mode and recorded in `monitor` mode.
- A2: binary/streaming/Range/HEAD/304 responses are byte-identical to the origin response (differential test).
- A3: HDD-side scan and mask time p99 ≤ 3 ms per 64 KiB window on the builder (origin body-wait during the hold is origin time, C14.9); hold timeout behavior verified.
- A4: scanner panic injection leads to pass-through with an alert and no connection reset.
- A5: masked JSON responses remain valid JSON in 100% of fixtures.
**Tests.**
- Integration (proxy + fault origins), differential, property (chunking), performance.
**Notes.** The documented limit (prefix-only scan beyond the window) is shown in S-097 and the readiness page.

### T-0410 · Response header policy engine (security headers, disclosure removal, per-site overrides)
`P21` `[DP][UI][API]` · deps: T-0361, T-0409, T-0200 · size: M · owner: dp
**Objective.** Set safe defaults on every response without breaking the origin's own choices.
**Steps.**
1. Implement the **policy document** per site: `strip` (list of headers to remove, defaults `Server`, `X-Powered-By`, `X-AspNet-Version`, `X-AspNetMvc-Version`, `X-Generator`, `X-Drupal-*`, `X-Pingback`), `set_always` (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-XSS-Protection: 0`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy` conservative default or none if the origin sets one), `set_if_absent` (`X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` and CSP `frame-ancestors 'self'` only when neither is present; opt-out per site/path), `hsts` per TLS policy, `server_banner` (`Hack-Dev-Defence` default, override or removal), and `custom` (additional headers with allowlisted names; forbidden: `Set-Cookie`, `Content-Length`, hop-by-hop).
2. Implement precedence: the origin's explicit security headers win over `set_if_absent`; `set_always` wins over the origin only for `X-Content-Type-Options` and `X-XSS-Protection`; per-path overrides win over site defaults; every decision is traceable (`header_policy_trace` in debug mode for the sandbox).
3. Implement **safe testing of CSP and framing risks**: before enabling `X-Frame-Options`, a preview scanner warns when the site is known to be embedded (owner marks `allowed_embedders` list); the policy supports `frame-ancestors` allowlists.
4. Add a **CSP report-only suggestion helper** (links to T-0412) that never enables enforcement automatically; enforcement requires an explicit toggle with a reminder of breakage risk, a staged rollout (report-only for ≥ 7 days recommended in the UI) and an easy revert.
5. Implement HSTS interplay with certificate state (HSTS only when a valid certificate exists and the HTTPS redirect is on; preload guidance but no preload submission by HDD).
6. Implement header-size and count limits on responses (reject or truncate the origin's oversized `Set-Cookie` bursts with a 502 and a clear event instead of passing malformed headers), duplicate `Content-Length` handling, and removal of `Via` when configured.
7. Wire the UI in S-052/S-097 sections: toggle each group, show effective headers for a sample URL ("Preview with the sandbox canary"), explain each header in plain language, and show a diff of origin headers versus final headers from the last sampled response (headers only, no bodies).
8. Write tests: precedence matrix (≥ 120 cases), per-path overrides, absent/present origin headers, HSTS gating, oversize header handling, no alteration of `Set-Cookie` here (cookie policy is T-0411), HEAD/304 handling, and HTTP/2 header casing.
**Deliverables.**
- header policy module, schema, UI wiring, tests, docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: the precedence matrix passes in all 120+ cases.
- A2: origin-set CSP/XFO are never overridden by `set_if_absent`.
- A3: HSTS is never sent without a valid certificate and the redirect enabled.
- A4: `Set-Cookie` is untouched by this stage (differential test).
- A5: policy preview matches live canary output byte-for-byte for the chosen URL.
**Tests.**
- Unit (matrix), integration (canary), differential.
**Notes.** The defaults aim to be non-breaking; anything with breakage potential is opt-in and reversible.

### T-0411 · Cookie and session protection (flag upgrades, scope hardening, fixation signals)
`P21` `[DP][SEC][UI]` · deps: T-0410, T-0361 · size: M · owner: dp
**Objective.** Reduce the damage of weak session handling in the protected application without changing application logic.
**Steps.**
1. Implement the cookie policy per site (all opt-in, default `report` mode): `secure_upgrade` (add `Secure` when the request was HTTPS), `httponly_upgrade` (add `HttpOnly` to cookies whose names match a configurable session-like pattern: `sess`, `sid`, `token`, `auth`, `PHPSESSID`, `JSESSIONID`, `connect.sid`, `laravel_session`, `ASP.NET_SessionId`, excluding cookies the app reads from JavaScript, listed by the owner), `samesite_default` (add `SameSite=Lax` when absent; `None` requires `Secure`), `prefix_hardening` (suggest `__Host-` prefixes; only report), `domain_narrowing` (drop broad `Domain=` attributes when the owner enables it), and `max_age_cap` (cap session cookie lifetime).
2. In `report` mode, record findings (cookie name hashed + attribute gaps, never values) in a per-site `cookie_audit` aggregate, displayed in S-043/S-097 with remediation text ("set these flags in your framework: …") for the common stacks.
3. Implement **session-fixation and hijack signals** (monitor first): the same session cookie value (HMAC'd keyed hash, never stored raw) seen from a new IP /24 and a new user-agent family within 60 s raises `session_anomaly` (soft score) with a tunable sensitivity; a session cookie value presented after the origin set a new value for the same cookie name on the same client (fixation indicator) is recorded; optional step-up (challenge) on high-risk anomalies for configured sensitive paths.
4. Implement a **session binding option** for strict sites (off by default): HDD adds a signed binding cookie (`__Host-hdd_bind`) containing a keyed hash of (client IP /24 or /56, UA family) and, if the application cookie arrives with a mismatching binding, applies the configured action (log, challenge, block). The option explains its drawbacks (mobile networks, privacy) and is rate limited to avoid lockouts; it fails open on missing binding to avoid breaking logged-in users during enablement (grace period 7 days).
5. Implement **cookie size/count protections**: reject responses with more than the configured number or total size of cookies (protects browsers and origin from cookie bombing), and strip cookies with invalid names.
6. Add **admin-path token tripwires**: the HDD-issued challenge clearance cookie (`__Host-hdd_cl`) is never forwarded to the origin (strip on the upstream request) and never logged.
7. Wire controls and explanations in the UI with a "what changes for your users" summary and a "revert" button; log every enablement as an audit event.
8. Write tests: attribute rewriting matrix (≥ 150 cases including multiple `Set-Cookie` headers, folded values, quoted values, unusual casing, partitioned cookies, `__Host-` and `__Secure-` prefixes), no mutation in `report` mode, binding behavior with grace period, clearance cookie stripping, performance (rewriting adds ≤ 50 µs per response with cookies).
**Deliverables.**
- cookie policy module, signals, UI, tests, docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: in `report` mode no `Set-Cookie` header is modified (differential test over 10,000 responses).
- A2: with upgrades enabled all matrix cases produce the documented output; `SameSite=None` without `Secure` is never emitted.
- A3: the clearance cookie never reaches the origin or logs.
- A4: session binding with a mismatch triggers the configured action only after the grace period.
- A5: cookie values never appear in events, logs or metrics (grep test).
**Tests.**
- Unit matrix; integration with test origins; privacy greps.
**Notes.** Session binding is an advanced option marked "may log out users on network changes".

### T-0412 · Client-side supply-chain visibility: CSP report collector, SRI advisor and third-party script inventory
`P21` `[API][DP][SEC][UI]` · deps: T-0410, T-0302 · size: L · owner: api
**Objective.** Help owners notice injected or compromised third-party scripts (skimmers, malicious tags) without HDD modifying page content.
**Steps.**
1. Implement the **reserved report endpoint** `POST /__hdd/csp-report/{site-token}` on customer domains (path prefix `/__hdd/` is reserved, handled before the origin), accepting `application/csp-report` and `application/reports+json` (Reporting API) with a 64 KiB cap, strict parsing, per-IP and per-site rate limits (30/min/IP), no cookies, CORS closed, and authentication by the unguessable per-site token in the path (rotatable). Reports never reach the origin.
2. Normalize and store aggregated reports: `(violated-directive, blocked-uri host/scheme, document-uri path template, source-file host, disposition)` with counts per day; discard query strings and fragments; sample at most 50 distinct raw reports per site per day with redaction; cap storage (plan-based).
3. Implement the **third-party script inventory**: from CSP reports plus (opt-in) a periodic **passive crawl** of the owner's own public pages through the sandbox/posture scanner path (`hdd-scan`, built in P27, ≤ 5 req/s, only the owner's verified domain) that extracts `<script src>`, `<link rel=stylesheet>`, `<iframe src>`, `<form action>` hosts and notes missing `integrity` attributes, `crossorigin`, and `rel=noopener` on external links. The crawl respects `robots.txt` disallow for the scanner UA only as informational; consent is explicit per domain.
4. Implement **new-host alerts**: a script/connect host never seen before on a checkout or login page (path classes declared by the owner) raises `new_third_party_host` as an attention item with severity depending on page class (payment pages high), and a "mark as expected" action with reason.
5. Implement the **SRI advisor**: for static third-party scripts on a CDN with stable URLs, compute and display recommended `integrity` hashes (fetched via the egress client from the pinned host, size-limited, shown with the fetch time and a warning that dynamic scripts cannot use SRI); never write hashes into the owner's pages.
6. Implement the **CSP builder wizard** (S-097 sub-page): starts from observed reports, generates a report-only policy with explanations per directive, shows risky patterns (`'unsafe-inline'`, wildcards, `data:` for scripts), and offers "add as report-only response header" through T-0410 (never enforced by default).
7. Add **form-action tripwire** (optional): for login/payment forms, report if `<form action>` host differs from the declared set (observed by the crawler only; HDD does not rewrite HTML in v5).
8. Provide events, metrics, API (`GET D/client-side/*`), notifications, and docs; add everything to the readiness score as low-weight informational items.
9. Write tests: report parsing fuzz (malformed JSON, huge arrays, deep nesting), rate limits, token rotation, redaction, aggregation, crawler extraction fixtures (static HTML fixtures with inline events and obfuscated loaders), new-host alert flow, SRI computation correctness, claims-lint ("helps you notice changes", never "prevents skimming").
**Deliverables.**
- report endpoint, aggregation, inventory, SRI advisor, CSP builder, UI, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: the endpoint rejects oversize/malformed/unauthenticated reports with the documented statuses and never forwards them to the origin.
- A2: aggregation stores no query strings/fragments (property test).
- A3: crawl traffic stays within the posture-scan rate limit and only targets verified domains (audit log check).
- A4: a newly added third-party host on a declared checkout page raises an attention item in the fixture scenario.
- A5: SRI hashes match independently computed values (`openssl dgst`) for fixture scripts.
**Tests.**
- Unit/fuzz (parsers), integration (endpoint, crawler against fixture origin), browser e2e for the CSP builder.
**Notes.** The `/__hdd/` prefix is reserved platform-wide; origin applications using it receive a warning at onboarding.

### T-0413 · Tenant egress safety in the data plane: SSRF guard, DNS pinning and rebinding verification
`P21` `[DP][SEC][QA]` · deps: T-0365, T-0163, T-0378 · size: M · owner: sec
**Objective.** Prove that HDD cannot be turned into a request-forwarding weapon against private networks or other tenants through origin configuration.
**Steps.**
1. Review and unify every code path in which HDD opens an outbound connection on behalf of a tenant: origin client, health checks, connectivity test, origin TLS diagnostics, CSP-related fetches, webhooks (P24), feed fetchers (no tenant input), SRI advisor, posture scanner, external DNS target resolution (flattening). Document each in `docs/EGRESS.md` with the guard used.
2. Centralize the guard in `hdd-common::egress` (the single connector): resolve → validate → connect-to-IP with SNI/Host preserved; reject loopback, link-local (including 169.254.169.254), private (RFC 1918/ULA), CGNAT (100.64/10), multicast, reserved, documentation, IPv4-mapped/translated IPv6 forms, `0.0.0.0`, broadcast, and the platform's own addresses, with overrides only for `owner_only` mode via the explicit `egress.private_origin_allowlist` profile entry (never for `saas`), never for the metadata/link-local ranges, and with the single built-in exemption `origin_kind=platform_internal` for HDD's own surfaces (section 2.9). Add the egress class `dns_resolution` (section 2.1) to the inventory, the kill switch (`hddctl egress disable dns_resolution`) and `docs/EGRESS.md`.
3. Add **pinning and revalidation**: connections use the validated IP; revalidation on every new connection and when a DNS TTL expires; if a hostname's A set changes to include a blocked address, the entire host is blocked (not just the address) until an owner edit, with an event `origin_rebinding_detected`.
4. Enforce **port allowlists** and **protocol allowlists** (no `file:`, `gopher:`, `ftp:`; schemes `http`/`https` only), no redirects followed anywhere in the egress client (a single code path, tested).
5. Add a **kill switch for egress classes** (`hddctl egress disable webhooks|probes|scan`) for incident response.
6. Build the **SSRF test matrix** (≥ 150 vectors): decimal/octal/hex IP encodings, IPv6 forms, userinfo tricks (`http://good@evil`), URL parser differentials (backslashes, tab/newline), unicode dots, trailing dots, `localhost` variants, DNS names resolving to private IPs, DNS rebinding with short TTL flip, redirect to internal, SSRF through `Host` and SNI fields, and the cloud metadata endpoints; run against every egress user via a common harness.
7. Add a **static analysis gate** (`xtask egress-lint`) that fails the build if any crate other than `hdd-common::egress` constructs a `reqwest::Client`/`hyper` client/`TcpStream::connect` toward a non-loopback target, with an explicit allowlist file for the host-local services.
8. Run the matrix in the lab with a DNS rebinding server (controllable authoritative server) and record evidence for AC-17.
**Deliverables.**
- unified egress module, egress documentation, test matrix, lint gate
**Acceptance.**
- A1: all 150+ vectors are rejected on every egress path (matrix report by path).
- A2: the egress-lint gate passes and fails when a violation is injected.
- A3: rebinding flips are caught at connect time and block the host.
- A4: `saas` mode has no override path for private ranges (config validation test).
- A5: `docs/EGRESS.md` lists every outbound path with its guard.
**Tests.**
- Matrix harness, static gate tests, lab rebinding server.
**Notes.** This is AC-17's data-plane half; the save-time half is T-0163.

### T-0414 · Bulk-exfiltration and scraping-of-data guard (response volume and record-count anomalies)
`P21` `[DP][SEC]` · deps: T-0408, T-0349, T-0312 · size: M · owner: dp
**Objective.** Limit damage when an injection or authorization flaw exists and the attacker starts pulling data.
**Steps.**
1. Implement per-client (IP /32,/64 plus session-hash when available) **response-volume tracking** on configured sensitive path classes (API collections, export endpoints, search, user listings): rolling counters for response bytes, response count, distinct resource ids observed in paths/queries (bounded sets), and JSON array element counts for responses within the scan window (only counts, never content).
2. Define anomaly rules with adaptive baselines (T-0349): a single client retrieving more than `k` times the p99 volume of normal clients within a window, sequential-id enumeration across many distinct ids, large JSON arrays returned repeatedly to the same client, and export endpoint usage bursts. Actions: soft score, rate limit, challenge, and (on high confidence) ban with attack category `data_exfiltration`.
3. Implement **response-size ceilings** (owner-configurable per path class): a response above the ceiling is replaced with a 502-style error when `block` is selected (default `monitor`), preventing accidental or malicious dumps from vulnerable endpoints.
4. Add **sensitive-data shape alarms** (optional, `monitor` by default): in the scan window, count occurrences of email addresses, 13–19 digit sequences passing the Luhn check (payment card shapes), SSN-like patterns and IBAN shapes; produce counts only (no content, no storage of matches). Events fire when a single response contains more than a configured count, flagged as "possible mass data disclosure" with the path template and Ray ID.
5. Integrate with the SQLi shield: when a hard SQLi hit was recorded for the same client in the last 10 minutes and an anomalous volume follows, escalate the ban TTL one rung and raise `possible_data_exfiltration`.
6. Expose UI controls in S-097/S-057 (path classes, ceilings, shapes toggle, thresholds) with plain-language descriptions and false-positive guidance (legitimate exports, mobile apps with paging).
7. Ensure privacy: counters are keyed with HMAC'd identifiers, retention 24 h, no content stored; the shape alarms are disclosed in the privacy docs (data processed in memory only).
8. Write tests: simulated enumeration, legitimate paging users, export usage, Luhn/IBAN validators (property tests with known valid/invalid sets), ceiling behavior, interaction with SQLi ban escalation, performance (≤ 0.2 ms added at p99 for scanned responses).
**Deliverables.**
- guard module, schema/settings, UI wiring, tests, docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: sequential-id enumeration of 500 ids by one client is flagged within the configured window with zero flags for 1,000 simulated normal clients.
- A2: Luhn-valid test card numbers in a response trigger the alarm; non-valid 16-digit numbers do not (fixtures).
- A3: no match content is stored anywhere (storage/log grep).
- A4: ceiling `block` mode returns the branded error and records an event.
- A5: SQLi-ban escalation integration test passes.
**Tests.**
- Unit/property (validators), simulation tests, integration, privacy greps.
**Notes.** This is a mitigation, not a data-loss-prevention product; the UI says so.

## PHASE P22: Platform admin panel (T-0417 to T-0440) · milestone M9 · gate G22

Requirement prefix `ADM`. Goal: a complete, safe operator console on the `admin` surface for running the platform: overview, tenants, users, domains, impersonation, tenant lifecycle, global jail and never-ban, rule packs, threat-intel feeds, infrastructure, abuse and signup policy, plans, audit, settings, email templates, announcements and flags, emergency controls, releases and backups, exposure board, shield and firewall views, and support lookup. Screens S-100 to S-130 are built here; screens whose data comes from later phases (S-125 to S-128) ship with the full contract, honest empty states and real wiring completed in P25 to P27.

Non-negotiables: the admin surface is isolated (own host, own session cookie scope, forced MFA, short timeouts, step-up for sensitive mutations, never reachable from the app host); every mutation writes an audit event with actor, reason and before/after; platform staff cannot read tenants' request bodies or secrets (R-22); impersonation is read-only, time-boxed, banner-marked and audited; no screen shows a number without a real source (R-16: "Unknown (reason)" otherwise); typed confirmation protects irreversible actions; the permission catalog (B4.2) is the only authority and is enforced server-side per route.

Gate G22 passes when: every S-1xx admin screen in scope renders from real data or an honest empty state; the platform-role privilege matrix passes in full (AC-01 admin isolation, AC-42 admin operations); all mutations are audited and chain-verified; accessibility, visual and performance checks pass for all admin screens; and no admin API can be reached with an org-role session or from the app host.

### T-0417 · Admin surface foundation: isolation, session scope, layout shell and navigation
`P22` `[UI][SEC]` · deps: T-0134, T-0125, T-0118, T-0073, T-0137 · size: L · owner: web
**Objective.** Build the secure frame in which every admin screen lives.
**Steps.**
1. Route the `admin_host` surface in `hdd-web` with a dedicated router and middleware stack: platform-role session required, host-header verification (admin routes are unreachable on app/www hosts and app routes are unreachable on the admin host; 404 without hints), `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, strict CSP with nonces, no third-party assets, frame denial.
2. Enforce the admin session policy from B4.1: separate cookie `__Host-hdd_adm` (distinct from the app cookie), forced MFA at login, idle timeout 15 min, absolute 8 h, step-up TTL 5 min for `S` permissions, session binding to the admin CIDR rule when `admin_exposure=routed_with_cidr`, concurrent session cap of 3 with a visible list.
3. Honor `admin_exposure`: in `tunnel_only` the listener binds to loopback or a private interface; in `routed_with_cidr` requests from outside `admin_cidrs` receive the neutral 404 before any application logic; document the tunnel setup (SSH/WireGuard) in the runbook.
4. Implement the admin layout: a left navigation grouped as Overview; Tenants (tenants, users, domains); Security (global jail, never-ban, rule packs, threat intel, abuse); Infrastructure (nodes and services, certificates and zones, releases, backups, shield and firewall, exposure); Platform (plans, signup policy, settings, email templates, announcements and flags, emergency); Audit and Support. A persistent top banner shows "ADMIN" with environment (pilot/production), the lifecycle stage and any active emergency state; the banner is not color-only (text + icon) and passes contrast checks.

8. Add the admin breadcrumbs, page titles and keyboard shortcuts consistent with the app shell, plus a compact density default for tables.
9. Add structured logging of every admin request (actor, route, outcome) to the platform audit stream (reads for sensitive screens are logged too), and rate-limit admin endpoints (60 req/min/session; 10 failed step-ups per hour lock the session).
10. Write tests: route-permission matrix for all admin routes (generated from the route registry), host confusion tests, org-role session rejection, timeout behavior, cookie flags, CSP presence, neutral 404 behavior outside CIDR, step-up gating, and a negative test that no admin asset URL is cacheable.

**Notes.** The admin surface is the highest-value target in the system; this task's tests are re-run in every later phase gate.

### T-0418 · Admin overview (S-100): real platform health and attention list
`P22` `[UI][API]` · deps: T-0417, T-0214, T-0140 · size: L · owner: web
**Objective.** Show operators the true state of the platform in one screen, with honest unknowns.
**Steps.**
1. Define the overview data contract (`GET P/overview`): edge health (proxy/DNS up, config revision, p99 proxy-added latency, snapshot age), control health (API/web/worker up, queue depth and oldest job), data stores (Postgres/Redis health, replication lag if any, disk), certificates expiring within a quarter of their lifetime, ban set size and kernel enforcement mode, shield state, attack summary for the last hour (top categories, top ASNs, blocked count, bans created), abuse queue size, signups in 24 h, pending upgrades, backup recency, and exposure board counters.
2. Implement collectors in `hdd-analytics`/`hdd-worker` that read from real sources (Prometheus-style internal registry, Postgres, Redis, heartbeats); every field carries `value`, `as_of`, `source` and `status` (`ok`, `warn`, `crit`, `unknown(reason)`).
3. Build the screen with a card grid (tokens from the design system), each card with title, primary number, a text status (not color-only), a sparkline (SVG, with a table alternative), an "as of" timestamp and a drill-down link to the owning screen.
4. Implement the **attention list**: derived from rules (certificate expiring, queue stuck, replication lag, backup stale, secondary lag, shield state, exposure overdue, mass ban anomalies, failed upgrades, disk usage), ranked by severity then age, each item with an owner suggestion and a deep link; items can be snoozed with a reason (audited) and reappear after the snooze.
5. Implement live updates through SSE at 5 s intervals for the top row of cards; if SSE is blocked, refresh via HTMX polling (30 s) and show "Live updates paused" state.
6. Implement time-range selector (1 h, 24 h, 7 d) for the attack summary, with data from rollups (T-0140); an empty rollup shows "No data in range" rather than zeros when the collector was down.
7. Add the "platform mode" strip: lifecycle stage, deployment mode, active maintenance/safe mode/signup freeze, and `lockdown` status of the admin surface.
8. Write tests: unknown handling (kill each source and verify the card shows `unknown(reason)`), attention rule unit tests (≥ 20 rules, each with trigger and clear conditions), snooze behavior, SSE fallback, performance (overview renders in ≤ 300 ms server time with warm caches), a11y.
**Deliverables.**
- API, collectors, screen, attention rules, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: killing Redis/Postgres/worker in a test shows the correct card status within one collection interval and creates the matching attention item.
- A2: no card ever displays a zero where the source is unavailable.
- A3: every number links to its source screen.
- A4: attention items clear automatically when the condition clears.
- A5: the screen meets contrast, keyboard and screen-reader checks.
**Tests.**
- Integration with fault injection; unit (rules); browser e2e; axe.
**Notes.** The overview is read-only; actions live on the owning screens.

### T-0422 · Impersonation (S-118): read-only view-as with time box and banner

### T-0423 · Tenant lifecycle: suspend, delete with grace, data export hold and purge
`P22` `[API][DB][SEC][OPS]` · deps: T-0419, T-0130, T-0421 · size: L · owner: api
**Objective.** Make every way a tenant can end or be stopped safe, reversible where it should be, and complete in data handling.
**Steps.**
1. Define the tenant state machine: `active → suspended → active` (reversible), `active/suspended → deletion_scheduled (grace 14 days) → deleting → deleted`, with `legal_hold` as an orthogonal flag blocking deletion. Document legal effects and customer-visible messages.
2. Implement suspend semantics: sign-in allowed for read-only access to export data (configurable), all domains switch to the neutral suspended page (S-148), DNS continues serving unless the reason is DNS abuse (admin choice), API keys return `ERR-TENANT-001`, ACME renewals pause, notifications continue to owners, webhook deliveries pause.
3. Implement deletion scheduling by org owner (typed confirmation, step-up, owner transfer prerequisite) or by platform (reason, step-up): 14-day grace, daily reminder emails (3 times), cancellation by owner at any time in grace, immediate effects on traffic only if the domains are removed by the owner first (the wizard warns about traffic impact and offers decommission guidance: revert DNS before deletion).
4. Implement the purge job: after grace, delete domain-scoped data in dependency order (events, bans, rules, DNS records and zones, certificates and keys (secure erase of key material), analytics rollups, API keys, webhooks, invitations, members), anonymize audit references (keep hashed identifiers for the chain), delete user accounts that have no other membership after their own grace, and emit a signed deletion receipt (JSON with counts, no content).
5. Implement DNS zone cool-down interplay (T-0399: apex reserved 24 h) and NS pair release.
6. Implement data export for owners before deletion (T-0130 reuse) and a platform-initiated export for legal requests with `platform_owner` approval and audit.
7. Implement backups and deletion: document that backups age out within the retention period (30 days default) and that restores must re-apply the deletion ledger (a `deletion_ledger` table replayed after any restore; restore drill test T-0435/T-0436 verifies this).
8. Implement abuse-driven immediate suspension path with a post-hoc review queue and a customer appeal contact.
9. Write tests: all transitions including illegal ones, grace cancellation, purge completeness (a table-scanner test asserts zero rows containing the org id across all tables after purge, except the ledger/receipt), key erasure verification, restore + ledger replay, legal hold block, and email timeline.
**Deliverables.**
- lifecycle service, jobs, API, UI flows, receipts, tests, docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: after purge, the scanner test finds zero org-scoped rows except the deletion receipt and ledger.
- A2: deletion cannot start without owner transfer or typed confirmation; platform deletion requires step-up and reason.
- A3: restore from backup replays the ledger and the tenant stays deleted (drill).
- A4: suspended orgs serve S-148 within 2 s and send no origin traffic.
- A5: certificate private keys of deleted tenants are unrecoverable (store scan).
**Tests.**
- Integration with the real database; scanner test across all tables; drill; browser e2e.
**Notes.** AC-42 verifies the lifecycle end to end including data deletion and receipts.

### T-0425 · Global rule packs and rollout (S-107)
`P22` `[UI][API][SEC]` · deps: T-0417, T-0245, T-0261 · size: L · owner: web
**Objective.** Let operators publish, stage, compare and roll back platform rule packs safely.
**Steps.**
1. Implement the pack catalog screen: packs (core SQLi, XSS, traversal, scanner fingerprints, virtual patches, outbound patterns, bot signatures), installed version, available versions, signature status (verified/failed), release notes, rule counts by category and severity.
2. Implement version detail: diff view between versions (added/removed/changed rules with before/after expressions rendered as code with syntax-neutral highlight, no execution), benchmarks (inspect time p50/p99 on the standard corpus), false-positive report from the benign corpus run, and ATK coverage delta.
3. Implement staged rollout: stages (internal canary org(s) → 5% of domains in `monitor` → 25% → 100%), each stage with a minimum dwell time, automatic gates (no increase in false-positive proxies: user-created exceptions rate, auto-rollback triggers), manual approval with step-up, and an abort button; rollout state is stored and visible.
4. Implement rollback (one click, reason, step-up) that restores the previous signed pack through `config_revisions`, with propagation display and the automatic-rollback explanation (C14.8).
5. Implement pack upload for platform-authored packs: signature required (platform signing key; verify at upload), schema validation, dry-run against fixtures, and refusal of unsigned or invalid packs; rule authoring remains a development workflow, not a UI free-text editor (the UI supports enabling/disabling individual rules platform-wide with reasons, and tenant-level exceptions remain in P12).
6. Implement the **canary evaluation**: run the new version in shadow against the last 24 h of sampled request vectors (stored as anonymized vector hashes and feature sets, not raw requests) to estimate block-rate changes before rollout; show the delta by category and top changed rules.
7. Wire alerts: rollout stalled, auto-rollback fired, signature failure, pack older than N days.
8. Write tests: signature verification (valid/invalid/tampered), staged rollout state machine, rollback, diff correctness, permission gating (`platform.rules.publish` with step-up), shadow-evaluation determinism, and propagation tests to the proxy.
**Deliverables.**
- API, screens, rollout engine, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: an unsigned or tampered pack cannot be installed (negative tests).
- A2: staged rollout advances only after dwell and gates and can be aborted at any stage.
- A3: rollback restores the previous version within 2 s of confirmation across proxies.
- A4: the diff view matches the pack's rule files byte-for-byte (property test).
- A5: shadow evaluation produces a deterministic delta for the same input.
**Tests.**
- Integration with proxy snapshots, unit, browser e2e.
**Notes.** Tenants can pin a pack version in Tier 2 (P32); in v5 platform packs apply to all tenants after rollout.

### T-0426 · Threat-intel feeds management (S-108)
`P22` `[UI][API][OPS]` · deps: T-0417, T-0348 · size: M · owner: web
**Objective.** Operate the feeds that populate reputation and blocklists with transparency and bounded risk.
**Steps.**

- API, screen, parsers, tests

- A1: entries covering private ranges, admin CIDRs or the runner are dropped and counted in 100% of fixtures.

### T-0430 · Platform audit (S-117): filters, chain verification and export
`P22` `[UI][API][SEC]` · deps: T-0417, T-0131, T-0147 · size: M · owner: web
**Objective.** Make the platform audit trail searchable, verifiable and exportable without becoming a data leak.
**Steps.**
1. Implement `GET P/audit` with filters (time range, actor, actor role, org, event type from the AUD-* catalog, outcome, resource id, IP /24, reason text contains), cursor pagination and saved filters; results show event, actor, target, outcome, and a diff viewer for before/after (secrets redacted).
2. Implement the **chain verification** UI: shows the last verified position, verification result, and a "Verify now" action (runs `GET P/audit/verify`, which recomputes hashes from a given range, bounded by time); a failure displays the first inconsistent sequence number and raises a critical alert; the verification also compares against the externally stored chain anchors (daily anchor hash written to an append-only file and optionally e-mailed to `platform_owner`).
3. Implement export: `POST P/audit/export` (JSON Lines/CSV), asynchronous with job status, size cap, signed manifest with SHA-256 and chain proof (first/last hash), expiry of the download link (24 h), and audit of the export itself.
4. Implement role-specific views: `platform_auditor` sees all audit but no other admin data; org-level audit events for tenants are visible to platform staff only in redacted form (no member emails, no request details) unless the viewer holds support permission with a reason.
5. Implement retention controls (default 400 days, minimum 180) with monthly partitioning and archival to compressed files with chain continuity (archival does not break verification; archived segments carry their anchors).
6. Implement alerting on suspicious audit patterns: many failed step-ups, impersonation volume, bulk exports, jail removals outside business hours (configurable), changes to never-ban entries, signup policy loosening.
7. Write tests: hash-chain integrity under concurrent writers, tamper detection (modify a row, delete a row, reorder rows) in a test database, export manifest verification, filter correctness, pagination under inserts, retention archival with verification, role-based redaction, and performance (10 million events: filtered query ≤ 500 ms with indexes).
**Deliverables.**
- API, UI, verification tooling (`hddctl audit verify` parity), export job, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: any tampering with a stored audit row is detected by verification (three tamper cases).
- A2: exports are signed (manifest) and verification of an export passes offline with `hddctl audit verify-export`.
- A3: auditor role sees no non-audit admin screens.
- A4: archival keeps verification passing across segments.
- A5: suspicious-pattern alerts fire in the simulation.
**Tests.**
- Integration, tamper tests, performance, browser e2e.
**Notes.** The audit log is itself a sensitive dataset; exports are rate limited and logged.

### T-0435 · Releases and updates (S-123) and backups and restore drills (S-124)

**Objective.** Operate upgrades and backups from the console with verification and rollback built in.

Implement S-123 releases: installed versions per component and node, available versions (from a signed release manifest fetched via the egress client from the pinned release host or imported offline), release notes, signature and SBOM verification results (cosign verification output summary), migration plan (database migrations that will run, reversible or not), and compatibility checks (minimum previous version, config schema changes).
2. Implement the upgrade workflow: pre-flight (health, backups recent, disk space, no active emergency), stage new binaries beside old (`hddctl upgrade --stage`), run migrations with the expand/contract pattern, health checks, atomic switch, automatic rollback on failure, post-upgrade smoke tests; the UI displays the steps and logs live (SSE), requires step-up and a typed confirmation, and refuses unsigned artifacts.

8. Write tests: signature verification (valid/invalid), upgrade state machine with injected failures at each step, automatic rollback, migration reversibility labeling, backup encryption/decryption roundtrip, drill pipeline in CI with a small dataset, ledger replay, permission gating (`platform.release` for owner only, `platform.backup`), and UI flows.

- API, UI, workflows, drill tooling, tests, runbooks

- A1: an unsigned or tampered artifact is refused in the UI and CLI (negative tests).
- A2: an injected failure at each upgrade step triggers automatic rollback to a healthy state (7 failure points tested).
- A3: restore drill reports measured RTO/RPO and verifies audit chain and certificate decryption.
- A4: backups are encrypted and the plaintext secrets scan finds nothing.
- A5: alerts fire for stale backups and drills.
**Tests.**
- Integration with the lab (compose), failure injection, browser e2e.
**Notes.** AC-54 (backups, restore, upgrade, disaster recovery) and AC-33 (signed updates) are completed in P28/P30; the UI here depends on tooling from P30 and ships with simulated manifests in tests only.

Implement lookups: by Ray ID (`GET P/support/ray/{ray}`), by IP (`/ip/{ip}`), by domain name (`/domain/{name}`) and by user email (`/user?email=`), each requiring a `reason` header (min 10 chars) logged in the platform audit and shown to the user in a confirmation dialog ("This lookup will be recorded").
2. Define the result shapes with strict field limits: Ray ID lookup returns the event (time, host, path template, verdict, category, rule ids visible to platform staff only, ban state, appeal state) without bodies or full cookies; IP lookup returns the ban status across orgs (counts, not tenant names unless the viewer has `platform.tenant.read`), global jail membership, reputation summary, recent categories; domain lookup returns state, mode, recent attention items, certificate status, recent blocks summary; user lookup returns membership and security events (reusing T-0420 masks).
3. Implement **timeline assembly**: merge events, bans, appeals, rule changes, and configuration revisions relevant to the lookup into a chronological view with filters and "copy as support note" (text with no sensitive details).
4. Implement a "Why was this blocked?" explanation generator for platform staff: shows the rule ids and scoring components that led to the verdict, the evidence snippet (redacted, ≤ 512 B), and suggested next actions (create tenant exception request, report false positive to rules team, unban); the *visitor-facing* pages remain free of rule names.
5. Implement safe actions from the lookup: create a global unban (via jail screen rules), create an exception proposal for the tenant (message to owners, never auto-applied), open a false-positive ticket (stored locally with a rule id and fixture hash for the rules team to build regression tests).
6. Implement abuse controls: rate limits per staff (60 lookups/h), alerts on bulk lookups, and mandatory second reason for IP lookups of addresses with tenant-specific context.
7. Write tests: reason requirement, redaction, field-limit schema tests, cross-tenant leak tests (support cannot learn tenant names from IP lookup unless permitted), timeline correctness against seeded data, rate limits, and a11y.
**Deliverables.**
- API, UI, explanation generator, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: no lookup works without a reason; every lookup appears in the audit with the reason.
- A2: IP lookup responses contain no tenant identifiers for roles lacking `platform.tenant.read` (schema test).
- A3: the "why blocked" explanation matches the stored verdict components for 100 seeded events.
- A4: the false-positive ticket stores the fixture hash and rule id, with no request content.
- A5: bulk lookup alerts fire in the simulation.
**Tests.**
- Integration, schema, browser e2e.
**Notes.** The explanation view is staff-only; visitors and tenants see only what S-140 and their own event views allow.

### T-0439 · Admin panel security and end-to-end test suite (AC-01 admin isolation, AC-42 operations)
`P22` `[QA][SEC]` · deps: T-0418, T-0419, T-0420, T-0421, T-0422, T-0423, T-0424, T-0425, T-0426, T-0427, T-0428, T-0429, T-0430, T-0431, T-0432, T-0433, T-0434, T-0435, T-0436, T-0437, T-0438 · size: L · owner: qa
**Objective.** Prove the admin plane is isolated, least-privileged, audited and usable.
**Steps.**
1. Generate the **privilege matrix test** from the route registry: for every admin route × each of the 9 roles (4 org, 4 platform, anonymous) × step-up fresh/stale, assert the expected status per B4.2; any route missing from the registry fails the build.
2. Run **horizontal/vertical privilege escalation** tests: org owner session against admin APIs, platform support against mutations, platform admin against staff management, tampered role claims, forged cookies, cross-host cookie replay (app cookie on admin host and vice versa), CSRF on every mutating route, origin/referer checks, and clickjacking.
3. Run the **audit completeness test**: execute every mutation once via the UI and API and assert exactly one audit event with actor, reason (when required), before/after and a valid chain; no mutation without audit (static scan of handlers for the audit macro plus runtime assertion).
4. Run **secret non-disclosure** tests across all admin responses (SMTP password, webhook secrets, API key material, TLS keys, MFA secrets, backup keys).
5. Run **UI end-to-end flows** with a headless browser: bootstrap admin login, tenant suspend/unsuspend with S-148 verification, impersonation start/end with banner, global jail add/remove with propagation, rule pack stage/rollback with signed fixture packs, emergency safe mode with auto-expiry, settings save with secret handling, email template publish with lint failure and success, announcement scheduling, and support lookup.
6. Run accessibility (axe plus keyboard traversal plus zoom/reflow), visual regression in both themes, and performance budgets across all admin screens (LCP lab ≤ 2.0 s, no layout shift above 0.05 on the 1280×800 profile).
7. Run the **abuse simulations**: staff enumeration, bulk lookups, rapid step-up failures, repeated impersonation, mass jail changes; verify alerts and rate limits.
8. Run the **deletion and restore** scenario: delete a tenant, restore from backup in the drill instance, verify the ledger replay keeps it deleted.
9. Record results in the acceptance runner (AC-01 admin part, AC-42), producing evidence with SHA-256.
**Deliverables.**
- test suites, evidence bundle, fixes for findings
**Acceptance.**
- A1: privilege matrix passes with zero unexpected statuses across all routes and roles.
- A2: every mutation is audited exactly once with a valid chain.
- A3: no secret appears in any admin response in the corpus scan.
- A4: all e2e flows pass in both themes; axe reports zero serious/critical issues.
- A5: abuse simulations raise the expected alerts.
**Tests.**
- The suites themselves, run in CI nightly and at gate time.
**Notes.** This suite is part of every later gate's regression set.

## PHASE P23: Analytics and reports (T-0441 to T-0452) · milestone M9 · gate G23

Requirement prefix `ANA`. Goal: turn the raw event and counter streams into trustworthy, fast, privacy-respecting analytics: partitioned storage with retention by partition drop, rollups with documented accuracy, the analytics screens (overview, geo/ASN, top attackers and paths), the event explorer and detail view, the live threat monitor, and reports (data model, deterministic snapshots, PDF pipeline, scheduling, delivery, digests), plus exports and correctness tests with ground truth.

Non-negotiables: every number on screen comes from stored counters or events with a visible "data complete up to" time (R-16); counts for "requests" come from proxy counters (not from events, which exist only for notable requests); rollup math is documented and tested against ground truth; IP addresses are shown according to the org's IP-truncation setting; event bodies are never stored beyond redacted 512-byte evidence snippets; no chart is the only way to read its data (every chart has a table alternative); reports are generated from immutable snapshots so a re-render is reproducible.

Gate G23 passes when: AC-52 (analytics correctness) passes with synthetic ground truth, the live monitor holds its latency and backpressure budgets, reports render identically from snapshots, the PDF output passes the accessibility checks chosen in the ADR, exports are bounded and audited, and all screens meet the UI definition of done.

### T-0441 · Event storage, partition retention and the rollup pipeline v1
`P23` `[DB][DP][API]` · deps: T-0140, T-0368, T-0214 · size: XL · owner: data
**Objective.** Store events and counters so that queries are cheap, retention is a partition drop, and totals reconcile.
**Steps.**
1. Finalize `waf_events` as a monthly-partitioned table with a covering index set: `(site_id, ts desc)`, `(site_id, ip_key, ts desc)`, `(site_id, category, ts desc)`, `(ray_id)` unique per partition plus a global lookup table `ray_index(ray_id, site_id, month)` for O(1) Ray ID resolution, and a trigram index on the normalized path template; confirm RLS policies on every partition (partition creation job copies policies and grants).
2. Implement the partition manager job: creates next-month partitions ahead of time (two months), detaches and drops partitions older than the maximum retention across plans (default 30 days events, 400 days audit, 90 days webhook deliveries), refuses to drop a partition while a legal hold flag exists, and writes an audit event for every drop. No row-by-row deletes on hot partitions.
3. Implement per-plan retention visibility: queries are bounded by `now - plan.event_retention_days` regardless of physical presence; for orgs with shorter retention than the global max, an off-peak batched purge deletes eligible rows from **closed** partitions only (bounded batches of 5,000 with sleep), documented as the only row-level delete.
4. Implement counter ingestion: the proxy flushes per-site per-minute counters (requests by status class, mode, verdict; bytes in/out; blocked by category; challenge issued/solved; rate-limited; origin errors; latency histograms in fixed log-scale buckets) through the queue table `proxy_counter_batches` (insert-only); the worker folds them idempotently into `rollup_minute` using batch ids to prevent double counting.
5. Implement rollups to hour and day by upsert from minute rows; dimensions as in the data model (`all`, `category`, `status_class`, `country`, `asn`, `rule`, `path_group`) with cardinality caps (top 200 keys per bucket plus `other`), `path_group` derived from path templates (never raw paths), and `asn`/`country` from enrichment done at event time.
6. Implement percentile handling: store HDR-style fixed bucket histograms per minute and merge buckets for hour/day (never average percentiles); document the relative error bound (≤ 2%) and show "approximate" labeling on percentile charts.
7. Implement late-data handling (5-minute window), backfill (`xtask rollup backfill --from --to`), reconcile job (sum of minutes equals hour equals day for additive metrics; mismatches raise an alert and are auto-repaired from minutes), and gap detection (a minute with no counter batch while the proxy was up is marked `gap`, never zero).
8. Implement privacy: events store the IP key (v4 /32, v6 /64) or the org's truncated form per setting; analytics rollups hold no IPs; top-IP queries run on events within retention only.
9. Write tests: idempotent folding (replay the same batch 10 times), partition lifecycle on a scratch database, retention bounds, RLS on partitions, reconcile repairs, histogram merge accuracy against exact percentiles on generated data (error ≤ 2%), and a migration-forward/rollback test.
**Deliverables.**
- migrations, partition manager, counter ingestion, rollup jobs, `xtask rollup`, docs `docs/ANALYTICS.md`
**Acceptance.**
- A1: replaying counter batches never changes totals (property test).
- A2: dropping a partition removes data older than retention without long locks (lock time < 50 ms measured).
- A3: hour and day rollups reconcile with minutes exactly for additive metrics.
- A4: percentile merge error ≤ 2% on the reference datasets.
- A5: a proxy outage produces `gap` markers, never zeros.
**Tests.**
- Integration (Postgres), property tests, performance (ingest 5,000 counter rows/s).
**Notes.** Totals come from counters and not from events; `docs/ANALYTICS.md` explains why event counts differ from request counts.

### T-0442 · Analytics API and the analytics overview (S-070)
`P23` `[API][UI]` · deps: T-0441, T-0088, T-0087 · size: L · owner: web
**Objective.** Let owners see traffic, blocked traffic, bandwidth, status classes and latency over any period with fast, honest charts.
**Steps.**
1. Implement `GET D/analytics/overview|timeseries|status|bandwidth|latency` with parameters `from`, `to`, `granularity` (auto selects minute/hour/day by range with documented thresholds), `compare=previous_period`, `tz`; responses include `data_complete_until`, `gaps[]`, `granularity_used` and `approximate: true` for percentiles.
2. Enforce guards: maximum range per granularity (minute ≤ 48 h, hour ≤ 31 d, day ≤ 400 d), RLS, `PERM-analytics.read`, response size caps, and ETag + `Cache-Control: private, max-age=10` on stable ranges.
3. Implement server-side computation with SQL over rollups (no unbounded scans), prepared statements, and a query timeout of 2 s with a clear `ERR-ANALYTICS-002` message.
4. Build S-070 with KPI tiles (requests, blocked, block rate, bandwidth out, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate), a requests-and-blocked time series (SVG renderer with table alternative and pattern fills for color-blind safety), status class stacked chart, bandwidth chart, latency percentile chart with the "approximate" footnote, a period selector (presets and custom range with validation), time zone indicator, comparison toggle, and domain selector (org-wide or per domain).
5. Handle empty/partial states: new domain with no traffic shows the honest empty state with the verification/cutover checklist link; ranges overlapping a gap show hatched regions labeled "no data".
6. Add chart interactions that do not require a mouse: arrow-key navigation among points with a live-region readout, a "view as table" toggle, CSV download of the displayed series.
7. Add performance work: pre-aggregated queries per granularity, covering indexes, and a small in-process cache keyed by (site, range, granularity) with invalidation by rollup watermark.
8. Write tests: API contract tests (OpenAPI), range/granularity selection edge cases (DST boundaries, leap days), comparison math, gap rendering, RLS/BOLA, a11y (axe, keyboard chart navigation), visual regression in both themes, and performance (p95 API latency ≤ 150 ms with 100M rollup rows).
**Deliverables.**
- API, screen, chart configurations, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: displayed totals equal the sum of the underlying rollup rows for random ranges (property test).
- A2: gaps are visible and never plotted as zero.
- A3: every chart has a working table view and CSV export that match its numbers.
- A4: DST and leap-day ranges produce correct buckets in the tested time zones.
- A5: performance budget is met on the reference dataset.
**Tests.**
- Contract, property, browser e2e, performance.
**Notes.** Percentiles are labeled approximate; the bound is stated in the footnote link.

### T-0444 · Top attackers, paths, rules and categories (S-072) with pivots
`P23` `[API][UI]` · deps: T-0441, T-0445 · size: M · owner: web
**Objective.** Answer "who is attacking, what are they hitting, and what stopped them" in one place with one-click pivots.

Implement `GET D/analytics/top/ips|paths|rules|categories|methods|user-agents` over events and rollups: top IPs (event-based within retention, honoring IP truncation), paths (templates), rules (rule ids with names for the owner), categories (matrix groups), user-agent families (hashed raw values, families only), each with counts, trends and sparklines.

### T-0445 · Event explorer and event detail (S-066)
`P23` `[API][UI][DB]` · deps: T-0441, T-0252, T-0253 · size: L · owner: web
**Objective.** Let owners search events, understand a single decision and act on it.

Implement `GET D/events` with keyset pagination and filters: time range, verdict (`blocked|would_block|challenged|rate_limited|allowed_notable|banned`), category/subtype, rule id, severity, hardness (hard/soft), IP or CIDR (respecting truncation), ASN, country, method, status, path template contains, query parameter name, user-agent family, mode, ban state, Ray ID exact, auth endpoint flag, cross-site context flag, `partial_scan`; combine with AND, support NOT for selected fields, and saved views per user.

### T-0446 · Live threat monitor (S-065): SSE event source, backpressure and accessible live regions
`P23` `[UI][API][DP]` · deps: T-0086, T-0445, T-0368 · size: L · owner: web
**Objective.** Provide a real-time view of what the shield is doing that remains usable and honest under load.
**Steps.**
1. Implement the event source: the proxy publishes notable events through the `Bus` trait (`hdd:events:{site}`: Redis streams or pub/sub when hosted, an in-process bounded broadcast in the local profile; capped, e.g., 5,000 entries) in addition to the batch insert; the API exposes `GET D/events/stream` as SSE on the same-origin `/api/v1` mount with RLS, `Last-Event-ID` resume, 15 s heartbeats, and server-side filters (verdict, category, severity); per-user and per-org concurrent stream caps (3 per user, 20 per org).
2. Implement sampling and backpressure: a display rate cap of 20 events/s per stream; excess events are summarized into `skipped` messages ("312 events not shown; use filters"), counts remain exact in the tiles; slow consumers are disconnected with a reconnect hint; the server never buffers unboundedly.
3. Build S-065 per B12.2: top tiles (events/min, blocked/min, active bans, top category), the live table (time, IP key, country, method, path template, category, verdict, mode, ban chip), row click opens the detail drawer, pause/resume with buffered count, filters, "freeze on hover/focus" so rows do not move while the user reads, clear, and a mode banner when the site is in `monitor` ("Would block" labels instead of "Blocked").
4. Implement accessibility: the live region defaults to `aria-live="off"`, with an opt-in "announce critical events" toggle using polite announcements limited to one per 10 s; keyboard shortcuts for pause, filter focus and row navigation; reduced-motion respected; contrast checked for all verdict chips (text + icon + color).
5. Implement the fallback path: if SSE fails twice, switch to HTMX polling every 5 s with a visible "Polling" indicator; offline detection shows a stale banner.
6. Implement the attack-mode overlay: when the event rate exceeds a threshold, show a banner summarizing the dominant category and suggested actions (links), and avoid DOM thrash by batching DOM updates per animation frame.
7. Add security: events rendered via safe templates, evidence not shown in the live table (details only on click), CSP-compatible island with no inline handlers, per-stream authorization re-checked on every reconnect.
8. Write tests: SSE reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` (no duplicates, no loss within the stream cap), backpressure behavior with a slow client, 5,000 events/s injection (UI remains responsive, memory bounded), filter correctness, polling fallback, a11y live-region behavior with a screen-reader smoke script, and cross-tenant isolation (stream of org A never delivers org B events).
**Deliverables.**
- stream endpoint, island, screen, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: at 5,000 events/s injected the server memory stays bounded and the UI shows exact counts with a sampled table.
- A2: resume after disconnect delivers missed events within the stream cap without duplicates.
- A3: org isolation holds under adversarial stream subscription attempts (BOLA tests).
- A4: the live region does not announce by default and critical announcements are rate limited.
- A5: reduced-motion and keyboard-only operation pass.
**Tests.**
- Integration, load (lab), browser e2e, a11y.
**Notes.** The monitor is a convenience view; the authoritative record is the event store.

### T-0447 · Report data model, section library and generated runs (S-073)
`P23` `[DB][API][UI]` · deps: T-0441, T-0442, T-0444 · size: L · owner: data
**Objective.** Define reports as reproducible snapshots of defined sections, independent of output format.
**Steps.**
1. Create the report schema: `report_templates` (system-defined and org-defined), `report_schedules`, `report_runs` (status, period, domain scope, snapshot hash, output artifacts), `report_artifacts` (HTML, PDF, CSV, JSON; storage path; size; SHA-256; expires_at), with RLS and retention (default 12 months for snapshots, 90 days for artifacts).
2. Define the **section library** with versioned section types: Executive summary, Traffic overview, Attack summary (categories, trends), Top attackers (with IP truncation honored), Bans and appeals, Rule and exception changes (from audit), DNS and TLS health (certificates, expiries, DNS changes), Origin protection status (lockdown state, readiness score), Vulnerability exposure summary (when P27 data exists; otherwise the section reports "not configured"), Operational notes (free text by the author), Data completeness (gaps, partial scans, truncated bodies counts).
3. Implement the **snapshot builder**: given (org, domains, period, sections, locale, time zone) it queries the analytics layer within a single consistent read (repeatable-read transaction) and produces an immutable JSON snapshot with a schema version and hash; all renderers consume only the snapshot; re-rendering never re-queries live data.
4. Provide system templates: Weekly summary, Monthly security review, Incident report (period around an event cluster, includes timeline), DNS/TLS health, Exposure and patch status; org-defined templates cloned from them with section selection and ordering.
5. Build S-073: template gallery, generated runs table (period, domains, status, size, generated by/at), run detail (preview of the HTML rendering, downloads, share link management with expiring signed URLs and optional password disabled by default), delete run, and permission gating (`PERM-report.read/write`).
6. Implement the honest-language rules in sections (claims-lint for generated text): "Detected N requests matching attack patterns; N were blocked in block mode" and statements of limits ("Signature-based detection may miss novel attacks"); never "prevented all attacks".
7. Implement the **completeness block**: every report lists known data gaps and the percentage of requests whose bodies were only partially inspected during the period.
8. Write tests: snapshot determinism (same inputs → same hash), renderer purity (renderers do no I/O), consistency between snapshot totals and analytics API totals, section versioning migrations (old snapshots still render), RLS/BOLA on runs and artifacts, signed link expiry, and claims-lint over all generated strings.
**Deliverables.**
- schema, snapshot builder, section library, S-073, tests, docs
**Acceptance.**
- A1: re-rendering a stored snapshot after data changes yields byte-identical HTML (golden test).
- A2: snapshot totals equal analytics API totals for the same period.
- A3: a report generated for an org never contains data from another org (BOLA tests over all sections).
- A4: shared links expire and are revocable.
- A5: claims-lint passes for all templates and locales.
**Tests.**
- Unit, golden, integration, security.
**Notes.** The PDF pipeline (T-0448) is one renderer of the snapshot; the HTML renderer is canonical.

### T-0448 · PDF pipeline decision, report builder and scheduling (S-074)
`P23` `[API][UI][OPS][DOC]` · deps: T-0447, T-0109, T-0110 · size: XL · owner: data
**Objective.** Produce accessible, deterministic PDF reports and deliver them on schedule.
**Steps.**
1. Run the PDF path **ADR**: candidates (a) headless Chromium print-to-PDF via `chromiumoxide` reusing the HTML renderer and design tokens, executed in a sandboxed worker (no network, read-only filesystem, dedicated user, seccomp, memory/time limits), (b) a Rust-native typesetting approach (for example the `typst` library or `printpdf`/`genpdf`) with dedicated templates, (c) delegating to an external service (rejected by default, violates the data-sovereignty goal). Criteria: fidelity with the design system, **tagged PDF / PDF/UA** capability, font embedding and licensing, determinism (same snapshot → same bytes modulo timestamp), memory and time per 30-page report, attack surface of the renderer, dependency footprint. Record measured results and the decision.
2. Implement the chosen pipeline as an isolated worker task with a strict contract: input = snapshot JSON + template id; output = PDF bytes; resource limits (60 s, 512 MiB, 50 MB output); no network egress (enforced by namespace or by the HTML renderer using only embedded assets); failure leaves no partial artifact.
3. Embed fonts and the logo, set document metadata (title, language, author = org), bookmarks and a table of contents, tagged structure (headings, tables with headers, figure alt text from the chart descriptions), and a fixed A4/Letter selection by locale.
4. Render charts in reports as static SVG with accompanying data tables; ensure the table appears in the PDF for each chart (accessibility) and that colors have pattern differentiation in grayscale printing.
5. Build S-074 (report builder and schedule): choose template, period (last 7/30 days, calendar month, custom), domains, sections and order, locale/time zone, recipients (org members and external addresses with confirmation emails to external recipients before the first delivery), format (PDF, HTML, CSV bundle), schedule (weekly/monthly/custom cron with time zone, next-run preview), delivery (email with a signed expiring link by default; attachment option ≤ 10 MB), and a **live preview** rendered from a snapshot of current data.
6. Implement the scheduler in `hdd-worker`: next-run computation with DST correctness, missed-run catch-up policy (run once on recovery), concurrency limits, retry/backoff, failure notifications to the schedule owner, per-plan limits via `QuotaGuard`, and pause/resume.
7. Implement delivery safety: external recipients must confirm opt-in; unsubscribe links in emails; delivery logs; bounce handling (suppression via `hdd-mailer`).
8. Implement PDF accessibility validation in CI using an oracle (veraPDF PDF/UA profile or `pdfua` checker; UNVERIFIED(`oracle_unavailable`) if absent) and visual diff of the first pages against goldens.
9. Write tests: pipeline limits (oversized input, hostile text, huge tables, RTL strings), isolation (no network access attempt succeeds in the sandbox), determinism, schedule math (DST transitions, month ends, leap years), delivery confirmation flow, and permission checks.
**Deliverables.**
- ADR, PDF worker, S-074, scheduler, validation tooling, tests
**Acceptance.**
- A1: the same snapshot renders to identical PDF content streams across two runs (metadata timestamps excluded).
- A2: the sandboxed renderer cannot open network connections (test attempts DNS and TCP and fails).
- A3: PDF passes the chosen accessibility validator or the gap list is documented as UNVERIFIED with reason.
- A4: schedules fire at the correct local times across two DST transitions in tests.
- A5: external recipients receive nothing until they confirm.
**Tests.**
- Unit, integration, sandbox tests, golden visual diffs.
**Notes.** The ADR slot referenced from P00 (PDF path) is settled here.

### T-0450 · Data export and portability (events, analytics, configuration)
`P23` `[API][SEC][OPS]` · deps: T-0445, T-0447, T-0130 · size: M · owner: api
**Objective.** Let owners take their data out safely, within limits, with audit and no accidental leaks.

<!-- PHASE:P24 -->
## PHASE P24: Notifications, integrations, public API and SDK (T-0453 to T-0462) · milestone M9 · gate G24

Requirement prefix `NTF`. Goal: make HDD tell people what matters, where they already work, and make everything scriptable: the alert-rule engine and routing, integration channels, a reliable webhook delivery engine with signing, the complete public API v1 with governance, a Rust SDK and generated clients, developer documentation, and log forwarding to SIEM tools.

Non-negotiables: alerts are deduplicated and rate limited so an attack cannot flood owners' channels (alert-flood control is a security feature); every outbound call uses the central egress client with the SSRF guard; secrets for channels are write-only and encrypted; webhook payloads and notifications never contain request bodies, cookies, credentials or full IPs beyond the org's truncation setting; the public API is versioned with a deprecation policy, and the OpenAPI document is the single source of truth for the API reference, SDK and contract tests.

Gate G24 passes when: alert rules route correctly with dedupe, quiet hours and escalation; all channel integrations pass contract tests against local fakes (and live smoke tests where the operator supplied test destinations); webhooks are signed, retried and idempotent; the API contract tests and breaking-change detector pass; the SDK passes its integration tests; and AC-45 passes.

### T-0453 · Alert rules (S-076) and notification routing core
`P24` `[API][DB][UI]` · deps: T-0141, T-0368, T-0441 · size: XL · owner: api
**Objective.** Turn platform events into the right notifications with controlled volume.
**Steps.**
1. Define the **trigger catalog** (each with a stable key, default severity, parameters and the event source): `sqli_hard_hit_auth_endpoint`, `possible_auth_bypass` (V13), `data_leak_detected`, `exposure_detected`, `mass_ban` / `ban_spike`, `campaign_detected`, `never_ban_attack_attempt`, `global_jail_promoted`, `rate_limit_spike`, `challenge_failure_spike`, `origin_down` / `origin_degraded`, `certificate_expiring`, `certificate_issue_failed`, `dns_secondary_lag`, `domain_verification_failed`, `readiness_score_drop`, `rule_pack_rollback`, `safe_mode_enabled`, `appeal_received`, `member_added`/`role_changed`, `api_key_created`, `login_anomaly`, `shield_state_change`, `vuln_sla_overdue`, `virtual_patch_expiring`, `report_failed`, `backup_stale` (platform).
2. Implement the **rule model**: scope (org/domain/all domains), trigger, parameters (threshold, window, minimum severity, category filter), channels (list), schedule (always, business hours, custom), quiet hours with critical override, grouping key, cooldown, and escalation policy (if not acknowledged in X minutes, notify an escalation channel). System-default rules are seeded per org on creation (conservative set, editable, deletable with warnings) so a new org has alerts without configuration.
3. Implement the **routing pipeline** in `hdd-notify`: consumes domain events from the outbox, evaluates rules (windowed counting using Redis with a database fallback), creates durable notifications (S-075) and enqueues channel deliveries; delivery records are idempotent per (rule, event group, channel).
4. Implement **flood control**: per-rule cooldown, per-channel rate caps (default 10/h for chat channels, 60/h for email), grouping ("12 SQLi attempts from 3 IPs in 5 minutes" as one notification with a count that updates until the group closes), digest mode when caps are hit with a final "N more events suppressed" message, and a global per-org cap with an alert to the owner by email that suppression occurred.
5. Implement acknowledgment and snooze: acknowledge via UI/API/button links in messages (signed single-use links with expiry), snooze a rule or trigger for N hours with a reason, escalate on no acknowledgment, and mark resolved when the source condition clears (for state-based triggers).
6. Build S-076: rule list with search and status, rule editor with plain-language preview ("When 5 or more hard SQL injection attempts hit your login endpoints within 10 minutes, email Alex and post to #security"), threshold sanity hints, a **test event** button that generates a synthetic notification clearly labeled "Test", and a channel health indicator (last success/failure).
7. Respect user preferences (S-087): per-user notification channels and per-severity opt-outs, with enforced minimums for security-critical account notifications.
8. Implement the API (`/alert-rules`, `/notifications`, `POST /notifications/{id}:ack`), permissions (`PERM-alertrule.write`, `PERM-notify.read`), audit events, and metrics (notifications created, suppressed, delivered, failed by channel).
9. Write tests: trigger evaluation with time-injected windows, grouping and cooldown properties, flood simulation (10,000 events → bounded notifications), quiet hours and critical override, escalation flows, idempotency under retries and crashes, RLS/BOLA, and UI e2e for the editor.
**Deliverables.**
- trigger catalog, rule engine, routing, S-076, API, tests, docs `docs/ALERTS.md`
**Acceptance.**
- A1: a simulated SQLi campaign of 10,000 events produces a bounded number of notifications per channel (caps respected) with the suppression summary.
- A2: seeded default rules exist for a new org and can be edited or removed.
- A3: escalation triggers exactly once when unacknowledged and stops upon acknowledgment.
- A4: notification creation is idempotent across worker restarts (crash test).
- A5: the editor preview text matches the evaluated behavior (golden tests).
**Tests.**
- Unit, property, integration with Redis/Postgres, browser e2e.
**Notes.** Message content rules are enforced here (no sensitive data) and re-verified by T-0454.

### T-0454 · Integration channels (S-077): email, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, PagerDuty
`P24` `[API][UI][SEC]` · deps: T-0453, T-0109, T-0413 · size: L · owner: api
**Objective.** Deliver notifications to the tools teams already use, safely.
**Steps.**
1. Implement a `Channel` trait (`validate_config`, `send`, `test`, `classify_error`) and the concrete channels: Email (through `hdd-mailer` with per-user and shared inboxes), Slack (incoming webhook URL and optional bot token variant), Discord (webhook), Telegram (bot token + chat id), Microsoft Teams (incoming webhook / workflow webhook), PagerDuty (Events API v2 routing key with dedup keys mapped to alert groups, resolve events on clear).
2. Implement configuration forms in S-077 per channel with inline help (where to find the URL/token), secret fields write-only (stored via envelope encryption, fingerprint display), URL validation (https only; hostnames must match the provider allowlist for hosted providers, for example `hooks.slack.com`, `discord.com/api/webhooks`, `api.telegram.org`, `events.pagerduty.com`, `*.webhook.office.com`/`*.logic.azure.com`; generic hosts are not allowed here), and an egress allowlist/SSRF check at save and send time.
3. Implement message formatting from a shared message model (title, severity, summary, key facts, link to the HDD screen, Ray ID or group id) rendered per channel with length limits, markdown/escaping rules specific to each platform (escape user-influenced strings such as hostnames and paths; mention-injection prevention for `@channel`/`@everyone`/`<!here>` on Slack and Discord), accessible plain text fallback, and **content policy**: only fields from the allowlist (`event_type`, `domain`, `category`, `count`, `window`, `ip` per org truncation, `ray_id`, `link`); nothing from request bodies or evidence snippets.

6. Implement per-integration quotas (plan-based), ownership (org-level vs user-level), and the permission model (`PERM-integration.write` for owner/admin).
7. Implement rotation helpers (replace secret, test, then save) and the "disconnect" action that deletes secrets immediately.
8. Write tests with local fake servers implementing each provider's documented API shape (contract-tested against saved examples from provider docs; mark UNVERIFIED(`capability_not_supplied`) for live smoke tests unless the operator provides test destinations): formatting golden tests, escaping and mention-injection fuzz, retry/circuit-breaker behavior, SSRF attempts through the URL field (≥ 40 vectors), secret leakage greps in logs/errors, and UI e2e.
