### E2.4 Generators that extend the seeds to the minimum counts

`xtask fixtures benign --generate` is deterministic (seed `0xbe91`) and composes entries from templates and vocabularies, never copying from attack fixtures:

| Generator | Template | Vocabulary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| names | `{given} {prefix}'{surname}` | 200 given names, prefixes O/D/L/N/Mc/Mac/St, 300 surnames, 40 languages |
| possessives | `{brand}'s {product}`, `{people}' {thing}` | 400 brands and products (synthetic), 80 nouns |
| elision | `l'{word}`, `d'{word}`, `dell'{word}`, `all'{word}`, `qu'{word}` | FR/IT/ES/PT word lists |
| measure | `{n}' {m}"` and `{n}"x{m}'` | numbers 1 to 20 |
| sql-words | `{lead} {kw} {tail}` where kw is one of SELECT, DROP, UPDATE, INSERT, DELETE, UNION, ORDER, GROUP, LIMIT, WHERE, HAVING, EXEC, ALTER, CREATE, TABLE, FROM, JOIN | 120 leads and tails of natural English; constraint: no quote followed by SQL structure |
| questions | `How do I {verb} {thing} in {db}?` | 50 verbs, 80 things, 8 databases |
| errors | `{engine} says: {message}` | 20 real-looking error messages quoted by users |
| dashes | `{phrase} -- {phrase}` and `{phrase}--{phrase}` | 100 phrases |
| math | `{a} = {b}`, `{a}' = {b}`, `{a} < {b} and {c} > {d}` | numbers and variables |
| search | `{adj} {product} under {n} dollars` | terms; includes OR/AND/NOT as English words |
| recipes | `{n} cup or {m} cups of {ingredient}` | 60 ingredients |
| addresses | `{n} {street}, {city}` | street types and cities (synthetic) |
| urls | `/{section}/{slug}?{k}={v}&{k2}={v2}` | apostrophes percent-encoded as %27 in values |
| json | `{"{key}": "{text}"}` with SQL-ish keys | keys: order, group, select, limit, offset, where, having, union |
| html | Allowed-tag rich text snippets | 20 tags, 30 attributes (benign) |

### E2.5 Near-miss report and corpus governance

1. Every gate run writes `reports/near-miss-<ts>.md`: entries with soft score ≥ 1, grouped by rule and field kind, with the rule's contribution, to guide weight tuning.
2. Real-world false-positive reports (S-060, S-066) can be exported as scrubbed corpus candidates (`xtask fixtures benign --add-from-report`), which require a reviewer note and provenance; accepted entries are added to the corpus and become permanent regression tests.
3. The **meta-test** adds a deliberately over-broad rule (for example any single quote) and requires the gate to fail; a gate that cannot fail is broken.
4. The corpus and the attack fixtures share **no** generator code paths, and a test ensures no line appears in both (set intersection must be empty); ambiguous lines are listed in `ambiguous.txt` with expected behavior per preset.

---
<!-- PART:E3 -->
## E3. Acceptance matrix (AC-00 to AC-62)

### E3.1 Rules common to every check

1. **Status taxonomy:** `PASS`, `FAIL(reason)`, `UNVERIFIED(reason_code)` with the closed reason set `capability_not_supplied`, `human_step_pending`, `environment_unsupported`, `oracle_unavailable`, `tool_unavailable`, `stage_not_reached`, `stage_forbids`, `skipped_by_operator`. No other status exists. A PASS needs at least one evidence artifact with SHA-256.
2. **Real-IP handling:** no `X-Forwarded-For` spoofing and no trusted test subnet; the runner uses its real IP. Tests needing several sources use `vantage_points` from the profile; otherwise they run sequentially with an unban between each, and the report states the vantage count used.
3. **Block assertions verify two things:** the 403 (or branded block page) with a Ray ID **and** a matching event record (category, client IP key, `ray_id`) via the events API, so jail blocks are never mistaken for detections.
4. **Inspect-first gate** (section 2.2) precedes every live attack-shaped payload; payload classes A/B/C are enforced by the connector; lab-mode checks target only Vuln-Lab addresses.
5. **Rate profiles** (section 2.3) and the kill switch apply to every check; checks can choose a lower profile but never a higher one.
6. **Stages:** `pilot` allows destructive checks with warning; `production` refuses them without the operator's approval of that specific run; after cutover only the non-destructive regression subset runs by default (AC-00, AC-03, AC-05, AC-20, AC-22, AC-35 login-only, sandbox-only checks).
7. **Failure budget:** three attempts per check (R-14); a check that passes only on retry is `Pass (flaky)` and is not release evidence until diagnosed.
8. **Catalog parity:** the typed catalog in `hdd-acceptance` and this appendix are compared by a CI test; adding a check means editing both in one change.

### E3.2 Suite tiers

| Tier | Contents | Where it may run | Typical duration |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `smoke` | AC-00, AC-05 (canary subset), AC-22 | pilot, production | < 5 min |
| `nondestructive` | smoke plus AC-03, AC-20, AC-01 login checks, AC-35 login-only, sandbox-only checks | pilot, production | < 30 min |
| `pilot-full` | nondestructive plus AC-02, AC-04 staging, AC-06 to AC-18, AC-21, AC-23, AC-34, AC-37, AC-45, AC-54 drills (bans use 60 s TTL; resilience announced) | pilot only | hours |
| `lab-full` | AC-26, AC-28, AC-29, AC-38, AC-39, AC-44, AC-48 oracle portions, AC-27 drill, floods in the closed lab | lab only | hours (nightly) |
| `local` | AC-55 plus every unit, integration and browser test, `profile-parity`, and `hdd-local selftest`; no live DNS, no kernel enforcement, no ACME | any supported builder (Windows, macOS, Linux) and the CI matrix | < 30 min |
| `release` | everything required for release gates: all tiers plus AC-24 (announced), AC-33, AC-40, AC-41, AC-55 to AC-58 and the manual evidence items | pilot + lab + the CI OS matrix | a day |

| P25 to P27 | AC-26, AC-27 (prep), AC-29, AC-30, AC-31, AC-32 |
| P28 | AC-38, AC-39, AC-15 (full), AC-19, AC-35, AC-36, AC-37, AC-40, AC-41, AC-43, AC-46, AC-48, AC-49, AC-50, AC-51 and a dry run of every ID |

### E3.4 Evidence record schema

```json
{ "check": "AC-39", "attempt": 1, "status": "PASS", "started": "2026-10-17T10:00:00Z", "finished": "2026-10-17T10:41:12Z",
  "environment": {"mode":"lab","stage":"pilot","commit":"<git sha>","kernel":"<uname -r>","tools":{"sqlmap":"1.8.x"}},
  "commands": ["xtask acceptance --only AC-39 --mode lab"],
  "artifacts": [{"path":"evidence/AC-39/matrix.csv","sha256":"<hex>","bytes":123456}],
  "assertions": [{"id":"A1","text":"100% would_block for M1-M6 x vectors","result":"pass","observed":"1944/1944"}],
  "unverified": null }
```

### E3.5 The checks

#### AC-00 · Preflight and safety-envelope self-tests

- **Area / first live:** Foundation · P11 (T-0217); self-tests T-0492 (P28)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0010, T-0217, T-0492
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** smoke · live + lab · read-only (self-tests send refused traffic only)
- **Procedure:** `hddctl preflight` validates the profile and environment; the self-test suite proves the guard rails (allowlists, class gating, rate ceilings, kill switch, runner-IP guard, stage refusals, oracle launcher refusal).
- **PASS when:**
  - Profile validates against schema_version 5; required fields present; `min_resources` met; kernel features and XDP mode recorded
  - Required ports reachable and no conflicts on 53/80/443; pilot NS and A records resolve to the VPS from the runner's resolver and two named public resolvers
  - Runner IP is not in `admin_cidrs` and is in the never-ban list; provider AUP confirmation recorded
  - Canary reachable directly while `lockdown_state=pending` and via HDD afterwards; DB/Redis authenticated; secret files 0600; clocks sane; `egress_allowlist` covers feeds and CA
  - Every refusal test shows zero packets sent to the forbidden destination (socket recorder)
- **Evidence:** preflight report, self-test report, socket-recorder logs
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `human_step_pending` (provider AUP, delegation not yet done), `capability_not_supplied` (lab for oracle refusal tests)

#### AC-01 · Authentication and admin isolation

- **Area / first live:** Security · P06 gate (T-0136); admin T-0439; full T-0503
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0125, T-0128, T-0134, T-0136, T-0417, T-0439, T-0503
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** nondestructive (login checks); pilot-full · live + lab · read-only plus authenticated requests
- **Procedure:** Verify unauthenticated and wrong-role access paths for every surface and API route; verify admin exposure mode and that data stores and SSH are not reachable from forbidden sources.
- **PASS when:**
  - Unauthenticated and bad-key requests receive 401; viewer cannot mutate; platform roles require MFA with enrollment forced at first login
  - Admin surface unreachable from non-allowlisted IPs (`routed_with_cidr`) or absent on the public interface (`tunnel_only`); cross-surface cookie replay fails
  - Port 22 reachable only from `ssh_allow_cidrs`; Postgres/Redis/metrics ports absent in a capped self-scan of the operator's own VPS
  - HDD's own login and signup block and ban the six mandated payloads (runner protected via second source)
  - Generated privilege matrix passes with zero unexpected statuses across all routes and roles
- **Evidence:** route-permission matrix output, scan output, event records
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `human_step_pending` (tunnel not set up), `capability_not_supplied` (second source for ban test)

#### AC-02 · Zone import and parity

- **Area / first live:** DNS · P08/P09 (T-0157, T-0184); full T-0507
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0157, T-0158, T-0184, T-0507
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live + lab · read-only (zone exports, lookups)
- **Procedure:** Import an existing zone (zone file, provider export, AXFR where permitted) and compare every record with the source provider's answers.
- **PASS when:**
  - `parity-check` shows every record identical to the source except intentionally proxied names
  - Unsupported and provider-proprietary types listed and acknowledged; parity FAILS until each is acknowledged
  - `export-zone` backup exists and re-imports to an identical zone (byte-stable canonical form)
  - Differential check: HDD DNS answers equal a reference implementation loaded with the source zone for every supported record
- **Evidence:** parity report, export hash, differential results
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied` (operator zone copy), `human_step_pending`

#### AC-03 · Authoritative DNS (real path)

- **Area / first live:** DNS · P11 basic (T-0218); full T-0402
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0207, T-0218, T-0389 to T-0396, T-0401, T-0402
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** nondestructive · live · read-only queries within functional/burst profiles
- **Procedure:** Per topology: query the VPS directly (or, in `hidden_primary`, the secondary and observe refusals from other sources) over UDP and TCP, then via at least two public recursive resolvers once delegated.
- **PASS when:**
  - Proxied names return only HDD IPs (never origin IP, no origin-derived AAAA, no origin hints in HTTPS/SVCB); grey names return stored values
  - NS/SOA correct; NXDOMAIN with SOA; NODATA; foreign zone REFUSED; public AXFR refused; `ANY` minimal; EDNS payload capped at 1232
  - Proxied toggle visible within 2 s (self-authoritative); capped burst engages RRL; `dig +trace` from the runner succeeds
  - hickory-client suite and differential tests pass; `delv` reports the zone insecure (no DNSSEC claim)
- **Evidence:** query transcripts (hex), tool versions, propagation timeline
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `human_step_pending` (delegation), `oracle_unavailable`

#### AC-04 · Real TLS and certificates

- **Area / first live:** TLS · P11 staging (T-0218); full T-0385; production T-0538
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0209, T-0218, T-0375 to T-0385, T-0538
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live · issuance on staging CA; production once with approval
- **Procedure:** Issue staging certificates via HTTP-01 and DNS-01 wildcard; verify TLS policy via oracles; force a short-window renewal; observe CT; after the operator's approval perform one production issuance.
- **PASS when:**
  - Staging cert for `test_hostname` via HTTP-01 and DNS-01 wildcard on the pilot zone validate against the staging root
  - TLS 1.2 or higher only; h2 negotiated; unknown and absent SNI refused; HSTS/redirect correct
  - Forced renewal on staging succeeds and the proxy serves the new cert within 2 s; CT entry observed
  - Apex certificate obtainable through CNAME-delegated `_acme-challenge`; production issuance validated by a public trust store
- **Evidence:** ACME logs (redacted), certificate chains, `testssl.sh` output, CT observations
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `human_step_pending` (CNAME delegation, production approval), `capability_not_supplied` (CT service)

#### AC-05 · Legitimate traffic and pass-through fidelity

- **Area / first live:** Proxy · P11 canary subset (T-0218); headers T-0415; regression T-0506
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0208, T-0210, T-0361, T-0410, T-0415, T-0506
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** smoke · live · read-only
- **Procedure:** Fetch declared-static assets and the canary through HDD and compare with the direct-origin baseline; verify header fidelity and policy.
- **PASS when:**
  - Static assets and canary: identical status and SHA-256 versus the baseline; dynamic pages: same status, content type and structural digest
  - `Server: Hack-Dev-Defence` present; origin `Server`/`X-Powered-By` absent; security headers and `HDD-Ray-ID` present
  - Origin-side `X-Forwarded-For`/`HDD-Connecting-IP`/secret header verified via canary echo or `origin_access_log`
  - Range, compression, redirects, HEAD/304, WebSocket/gRPC smoke behave as the origin
- **Evidence:** hash comparisons, header dumps
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied` (canary not installed and no access log)

#### AC-06 · False-positive baseline

- **Area / first live:** Detection · P13 (T-0255); P28 (T-0508)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0255, T-0279, T-0508
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live + lab · read-only (benign replay)
- **Procedure:** Replay the scrubbed HAR (GET/HEAD unless allowlisted), the authorized rate-limited crawl and the benign corpora (E2) through `monitor` and then `block` mode, inbound and outbound.
- **PASS when:**
  - Zero `would_block` and zero blocks on all benign corpora at Balanced, Strict and Shield Balanced (paranoia 1 and 2)
  - Held-out benign set reported separately
  - Any hit is investigated and the rules fixed (never the corpus); HAR cookies/tokens stripped before any file is written
- **Evidence:** replay logs, near-miss report
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied` (no HAR/crawl supplied; corpora still run)

#### AC-07 · Detection matrix

- **Area / first live:** Detection · P13/P14 (T-0283); P28 (T-0508)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0260, T-0283, T-0313, T-0508
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live + lab · Class A live, B on sandbox, C inspect API only
- **Procedure:** Run the fixture families (E1) across vectors via the inspect API, live Class A shapes, and a live enforcement subset in `block` mode (one payload per category and vector, unban between).
- **PASS when:**
  - Core set (M1 to M6 plus variants and the evasion catalog) 100% `would_block` with the right category
  - Held-out and public-corpus sets: detection at least 95% for hard families; false positives at most 0.1% on public benign corpora
  - Live subset: 403 with Ray ID and matching event; follow-up from the same IP receives the jail response
  - Per-ATK status table generated (no ATK id without a fixture and a status)
- **Evidence:** matrix CSV, coverage table, event cross-checks
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `stage_forbids` (production), `capability_not_supplied` (no sandbox)

#### AC-08 · Ban persistence, enforcement and unban

- **Area / first live:** Bans · P16 (T-0330); kernel T-0471; full T-0500
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0316 to T-0322, T-0330, T-0464, T-0471, T-0500
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live + lab · 60 s test bans; runner protected unless second source
- **Procedure:** Attack from a test source; verify L7 jail, Redis, Postgres and kernel set; restart components; unban.
- **PASS when:**
  - Attack gives 403 plus event; harmless follow-up from the same IP gives 403 `ip_jail`; ban appears in the API, Redis and Postgres
  - Ports 80/443 dropped in the kernel set while SSH and DNS from the same IP still work
  - `DELETE` unbans and the IP is served again within 2 s; deleting a non-banned IP gives 404
  - Ban survives proxy restart, Redis flush and Postgres restart; IPv6 /64 behavior tested where IPv6 exists
- **Evidence:** ban records, kernel set dumps, timing histograms
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `environment_unsupported` (no nftables), `capability_not_supplied` (no IPv6)

#### AC-09 · Other attack classes (XSS, LFI, RCE, XXE, SSRF-parameter, CRLF, deserialization, upload, honeypots)

- **Area / first live:** Detection · P15 (T-0314); P28 (T-0508)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0285 to T-0314, T-0508
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live + lab · A/B/C per fixture
- **Procedure:** Run families AG-02 to AG-07 and AG-15 from the attack matrix via inspect API, sandbox and the Vuln-Lab.
- **PASS when:**
  - Each category blocked with an event; honeypot hits ban outside cross-site context
  - `/wp-admin` is not a trap when `site.platform=wordpress`
  - Benign twins of each family pass
- **Evidence:** per-ATK table, events
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied`

#### AC-10 · Outbound leak control

- **Area / first live:** Outbound · P21 (T-0415)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0408, T-0409, T-0415
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live + lab · canary file only
- **Procedure:** Fetch the canary `leak.txt` through HDD in `monitor` and `block` modes; run lab leak fixtures including binary and streaming negatives.
- **PASS when:**
  - `block`: masked 500, leaked string absent from body and headers, `critical data_leak` event; `monitor`: recorded and passed
  - Path exclusion works; body larger than the scan window is tagged `partial_scan`
  - Binary, streaming, Range, HEAD and 304 responses are byte-identical to the origin
  - Benign outbound corpus (500 pages) produces zero blocks
- **Evidence:** responses, events, differential hashes
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied` (canary not installed; lab evidence reported separately)

#### AC-11 · Rate limiting

- **Area / first live:** Behavior · P17 (T-0351); full T-0501
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0333 to T-0336, T-0351, T-0501
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live (burst) + lab · burst profile
- **Procedure:** One capped burst (up to 100 requests to the canary) and lab load for accuracy and fairness.
- **PASS when:**
  - 429 with `Retry-After`, then auto-ban per policy; recovery after TTL; legitimate visitors unaffected
  - Counter-algorithm limits within ±5% of the reference implementation and exactly correct on authentication endpoints (exact algorithm, T-0333); store-down local fallback works; per-tenant fairness holds
- **Evidence:** burst logs, accuracy table
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied` (second vantage point)

#### AC-12 · Dynamic rules and dry-run

- **Area / first live:** Policy · P12 (T-0229); P28 (T-0505)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0228, T-0229, T-0234, T-0237, T-0505
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live · sandbox site changes via normal API
- **Procedure:** Add and remove path, CIDR and allow rules; run dry-run against the baseline.
- **PASS when:**
  - Rules effective within 2 s without restart; invalid, oversized or unsupported regex rejected with 422
  - Dry-run reports false positives on the baseline; revisions created and rollback restores behavior
- **Evidence:** revision list, timings
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** none

#### AC-13 · Modes, safe mode and automatic rollback

- **Area / first live:** Policy · P18 (T-0374); P28 (T-0505)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0370, T-0371, T-0374, T-0434, T-0505
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live (sandbox site) · Class A
- **Procedure:** Exercise `off`, `monitor`, `log`, `block`, safe mode and the auto-rollback triggers.
- **PASS when:**
  - `monitor/log` record but pass; `off` skips; safe mode lets the same attack through with TLS/routing intact and exiting restores blocking
  - An induced bad rule that blocks a known-good probe is reverted automatically with an alert (`rollback.min_distinct_ips=1` on the sandbox site)
  - Site-wide 403/5xx spikes from one IP never trigger rollback
- **Evidence:** mode transition logs, rollback events
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** none

#### AC-14 · Protocol hardening

- **Area / first live:** Proxy · P18 (T-0373)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0353 to T-0360, T-0373
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live (sandbox only) · protocol-abuse profile
- **Procedure:** Run the PRO catalog (E1.7) with raw sockets and h2 builders against `sandbox_hostname`; cross-check with `h2spec` where available.
- **PASS when:**
  - CL/TE and obs-fold/absolute-form/CRLF anomalies rejected; oversized header/body give 431/413; slowloris cut off
  - gzip/brotli bombs rejected by ratio cap; h2 Rapid Reset, CONTINUATION, HPACK, SETTINGS/PING floods contained with the process healthy
  - h2→h1 smuggling attempts rejected; WebSocket/gRPC passthrough works
- **Evidence:** transcripts, health graphs
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `oracle_unavailable` (`h2spec`), `capability_not_supplied` (no WebSocket/gRPC on site)

- **Area / first live:** Operations · P18 subset (T-0362); full T-0498
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0364, T-0498
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full (announced) · live (pilot) + lab · destructive, pilot stage only
- **Procedure:** Stop/kill Redis, Postgres, proxy, DNS, origin and others per the T-0498 scenario list while sending the mandated payload.
- **PASS when:**
  - No scenario causes inspection fail-open in `block` mode
  - Hot path never awaits the DB; recovery times meet documented targets; rollback not triggered by storms
  - Documented alerts fire for each scenario

#### AC-16 · Config revisions and convergence

- **Area / first live:** Operations · P18 subset; full T-0505
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0211, T-0234, T-0362, T-0505
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live + lab · read-only plus sandbox changes

- **PASS when:**

  - Security-relevant changes converge ≤ 2 s p95; a node that misses messages converges via revision-gap resync; invalid or older revisions never applied

#### AC-17 · SSRF and configuration safety

- **Area / first live:** Security · P08 (T-0163); P21 (T-0413, T-0415)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0009, T-0163, T-0365, T-0413, T-0415

  - DNS-rebinding rejected at connect time; untrusted/mismatched origin certificate gives 502 with no downgrade
  - Domain-ownership proof enforced; 150+ SSRF vectors rejected on every egress path

#### AC-18 · Origin protection

- **Area / first live:** Origin · P21 (T-0415)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0405 to T-0407, T-0415
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full · live · read-only plus operator-applied firewall
- **Procedure:** With `lockdown_state=applied`: direct requests to the origin IP are refused or lack content; requests without the secret header rejected by the origin (if supported). While `pending`: print instructions. In all states: origin IP absent from DNS, MX, SPF, HTTPS hints and HDD output.
- **PASS when:**
  - Off-platform probe proves direct access refused (`verified`)
  - Origin IP absent from every DNS answer, MX, TXT/SPF, HTTPS/SVCB hints, HDD header/body (scan)

  - Across the enumerated campaigns and the stated number of runs, no campaign causes a ban, a response change in `shadow`, a latency violation or an other-tenant data leak
  - No learned signal alone produces a ban in any mode
  - Observed benign false-positive rate at the operating point is at most 0.01% on replays of at least 100,000 requests each, with the 95% upper bound stated; non-Latin text stays within budget
  - The unseen-family and evasion numbers are measured and published with their manifest hashes and limits
- **Evidence:** campaign reports, model card, manifests, differential output
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied` (no optional analyst model available)

#### AC-60 · Bypass Guard and go-live gate

- **Area / first live:** Origin protection · P34 (T-0588)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0588 to T-0592, T-0599
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** pilot-full, lab · builder-local and lab · non-destructive probes only against sites the operator owns
- **Procedure:** Verify signed origin authentication across server families (valid, missing, replayed, tampered, wrong-site); connect the tunnel with all inbound ports closed; check the firewall and cloud allowlist generators against fixtures; inject bypasses (direct IP, leaked origin hostname, alternate port, stale DNS) and confirm detection within 2 probe intervals (default 2 hours); exercise the go-live gate and the protected-state wording contract.
- **PASS when:**
  - Unsigned and invalid requests never receive protected content from a verifier; replays are rejected within the window
  - With the tunnel active and inbound closed, none of the defined vantage points reaches the origin over the defined probe set
  - Every injected bypass moves the state to `bypass_detected` and raises an incident within 2 probe intervals
  - `block` mode is refused with `ERR-BYPASS-001` unless the lockdown is `verified` or a recorded risk acceptance exists; no surface says "protected" otherwise
- **Evidence:** verifier matrix, probe logs, state timeline, gate test output
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied` (second vantage point), `oracle_unavailable`, `environment_unsupported` (no isolated lab network)

#### AC-61 · Known-vulnerability coverage and ATK-301 to ATK-390

- **Area / first live:** Vulnerability management · P34 (T-0594)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0594 to T-0596, T-0599
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** lab-full, release · lab · lab-site and fixtures only
- **Procedure:** Import VKB sources from fixtures; match entries to a fixture inventory; run the exploit-signature pipeline (lint, false-positive gate, staged rollout, emergency channel, rollback); execute every ATK-301 to ATK-390 fixture with its action code; verify `lab-proven` and `shape-only` labels.
- **PASS when:**
  - Every matched entry shows the correct rule state and never "protected"
  - A signature that fails lint, or that matches the full-request replay corpus beyond its bound, is rejected or narrowed to a product and path scope and never reaches production rings; a rolled-back rule's bans are removed
  - Every ATK-301 to ATK-390 row has a fixture, an expected action and a recorded result; rows without lab proof are labeled `shape-only`
  - The emergency channel needs two approvers, starts in `monitor`, expires after 24 hours, reaches 95% of a 20-node test fleet within 10 minutes and rolls back when a stated quantitative trigger fires (hit-rate spike, ban rate or 4xx/5xx change on matched requests); an old-serial, expired or revoked-signer bundle is refused
- **Evidence:** pipeline logs, matrix results, rollout and rollback records
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `oracle_unavailable`, `capability_not_supplied`, `environment_unsupported` (no isolated lab network)

#### AC-62 · Additional hardening

- **Area / first live:** Detection · P34 (T-0593)
- **Implemented and run by:** T-0593, T-0597, T-0598, T-0599
- **Tier / mode / safety class:** lab-full, release · lab · lab-site and fixtures only
- **Procedure:** Run the parser-differential matrix (duplicate parameters, conflicting content types, chunk and length conflicts, multipart and JSON edge cases); padded, split and slow payload tests against the inspection window; the cache guard (poisoning and deception); honeytoken and integrity-watch triggers; script integrity checks; and the AI-endpoint protections (prompt-injection markers, abusive token usage, tool-call abuse shapes).
- **PASS when:**
  - Per stack profile, the interpreted request equals the lab stack's except for the documented list (T-0593 A1); a profile mismatch is never silently allowed, and the generic profile's detections are a subset of every profile's
  - With `over_limit_policy=block`, padding or splitting a payload beyond the inspection window never produces `allow`; with the default policy the verdict is tagged `truncated`, and the rolling window detects the padded fixtures; both settings are tested
  - Cache-guard, honeytoken, integrity and AI-endpoint tests produce their signals and, in `block`, their actions, with zero benign false positives
  - Latency budgets of E4 hold with all hardening features on; legitimate-client fixtures (non-UTF-8 charsets, large identifiers, signed webhook bodies, LF-only clients, matrix parameters, encoded slashes) pass unchanged
  - Rows ATK-348 to ATK-355 and the outbound-secrets-in-model-responses check each have a recorded result
- **Evidence:** differential matrix, trigger logs, benchmark tables
- **UNVERIFIED allowed only for:** `capability_not_supplied`, `environment_unsupported` (no isolated lab network)

## E4. Default numeric thresholds

The agent may **tighten** any value freely. **Loosening** a value needs the operator's approval in chat and an entry in `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` (rule R-15). Values marked *initial* are re-baselined by measurement at the gate named in the last column. The column "v4.1" records the predecessor's value where one existed so deviations are traceable.

## E5. Gate report template and gate table

### E5.1 Gate report (fixed format, used at every gate and mirrored in `STATUS.md`)

Each gate task writes `docs/gates/Gnn.md` (two-digit gate number) using exactly this structure. Output tails are pasted verbatim; full logs are stored under `docs/gates/evidence/Gnn/` with their SHA-256 listed.

```markdown
# Gate Gnn: <phase name>

- Phase / milestone: Pnn / Mx   - Commit: <git sha>   - Date: <UTC>   - Author role: <agent role>
- Environment: stage=<pilot|production> mode=<live|lab|ci> host=<id> kernel=<uname -r> toolchain=<rustc -V>

## 1. Commands run (with output tails)
| # | Command | Exit | Output tail (last 20 lines) | Full log sha256 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

## 2. Acceptance criteria
| Task | Criterion | Status | Evidence ref | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
(one line per criterion A1..A5 of every task in the phase)

## 3. Acceptance checks (AC-xx) touched by this phase
| Check | Status | Reason code if UNVERIFIED | What the operator must supply | Evidence |

## 4. Metrics
rust-share | tokei totals | test count | coverage (lines/branches) | mutation score | clippy | audit | deny | vet | unsafe-scan | claims-lint | docs-test | a11y violations | perf deltas

## 5. Deviations and assumptions
New or changed entries in docs/DEVIATIONS.md (id, reason, approver, expiry) and assumptions made.

## 6. UNVERIFIED register
Every UNVERIFIED with its reason code and the exact operator action that resolves it.

## 7. Findings
| Id | Severity | Area | Summary | Status (fixed / accepted-with-owner / open) | Link |

## 8. Risks and open questions
Top 5 risks with mitigation; questions awaiting the operator.

## 9. Rollback
How this phase's changes (migrations, config, units) are rolled back and the test that proves it.

## 10. Next steps
Next 10 tasks (ids and titles) and their blockers.
```

### E5.2 Session state files

| File | Purpose | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | Digest of at most 150 lines: non-negotiables, commands, current phase, pointers to `docs/SPEC.md` and `docs/spec/` | Updated at every gate; size checked by `xtask verify` |
| `STATUS.md` | Done, next, open risks, open questions, UNVERIFIED list, task index summary | Updated at every task completion |
| `HANDOFF.md` | Phase, failing tests, next 10 tasks, decisions, open questions | Updated at the end of every working session |
| `INDEX.md` | 599 task rows with status and links (generated; see E14), plus the execution order from `xtask tasks order` | Generated by `xtask tasks index`, checked by `--check` |
| `docs/DEVIATIONS.md` | Deviation id, reason, date, approver, expiry | Required for every loosened value or substituted technology |
| `docs/diagnoses/<id>.md` | Symptom, evidence, hypotheses tried, options | Created on the third failed attempt (failure budget) |
| `docs/adr/NNNN-*.md` | Architecture decision records | Required for every ADR slot named in tasks |
| `docs/gates/Gnn.md` | Gate reports (E5.1) | One per gate |
| `docs/CAPABILITY-MATRIX.md` | Requirement-level status (REQ-<PREFIX>-<k>) | Generated from task blocks plus evidence ids |

### E5.3 Failure budget and diagnosis template

A task or check that fails three times with different attempted fixes stops (R-14). The agent writes `docs/diagnoses/<task>-<n>.md` with: symptom; exact commands and outputs; the three hypotheses and what each attempt changed; what was observed; options (with cost and risk) for the operator; the recommended option; the task state (`blocked`) and what unblocks it. The agent then moves to the next unblocked task whose dependencies are met; blocked tasks are listed in `STATUS.md`. The failure counter resets only when a root cause is recorded.

#### E5.4.1 Pass conditions (quoted from Part D)

**G00 · Bootstrap and governance**

> Gate G00 passes when: `docs/SPEC.md` and its split exist with a matching checksum; `AGENTS.md` is at most 150 lines; `cargo check --workspace` and `cargo xtask verify` are green; `hddctl preflight --profile-only` reports honestly (including real failures); the egress guard tests pass; the capability matrix is generated; the first response of section 9 has been delivered and the operator's answers are recorded or marked open.

**G01 · UX research, personas, information architecture, journeys**

> Gate G01 passes when: the UX charter, personas, information architecture, journeys, states, accessibility and i18n plans, security-UX review and the review pack exist in `docs/UX/` and link to each other; `xtask ux check` reports zero orphan screens or journeys; the open operator decisions each have a default and an owner; and `docs/gates/G01.md` exists in the E5.1 format with the pasted command output. G01 is a light gate: the operator is shown the pack, but design sign-off is the heavier gate G03.

**G02 · Design system**

> Gate G02 passes when: the contrast check, token build and CSS budget checks pass; every component renders in the static gallery in both themes; the axe oracle reports no serious or critical findings on the gallery; keyboard maps are documented; the operator has seen screenshots of the gallery.

**G03 · Screen design and clickable design prototypes**

> Phase gate G03 passes when: all 143 screens have prototype pages in all required states; heuristic and accessibility reviews have recorded fixes; the claims-lint passes; and the operator has reviewed screenshots and recorded sign-off or a list of changes (UNVERIFIED(`human_step_pending`) until then, which blocks only the build of the affected screens).

**G04 · Frontend foundation**

> Gate G04 passes when: `hdd-web` starts from environment configuration, serves the gallery at `/admin/design-system` behind a placeholder-free authorization hook (loopback-only until P06), CSP has no violations, axe reports zero serious/critical on the gallery and error pages, JS/CSS budgets pass, visual baselines exist, and the frontend security suite is green.

**G05 · Public website, docs and status**

> Gate G05 passes when: every public page passes axe (zero serious/critical), keyboard, reflow and performance checks and works with JavaScript disabled; the network trap sees no third-party requests; only essential cookies are set; claims-lint, docs check, link check and i18n check pass; the evidence-driven claims display correctly with and without evidence; the legal guard and signup gating behave when legal text is unresolved; and the gate report lists every UNVERIFIED item (screen-reader checks, operator legal text, external status hosting).

**G06 · Identity: signup, login, MFA, sessions, teams, tenant isolation**

> Gate G06 passes when: AC-01 (auth and admin isolation), AC-35 (identity e2e), the identity part of AC-36 (RLS + BOLA), AC-46 (email security) pass on the pilot, the abuse-test suite is green, the ASVS checklist is recorded, and the first-run bootstrap works end to end.

**G07 · Customer app shell and overview**

> Gate G07 passes when: the app shell and all P07 screens pass the UI verification suite (axe, keyboard, reflow, visual, performance), permission-filtered navigation is verified for every role, the command palette never leaks other tenants' data (BOLA tests extended), and the capability matrix rows for REQ-APP are linked to passing tests.

**G08 · Domain onboarding and verification**

> Gate G08 passes when: AC-37 passes for all integration modes against the operator's pilot subzones (`test_hostname`, `sandbox_hostname`) and against local test zones, AC-17 (SSRF/config safety) passes for onboarding paths, and the wizard is completable with keyboard and screen reader checks recorded.

**G09 · DNS management**

> Gate G09 passes when: records, zones, versions and imports work through UI and API with RLS; the answer engine passes the protocol-correctness table tests; previews agree with the answer engine in 100% of property tests; safety checks block the unsafe changes in the catalog; and all screens meet the UI definition of done.

**G10 · TLS and certificate management**

> Gate G10 passes when: private keys are only ever stored under envelope encryption, TLS settings changes publish snapshot revisions, the budget service is verified against the CA's published limits at build time, custom certificate validation passes the hostile-input corpus, and all screens meet the UI definition of done.

**G11 · Walking skeleton on the pilot**

> Gate G11 passes when: AC-00 passes, AC-03 (basic), AC-04 (staging HTTP-01 and DNS-01 wildcard), and AC-05 (canary subset) pass on the pilot with pasted real output, the deploy path including rollback has been exercised, and the walking-skeleton report records the ADR confirmations.

**G12 · Security control center**

> Gate G12 passes when: every policy change is validated, versioned, diffable, and rollbackable; self-lockout guards work for access lists, rules and mode changes; all screens meet the UI definition of done; and the policy snapshot reaches the proxy within 2 s.

**G13 · WAF core engine**

> Gate G13 passes when: unit, property and fuzz-smoke suites pass; coverage ≥ 85% on the crate; `cargo-mutants` score ≥ 80%; benign corpus yields zero matches; the inspect API and the proxy integration work end to end in monitor and block modes on the builder; and the inspection benchmark meets p50 < 1 ms on the reference corpus.

**G14 · SQL injection shield**

> Gate G14 passes when: the mandated set and all variant fixtures are 100% `would_block` with category `sqli` in every vector of C4.2; held-out detection ≥ 95%; benign corpora produce zero false positives; the sqlmap monitor-mode campaign coverage ≥ 95% of injection-bearing requests (exact figure and unflagged classes reported); mutation score on SQLi modules ≥ 80%; fuzz smoke is clean.

**G15 · All other attack detectors**

> Gate G15 passes when: every ATK row marked as detected has fixtures and tests; held-out detection ≥ 95% per group; the benign gate stays at zero false positives; the mutation score for new modules ≥ 80%; fuzz smoke is clean; and inspection latency budgets still hold with all detectors enabled.

**G16 · Bans, jail, appeals and end-to-end proof**

> Gate G16 passes when: AC-08 (ban persistence and unban), AC-34 (ban-poisoning resistance), AC-22 (IP resolution) subsets, the builder-local vulnerable-origin proof, loom/shuttle concurrency tests and all P16 UI checks pass; AC-38/AC-39 full lab proofs remain scheduled for P28 with the minimal local equivalent passing now.

**G17 · Rate limits, bots, challenge and reputation**

> Gate G17 passes when: AC-11 (rate limiting), AC-44 (challenge and bots), credential-stuffing lab tests, and AC-48 (scanner/bot detection) subsets pass; challenge pass rates and solve times meet targets on a reference device matrix; false-positive tests on benign traffic replays show zero blocks and bounded challenge rates; and all UI screens meet the UI definition of done.

**G18 · Proxy core pipeline and HTTP hardening**

> Gate G18 passes when: AC-14 (protocol hardening) passes against the sandbox hostname with process health maintained, AC-15 resilience scenarios (pilot stage) pass, AC-13 (modes, safe mode, auto-rollback) passes, AC-16 convergence subsets pass, performance budgets (proxy-added p99 ≤ 5 ms functional profile) hold, and fuzz smoke on HTTP parsers is clean.

**G19 · TLS, ACME and certificate store (data plane)**

> Gate G19 passes when: AC-04 (staging) passes in full including DNS-01 wildcard, forced short-window renewal, CT observation, TLS policy checks via oracles; the production issuance procedure is rehearsed on staging and documented; and nothing in this phase issues production certificates without the operator's approval.

**G20 · Authoritative DNS, full data plane**

> Gate G20 passes when: AC-03 (DNS protocol and parity) passes in full on the pilot subzone with `dig`, `kdig`, `delv` where applicable and the independent hickory-client suite; AC-21 (secondary and TSIG) passes or is `UNVERIFIED(human_step_pending)` only for the external secondary's availability; AC-28 amplification ratio and RRL checks pass in the closed lab; the DNS fuzz smoke is clean; qps and memory budgets are met; and DNSSEC is not claimed anywhere unless `delv` validates it.

**G21 · Origin protection and outbound filter**

> Gate G21 passes when: AC-10 (outbound leak control) passes with the canary `leak.txt` and the lab leak fixtures including binary and streaming negatives; AC-18 passes or is `UNVERIFIED(human_step_pending)` only for the operator-side firewall change; AC-05 header checks pass with the canary echo; AC-17 connect-time SSRF checks pass in the proxy; zero false positives on the benign outbound corpus; and the claims-lint passes for every new string.

**G22 · Platform admin panel**

> Gate G22 passes when: every S-1xx admin screen in scope renders from real data or an honest empty state; the platform-role privilege matrix passes in full (AC-01 admin isolation, AC-42 admin operations); all mutations are audited and chain-verified; accessibility, visual and performance checks pass for all admin screens; and no admin API can be reached with an org-role session or from the app host.

**G23 · Analytics and reports**

> Gate G23 passes when: AC-52 (analytics correctness) passes with synthetic ground truth, the live monitor holds its latency and backpressure budgets, reports render identically from snapshots, the PDF output passes the accessibility checks chosen in the ADR, exports are bounded and audited, and all screens meet the UI definition of done.

**G24 · Notifications, integrations, public API and SDK**

> Gate G24 passes when: alert rules route correctly with dedupe, quiet hours and escalation; all channel integrations pass contract tests against local fakes (and live smoke tests where the operator supplied test destinations); webhooks are signed, retried and idempotent; the API contract tests and breaking-change detector pass; the SDK passes its integration tests; and AC-45 passes.

**G25 · Host defenses: kernel firewall, XDP and kernel tuning**

> Gate G25 passes when: AC-26 (XDP) and AC-29 (tuning) pass in the lab or are `UNVERIFIED(environment_unsupported)` with the fallback proven; kernel ban/unban propagation meets ≤ 2 s; the dead-man timer detaches XDP when unconfirmed; the nftables baseline and tuning apply and undo cleanly on a disposable VM; the hardening report passes; and no lab flood traffic left the closed lab.

**G26 · Shield, escalation and DNS survivability**

> Gate G26 passes when: the state machine passes the recorded-trace test suite (including flapping, slow-ramp and saturation traces); live low-rate checks confirm alerts, heartbeat and audit events; provider activation dry-run documentation exists; manual standby-edge failover is rehearsed in the pilot with measured TTL-bound timing; AC-25 and AC-27 are PASS or UNVERIFIED with exact reasons.

**G27 · Vulnerability management, virtual patching and posture scanning**

> Gate G27 passes when: feeds ingest from pinned sources (or offline files) with verification; matching reproduces a fixture set with documented false-positive handling; SLA clocks and alerts behave per policy; virtual-patch lifecycle enforces preconditions and expiry; the posture scanner produces the generated report from the sandbox/test hostname without exceeding its rate or leaving its allowlist; and AC-30, AC-31 and AC-32 pass or are UNVERIFIED with exact reasons.

**G28 · Acceptance suite, closed lab and the Vuln-Lab**

> Gate G28 passes when: the runner executes the complete catalog AC-00 to AC-54 (AC-55 to AC-58 are registered and stay `UNVERIFIED(stage_not_reached)` until P33) with a rendered report in which every item is PASS, FAIL (none allowed at the gate) or UNVERIFIED with an enumerated reason; AC-38 and AC-39 pass in the lab including the oracle campaign figures; the safety self-tests (AC-00) pass; and no acceptance traffic left its allowlist (audit and packet-capture proof).

**G29 · Performance, chaos, fuzz and supply chain**

> Gate G29 passes when: AC-24 numbers meet the budgets (or documented deviations exist with tracked tasks); soak runs show no leaks; chaos scenarios keep invariants (no fail-open in `block` mode); fuzz smoke is clean and the nightly campaign has no open crash; mutation and coverage gates pass; AC-33 passes (signed update with rollback exercised); and the self-security review has no open high finding.

**G30 · Deployment, backup, upgrade and operations**

> Gate G30 passes when: a clean VPS can be brought to a working production-shaped deployment by `hddctl deploy` alone; a total-loss disaster recovery drill meets the stated RTO/RPO; an upgrade and a forced rollback succeed; key rotations complete without downtime; monitoring, alert rules and runbooks cover every alert; and AC-54 passes.

**G31 · Documentation, cutover readiness and final report**

> Gate G31 passes when: documentation is complete and tested; the legal templates and claims audit are done; the cutover pack passes its checklist and rehearsal; the operator confirmations are recorded; production issuance is completed or explicitly deferred; the cutover (if authorized) is completed and stabilized with monitor-first findings addressed, or explicitly deferred; and the final report with residual risks is delivered.

**G32 · Backlog, Tier 2 to Tier 6**

> Gate G32 is the per-task closing review used each time a backlog item completes (the gate report format is the same, appended to `docs/gates/G32-<task>.md`).

**G33 · Runtime profiles, local mode, 24/7 hosting and defense completeness**

> Gate G33 passes when: AC-55 (local runtime, including `profile-parity` with zero verdict differences), AC-56 (24/7 hosting readiness), AC-57 (access gate, API discovery and business flows) and AC-58 (coverage map integrity and absolute-wording lint) pass; the local suite is green on Windows, macOS and Linux CI runners; the hosting check passes on the pilot server with a successful reboot test and a restore drill; and the coverage map lists every mapped category with a status and the "does not cover" section.

**G34 · Learned detection, Bypass Guard and known-vulnerability coverage**

> Gate G34 passes when: AC-59 (Sentinel safety, robustness and shadow evidence), AC-60 (Bypass Guard), AC-61 (known-vulnerability coverage and ATK-301 to ATK-390) and AC-62 (additional hardening) pass or end `UNVERIFIED` with enumerated reasons; no learned component can ban alone (tested); a site cannot enter `block` mode while its lockdown is not verified (tested); the held-out evaluation, including leave-one-family-out runs, is published with its limits; and the coverage map (E15) is regenerated with the new rows and no covered row without evidence.

## E6. Hostile review checklists

Every diff gets a hostile self-review before it is committed (task lifecycle step 8, section 0): read it as an attacker, a malicious tenant, a careless operator and a failing dependency. The universal list applies always; area lists apply when the diff touches the area. Findings are recorded in the PR description or commit body; unresolved items become tasks or `docs/diagnoses/` entries.

### E6.1 Universal (every diff)

- [ ] Does any new input reach a parser, a query, a path, a command, a template or a URL without validation at the boundary and a size/time bound?
- [ ] Is every buffer, queue, cache, map, loop, retry and recursion bounded (and is the bound tested)?
- [ ] Can an unauthenticated or low-privileged caller trigger work that costs the platform more than it costs them?
- [ ] Does the error path leak secrets, stack traces, internal hostnames, SQL or tenant identifiers?
- [ ] Are secrets kept out of logs, metrics labels, events, panics, `Debug` output, URLs and test fixtures?
- [ ] Is there any `unwrap`/`expect`/indexing/arithmetic that can panic or overflow on attacker-controlled data?
- [ ] Does the change fail closed on inspection and fail safe elsewhere, and is that documented where it differs?
- [ ] Is the new behavior covered by a failing-then-passing test and, for security properties, a negative test?
- [ ] Are time, randomness and I/O injectable so tests are deterministic?
- [ ] Does the change add a dependency, and if so does it pass deny/audit/vet and justify its unsafe and transitive surface?
- [ ] Does the change alter a claim in the UI/docs? Is it still true, evidenced and limited (claims-lint)?
- [ ] Does it weaken a threshold from E4? If so, is there approval and a DEVIATIONS entry?
- [ ] Can this change lock the operator out (SSH, admin, firewall, DNS) and does it have the timed revert / preview?
- [ ] Is the audit event written exactly once with actor, reason, before and after?
- [ ] Is the migration expand/contract safe under version skew and is rollback documented?
- [ ] Are tenant boundaries enforced in the query (RLS plus explicit scoping) and in the cache key?
- [ ] Does anything depend on the order of concurrent operations without a lock, version check or idempotency key?
- [ ] Is the behavior identical for IPv4 and IPv6, and for h1, h2 (and h3 once present)?
- [ ] Are accessibility, reduced motion, no-JS fallback and both themes preserved for UI changes?
- [ ] Is the documentation or runbook updated, and does its sample command still run (docs-test)?

### E6.2 Web UI and templates

- [ ] Is every dynamic value escaped by default; is `SafeHtml` constructed only from sanitizer output or constants?
- [ ] Does the page work with CSP nonces and Trusted Types and without inline handlers or `eval`?
- [ ] Are forms protected by CSRF tokens bound to session, Origin/Fetch-Metadata checks, and idempotency/PRG?
- [ ] Are HTMX endpoints returning partials only to HX requests and full pages otherwise, with correct `Vary`?
- [ ] Are focus management, labels, error association, live regions and keyboard operation correct?
- [ ] Are destructive actions behind typed confirmation or step-up with an audit preview?
- [ ] Does the screen show real data or an honest empty state (never mock numbers)?
- [ ] Are charts accompanied by tables and non-color encodings?
- [ ] Does any link use `target=_blank` without `rel=noopener noreferrer`?
- [ ] Are cookies `__Host-` prefixed with `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite` where applicable?

### E6.3 API and control plane

- [ ] Does the route have a permission annotation and a negative authorization test for every role?
- [ ] Are object ids authorized against the caller's org on every access (BOLA), including list filters and bulk endpoints?
- [ ] Are request bodies strict (`deny_unknown_fields`), size-capped, depth-capped and content-type checked?
- [ ] Are pagination, filtering and sorting parameters allowlisted and bound (no injection into SQL fragments)?
- [ ] Are `If-Match` and idempotency keys honored for mutating endpoints?
- [ ] Is rate limiting per key and per IP present, with stricter limits for expensive endpoints?
- [ ] Are error responses RFC 9457 with stable ERR codes and no internals?
- [ ] Are responses shaped by role (field-level permissions) and free of secrets?
- [ ] Are webhook/URL/host inputs passed through the egress guard?
- [ ] Is the OpenAPI document updated and the contract test passing?

### E6.4 Identity and sessions

- [ ] Are tokens opaque, high-entropy, stored hashed, single-use where required and constant-time compared?
- [ ] Do login, reset and signup responses and timings avoid account enumeration?
- [ ] Are sessions rotated on privilege change and revoked on password/MFA/role change?
- [ ] Is step-up required and fresh for sensitive actions, and bound to the session?
- [ ] Are lockouts and rate limits resistant to attacker-induced victim lockout?
- [ ] Is MFA enrollment forced for platform roles and are recovery paths documented and audited?
- [ ] Are passkey/TOTP replay protections tested (sign counter, last used step)?
- [ ] Is the pepper/key versioning present for rotation?
- [ ] Is impersonation read-only, time-boxed, bannered and audited?
- [ ] Are API keys scoped, hashed, shown once and re-evaluated against the creator's permissions on each call?

### E6.5 Database and migrations

- [ ] Does every new tenant table have `org_id`, RLS and an index leading with it; are policies tested with a forged `app.org_id`?
- [ ] Are `SECURITY DEFINER` functions avoided or reviewed with a fixed `search_path`?
- [ ] Are queries parameterized (sqlx compile-time checked) with no string-built SQL?
- [ ] Are migrations additive, lock-timeout bounded, reversible where claimed, and linted?
- [ ] Are partitions created ahead and retention implemented by partition drop?
- [ ] Are secrets stored with envelope encryption and AAD binding?
- [ ] Are long transactions, unbounded `IN` lists and sequential scans avoided in hot paths?
- [ ] Is the deletion ledger replayed after restore?

### E6.6 Proxy and data plane

- [ ] Is the hot path free of awaits on the database and of unbounded allocation?
- [ ] Is inspection performed before any upstream I/O and before cache lookup; does it fail closed in `block` mode?
- [ ] Are client-supplied forwarding headers stripped and the real client IP resolved from the socket or trusted proxies only?
- [ ] Are request smuggling vectors (CL/TE, obs-fold, duplicate headers, h2→h1 translation) rejected?
- [ ] Does the origin client verify certificates with no bypass path and refuse private/platform addresses at connect time?
- [ ] Are redirects never followed and loops detected?
- [ ] Are per-tenant fairness budgets and global shed policies in place?
- [ ] Do panics stay isolated per request and fail closed with a Ray ID?
- [ ] Is the secret origin header never emitted to clients, logs or events?
- [ ] Are branded pages free of tenant cross-leakage and rule names?
- [ ] Is `/__hdd/` handled before routing to the origin and unreachable by tenants' paths?
- [ ] Are websocket/gRPC upgrades inspected at handshake and capped afterwards?

### E6.7 WAF engine and detectors

- [ ] Is the engine pure (no I/O, no clock, no randomness) and deterministic for identical input?
- [ ] Are all three views (raw, decoded, canonical) evaluated and decoding bounded (depth, size, iterations)?
- [ ] Do regexes avoid catastrophic backtracking (automata engine or bounded) and have worst-case tests?
- [ ] Does the new rule have positive, negative and counter-example fixtures and a benign-corpus run?
- [ ] Are hard versus soft semantics, hardness tags and field-kind policy respected?
- [ ] Can an attacker use a new rule to cause bans of victims (cross-site context, spoofed headers, shared addresses)?
- [ ] Are evidence snippets redacted and ≤ 512 bytes?
- [ ] Is performance measured (p50/p99, worst-case input) and within budget?
- [ ] Does the change keep `monitor` mode honest (records `would_block`, no side effects)?
- [ ] Is the detector registered in the attack-matrix check with ATK ids?

### E6.8 DNS

- [ ] Does the query path touch only the immutable snapshot (no DB, no network except bounded flatten tasks)?
- [ ] Are responses minimal, size-capped, correct for NXDOMAIN/NODATA/wildcard/ENT/CNAME cases, and tested against the reference implementation?
- [ ] Is HDD unable to act as a reflector (no recursion, RRL, cookies, TC=1 behavior, ANY minimal)?
- [ ] Are zone transfers TSIG-only with source allowlists and no information leak on refusal?
- [ ] Can a tenant create names that collide with platform names or other tenants' zones?
- [ ] Does the proxied-answer path guarantee that origin addresses never leave in answers or hints?
- [ ] Are serials monotonic across imports, rollbacks and restores?
- [ ] Is DNSSEC never claimed without validation?

### E6.9 TLS, ACME and certificates

- [ ] Are private keys only ever stored encrypted and decrypted in the proxy process, zeroized on drop?
- [ ] Is production issuance gated on the operator's approval and the failed-validation budget?
- [ ] Are CAA, CT and ARI considered; are validation guards tenant-safe (no cross-tenant challenge hijack)?
- [ ] Is unknown/absent SNI refused and HSTS gated on a valid certificate?
- [ ] Is the minimum TLS version and cipher policy enforced and tested with an oracle?
- [ ] Does certificate hot reload leave in-flight connections unaffected?

### E6.10 Firewall, XDP and host

- [ ] Does the change preserve SSH and admin access and use the timed auto-revert?
- [ ] Are never-ban/never-drop lists consulted on every kernel path?
- [ ] Is `unsafe` confined to the allowlisted module and each block justified?
- [ ] Are map updates atomic and legitimate-traffic regressions tested?
- [ ] Are commands built as argument arrays and inputs parsed to typed values first?
- [ ] Can the operator undo every host change exactly (before/after hash)?

### E6.11 Shield and escalation

- [ ] Can an attacker trigger a harmful escalation by spoofing signals or poisoning bans?
- [ ] Does every action record `skipped(feature_absent)` or its result, with an undo?
- [ ] Does the system fail safe (revert) if the shield dies?
- [ ] Are capacity statements limited to the three provenance-labeled numbers?

### E6.12 Vulnerability management and scanning

- [ ] Is feed content treated as untrusted data (escaped, size-bounded, no actions)?
- [ ] Does the matcher avoid guessing versions and mark unknowns?
- [ ] Can a virtually patched item ever be marked resolved or stop its SLA clock?
- [ ] Is the scanner restricted to the allowlist, rate-limited and incapable of sending exploit payloads?

### E6.13 Operations, deployment and supply chain

- [ ] Are artifacts verified (signature, checksum, provenance) before install, and is rollback automatic on failure?
- [ ] Are secrets generated, stored 0600 and never baked into images or compose files?
- [ ] Are services least-privileged (capabilities, users, sandboxing) and scored by `systemd-analyze security`?
- [ ] Are backups encrypted with keys not stored on the host and restore-tested?
- [ ] Does the dependency change pass deny/audit/vet and keep the SBOM correct?
- [ ] Is the lab (Vuln-Lab, chaos, oracles) excluded from release artifacts?

### E6.14 Documentation and claims

- [ ] Does every statement about protection, performance, availability or compliance map to evidence and carry its limits?
- [ ] Are forbidden phrases absent (unhackable, complete protection, guaranteed, compliant, certified, AI-powered without evidence)?
- [ ] Are mandatory disclosures present (readiness footnote, mitigated-not-fixed, partial scan, geolocation approximation, lab-proven labels)?
- [ ] Do documented commands and routes exist and run?

### E6.15 Lab, fixtures and tests

- [ ] Does every fixture carry a class and obey target rules (A live test host GET/HEAD, B sandbox, C inspect API only)?
- [ ] Do lab tools refuse non-lab targets and public addresses?
- [ ] Are held-out sets untouched by tuning?
- [ ] Is every sleeping or time-dependent test using injected clocks?
- [ ] Do chaos and flood tools clean up faults on exit and on crash?

### E6.16 Runtime profiles and local mode (new in v5.1)

- [ ] Does any new code branch on the runtime profile outside `hdd-local`, `hdd-common::kv`, `hdd-common::profile` or the `Enforcer` factory? (It must not; R-31.)
- [ ] Does any new runtime state bypass the `KvStore`, `Bus` and `Limiter` traits, and does it have a conformance test on both backends?
- [ ] Is every new durable state rebuildable from Postgres at startup (the `MemoryKv` restart contract)?
- [ ] Can a web page the operator opens reach, read or change anything in the local control plane (Host, Origin, Fetch Metadata, CSRF, CORS, Private Network Access)?
- [ ] Is every listener loopback-only unless the data-plane LAN exposure acknowledgement is present, and is that tested from a non-loopback address?
- [ ] Does any action touch the OS (trust store, hosts file, firewall, autostart, ports below 1024) without an explicit consent step, a precise diff and a reversal that restores the original?
- [ ] Could a loopback ban, a never-ban change or a rate limit lock the operator out of the dashboard (R-19)?
- [ ] Are secrets absent from command lines, child environments, logs and the process table?
- [ ] Does any copy imply that local mode is always on or highly available (section 4)?

### E6.17 Access gate, API discovery and business flows (new in v5.1)

- [ ] Does gate matching use both the raw and the canonical path, and does the bypass suite include the new shape you just thought of?
- [ ] Are unknown-user and wrong-secret gate responses identical in status, body and timing?
- [ ] Can a gate rule lock out the acting user without the preview and acknowledgement (`ERR-GATE-004`)?
- [ ] Does API learning store any request value (it must store types, bounds and names only), and does the privacy test cover the new field?
- [ ] Can an imported API description trigger a network fetch, unbounded recursion or memory growth (remote `$ref`, deep nesting, expansion)?
- [ ] Do schema violations ever ban on their own (they must not), and does switching to `block` require the preview acknowledgement?
- [ ] Does any business-flow signal store card numbers, credentials or form values, and does the event explain which signals fired in plain language?
- [ ] Do flows start in `monitor`, and does `monitor` change no response (differential test)?
- [ ] Does any new coverage-map row claim `covered` without an ATK group, an AC and a task, and does any new text use a forbidden phrase (section 4.2)?

## E7. Canonical names registry

One spelling for every name. Code, docs, tests, UI strings and fixtures use these exactly; a mismatch is a defect. `xtask names check` greps the repository for known variants (for example `hdd_proxy` versus `hdd-proxy`) and for names that appear in this registry but not in the code (or the reverse).

### E7.1 Crates, binaries and tools

| `hdd-waf-core` | lib | normalizer, detectors, tokenizers, scoring, rules, leak scanner | pure, no I/O, `forbid(unsafe_code)` |

### E7.4 HTTP headers

| Header | Direction | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HDD-Ray-ID` | response (and upstream request) | 16 hex chars + `-HDD1`; on every response |
| `HDD-Connecting-IP` | upstream request | resolved client IP (origin should trust only from HDD) |
| `X-Forwarded-For`, `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-Proto`, `X-Forwarded-Host` | upstream request | standard forwarding set; inbound variants stripped |
| `HDD-Origin-Auth` | upstream request | secret origin header (per site, rotated with overlap) |
| `HDD-Hop` | upstream request | loop detection counter (508 on loop) |
| `HDD-Signature` | webhook request | `t=<unix>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>` |
| `HDD-Event-Id`, `HDD-Event-Type`, `HDD-Delivery-Id` | webhook request | delivery identity |
| `Idempotency-Key` | API/webhook | 24 h replay semantics |
| `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining`, `RateLimit-Reset`, `Retry-After` | API response | rate-limit state |
| `Deprecation`, `Sunset` | API response | deprecation policy |
| `X-Vuln-Lab: intentionally-vulnerable` | Vuln-Lab response | lab banner |
| `HDD-Scan-Allow` | posture scanner request | documented scanner identification token |
| `Server: Hack-Dev-Defence` | response | default banner (per-site override) |

### E7.6 Reserved paths on customer domains

`/__hdd/` is handled by HDD before routing: `/__hdd/challenge/*`, `/__hdd/appeal/*`, `/__hdd/csp-report/<site-token>`, `/__hdd/gate/login` and `/__hdd/gate/link/<id>` (access gate, C19.2), `/__hdd/health` (disabled by default), `/__hdd/static/*` (block/challenge page assets, with SRI). Origins that use the prefix receive a warning at onboarding. Also reserved: `/.well-known/acme-challenge/*` (HTTP-01) and `/.well-known/hdd-verification/*`.

### E7.9 Redis keys and channels

The authoritative list is B5.12; all of it is reached only through the `KvStore`, `Bus` and `Limiter` traits (R-31), and v5.1 adds `hdd:gate:sess:{site}:{token_hash}`, `hdd:flow:{site}:{flow}:{key}` and `hdd:lo:{ua_hash}`. Additions in v5: `hdd:shield:state` (current shield state, heartbeat-guarded), `hdd:fw:ack:{revision}` (enforcement acknowledgments), `hdd:cache:purge` (cache purge channel, Tier 2), `hdd:events:{site}` capped streams for the live monitor, `hdd:node:{id}:hb` (node heartbeats). All keys use the `hdd:` prefix and a documented TTL; no key stores secrets in plaintext.

### E7.10 Host paths

**Local profile data directory (`HDD_DATA_DIR`):** Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hdd\`, macOS `~/Library/Application Support/hdd/`, Linux `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/hdd/`; contents `pg/`, `secrets/`, `snapshot/`, `spool/`, `backups/`, `logs/`, `ca/`, `bootstrap.token`, `lock`. **Hosted:**

`/etc/hdd/` (config, `secrets/` 0700, files 0600), `/var/lib/hdd/` (state: `dns/snapshot.bin`, `shield-state.json`, `deploy-state.json`, `tune-undo.json`), `/var/log/hdd/` (if not journald), `/run/hdd/` (sockets), `/opt/hdd/releases/<version>/` with `/opt/hdd/current` symlink, `/var/run/hdd-safe-mode`, `/var/run/hdd-maintenance`, `/var/run/hdd-acceptance.stop`, `/usr/lib/systemd/system/hdd-*.service`.

### E7.11 Metric, error, audit and permission families

Prefixes: metrics `MET-hdd_<area>_<name>`; errors `ERR-<AREA>-<nnn>` (AREA: VAL, AUTH, PERM, RATE, CONC, IDEMP, ORG, TENANT, DOM, DNS, TLS, ORIGIN, WAF, BAN, APPEAL, KEY, HOOK, REPORT, ANALYTICS, PLAT, ACME, LOCAL, HOSTING, GATE, APIDISC, FLOW, VISITOR, SYS); audit `AUD-<area>.<action>`; permissions `PERM-<area>.<action>`; screens `S-nnn`; journeys `J-nn`; attack ids `ATK-nnn` in groups `AG-nn`; acceptance `AC-nn`; requirements `REQ-<PREFIX>-<k>`; tasks `T-nnnn`; gates `Gnn`; milestones `Mn`; deviations `DEV-V5-nnn`; ADR files `docs/adr/NNNN-slug.md`.

### E8.1 Decision confirmations the agent must ask for explicitly (never assume)

1. Switching any production-facing site from `monitor` to `block` (with the impact summary).
2. Production ACME issuance (one event per approved request).
3. Any `load` profile run and any destructive resilience/chaos test in production stage (with a maintenance window).
4. Opening public signup (`signup.mode: open`).
5. Cutover of the apex (registrar changes) and the rollback decision deadline.
6. Accepting any NO-GO cutover gate item (item-specific, written, dated).
7. Loosening any threshold in E4 or substituting any technology from section 6 (DEVIATIONS entry).
8. Enabling auto-update, auto-failover, or any Tier 2 to 6 feature that changes the attack surface.
9. Sending any email to an address other than `operator_email` during development.
10. Any volumetric test beyond the closed lab, which needs the provider's written permission.

### E9.2 What v5 adds

- **A product, not only an engine:** UX research, a dark-first design system with verified WCAG 2.2 AA tokens, 143 designed screens, a public site, signup and login with MFA and passkeys, organizations and roles, a customer dashboard, an admin panel, analytics, reports, notifications, a public API and SDK (P01 to P08, P22 to P24).
- **Multi-tenancy and SaaS safety:** `deployment_mode`, ownership verification, five integration modes, per-tenant fairness, row-level security with a BOLA suite, SSRF-safe egress, abuse tooling (P06, P08, P21, P22).
- **Domain onboarding and full domain controls:** an eight-step wizard, DNS import and parity, record editor, TLS and certificate management, origin configuration, lockdown wizard, readiness score, decommission (P08 to P10, P20, P21).
- **The SQL-injection doctrine and the vulnerable-origin shield:** a three-view normalizer, SQL tokenizer with fingerprints, hard families H1 to H8, field-kind policy, ban-on-first-hard-hit with a progressive ladder, ban-poisoning defenses, auth-endpoint strict mode, outbound leak control, virtual patches and the Vuln-Lab proof (C3, C4, P14, P16, P21, P27, P28).
- **A 390-row attack coverage matrix** with action codes and per-row fixtures and tests (C5, P15, P28).
- **Challenge, bots and reputation:** proof-of-work challenge, verified bots, bot scoring, credential-stuffing detection, anti-scraping (P17).
- **Operational completeness:** backup and restore drills, expand/contract upgrades, key rotation, monitoring and runbooks, disaster-recovery drill, signed releases (P29, P30).
- **Honesty machinery:** claims policy with lint and audit, the three capacity numbers, UI disclosures, UNVERIFIED reason codes, lab-proven labeling (A section 4, E3, T-0534).
- **Backlog design:** Tier 2 to Tier 6 tasks specified to the same level as Tier 1 (P32).
- **Two runtime profiles (v5.1):** `local` (a personal computer, no Docker, live only while HDD runs) and `hosted` (a server, 24/7), one code path (R-31), store traits with Redis and in-process backends, embedded PostgreSQL, local CA, loopback identity, control-plane hardening against hostile pages, hosting profiles H1 to H5 and `hddctl hosting check`, watchdog supervision, last-known-good snapshot autonomy, backups and runbooks (C18, P33).
- **Defense completeness (v5.1):** access gate for sensitive paths, API discovery with positive security, business-flow protection, and the coverage map with the permanent "does not cover" list (C19, E15, P33), under the rule that no absolute claim is made (R-32).
- **Learned detection, bypass control and known vulnerabilities (v5.2):** Sentinel (bounded, advisory-first, explainable machine learning plus an optional off-path analyst, C20, R-33), the Bypass Guard (signed origin authentication, outbound tunnel, firewall generators, continuous outside verification, go-live gate, R-34, C21), the Known-Vulnerability Knowledge Base with exploit-signature pipeline, 90 more matrix rows (ATK-301 to ATK-390) and additional hardening (C22, P34, AC-59 to AC-62).
- **Delivery slices (v5.1):** DS0 to DS6, computed dependency closures with planning effort (section 0.8, E13.5).

### E9.3 Intentional changes of behavior and numbering

| Topic | v4.1 | v5 | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mandated SQLi payloads | "7 required" (six listed) | Six (M1 to M6) plus variant families | The operator's message lists six; the seventh was undefined (`DEV-V5-003`) |
| Acceptance ids | AC-00 to AC-34 (AC-25 to AC-33 in sections 21/22) | AC-00 to AC-58 in one table | Single source of truth; AC-19 keeps its meaning (dashboard and headers, extended); AC-54 is backup/restore/upgrade/DR |
| Phases | 9 phases + Tier 6 | 35 phases (P00 to P34), 599 tasks, 15 milestones (M0 to M14) and delivery slices DS0 to DS6 | UI/UX-first product build requested by the operator |
| API base path | `/api/waf/*`, `/api/...` | `/api/v1/...` with `D/O/P` shorthand | Versioned public API |
| Dashboard | single admin UI on :3000 | three surfaces (www/app/admin) from one `hdd-web` on :3000 plus `hdd-api` on :8000 | Product surfaces and isolation |
| Amplification ratio | ≤ 4.0 (≤ 2.0 for `ANY`) | ≤ 3.0 (≤ 1.5 for `ANY`) | Tightened (allowed without approval) |
| Fixture class rules | A/B/C with sandbox | Unchanged, plus lab exemption for the Vuln-Lab only | Section 2.8 |
| `AC-24` performance | Tier 6 only | Release-tier check with environment-tagged numbers (P29) | Performance statements must cite measurements |
| Dashboard framework | unspecified | askama + HTMX + vanilla islands (spike T-0071 may choose Leptos SSR) | Rust-first with minimal JS (`DEV-V5-002`, `DEV-V5-005`) |
| Challenge | not specified | Proof-of-work challenge and clearance cookie | Bot and under-attack defenses |
| Ban key for IPv6 | /64 | /64 (unchanged), /56 aggregation for DNS RRL | Consistency |
| Test ban TTL | 60 s | 60 s (unchanged) | Safety |
| Cutover gates | 6 items | 7 items (adds product-surface checks) | Public product exposure |
| Gate numbering | phase numbers | `Gnn` = end of `Pnn` (G01 is a light gate closed by T-0028) | Traceability |
| Attack groups | none | `AG-01` to `AG-17` | Matrix navigation (avoids clashing with gate ids) |
| Runtime | one hosted VPS shape | `runtime.profile: local` or `hosted`, hosting profiles H1 to H5 | Run on a personal computer or 24/7 on a server with one code path (R-31) |
| Password pepper | HMAC pre-hash with one pepper | Argon2id keyed `secret` with `users.password_pepper_kid` and rotation | Cleaner rotation and standard construction (T-0106, T-0526) |
| Audit retention default | 365 days | 400 days, floor 180 | One value everywhere (B10, E4) |
| Proof-of-work tiers | one difficulty | one table: baseline 14, appeal 14, elevated 18, automation 20 to 22 bits | Removes the earlier conflicting values (C7.2) |
| Platform surfaces behind the proxy | loopback HTTP origin | `origin_kind=platform_internal` (Unix socket) and a same-origin `/api/v1` mount for cookies | SSRF guard exemption that tenants can never reach (section 2.9, B2.1) |
| NOTRACK | by port | per direction, client flows stay tracked | Keeps ACME, feeds and SMTP return traffic working (C11.5) |
| Proxy-added latency | undefined during the outbound hold | origin body-wait is origin time (C14.9) | One measurable definition |
| Gate G01 | folded into G03 | a light gate closed by T-0028 | Every phase has a gate report |

### E9.5 Not carried forward

- The single-page "dashboard" scope of v4.1 (superseded by the product surfaces).
- The assumption that the operator is the only tenant (kept as `owner_only` mode, but the architecture is multi-tenant throughout).
- Unstructured "capability backlog" ordering (replaced by P32 with tiers and triggers).
- Any text that granted the agent implicit approval for production actions (all production-affecting steps remain human-gated, now with explicit confirmation lists in E8.1).

### E9.6 What changed between the v5.0 draft and v5.1

An external review of the v5.0 draft produced the findings below. Each was checked against the text; the valid ones are fixed here, and two claims were checked and found incorrect (stated last).

| Finding | Change in v5.1 |
| --- | --- |
| Platform-surface routing to loopback conflicts with the SSRF guard that rejects loopback and platform addresses | `origin_kind=platform_internal` exemption, Unix sockets, no tenant path (section 2.9, T-0355, T-0413) |
| Onboarding scans and the delegation checker need iterative DNS, which the egress rules did not allow | Egress class `dns_resolution` with its limits (section 2.1, T-0156, T-0161, T-0413) |
| Pepper design: HMAC pre-hash with no rotation identifier | Argon2id keyed `secret`, `password_pepper_kid`, rotation by kid (B5.2, B10, T-0105, T-0106, T-0526) |
| `ERR-ACME-*` referenced but not defined | `ERR-ACME-001` to `-007` in B7, referenced from T-0396 |
| Proof-of-work difficulty stated as 12 to 14, 14, 16, 18 and 20 in different places | One table in C7.2; T-0324, T-0337 and E4.6 cite it |
| Audit retention 365 versus 400 days | 400 days with a 180-day floor everywhere |
| T-0001 creates a skeleton but its criterion forbids files outside `docs/` and `README.md` | Criterion A5 allows only the `.gitkeep` skeleton |
| G01 declared "folded into G03" while the gate numbering promises one gate per phase | G01 is a light gate closed by T-0028 with `docs/gates/G01.md` |
| T-0207 writes the final ADR before the spike has produced results | Preliminary ADR stub; final ADR in T-0387 |
| `hdd_readonly` missing from the deployment role list; v5 Redis keys missing from B5.12 | Both added |
| Counter-based rate limiting described as exact | Documented error bound; exact algorithm for authentication endpoints (T-0333, AC-11) |
| T-0537 depends on T-0538 but is numbered before it | Execution-order note in the P31 header and T-0537 |
| Vuln-Lab command-injection and deserialization proofs read as proofs of RCE protection | Scoped wording and claims rules 5 and 6 (section 4.1, T-0495, T-0497, T-0540) |
| Partitioned tables with primary keys that lack the partition key; `COPY` into an RLS table without an organization context | Composite keys, no foreign keys to partitioned tables, `waf_events_ingest` with a worker drain (B5.1, B5.7) |
| Cookie sessions with a separate `api.` host and CORS | Same-origin `/api/v1` mount on `app` and `admin`; `api.` is bearer-only (B2.1, B6.1, C9.1) |
| NOTRACK rules by port break the host's own outbound client flows | Direction-specific rules (C11.5, T-0468) |
| Proxy-added latency ambiguous while the outbound filter holds the response | Definition in C14.9 and B9; T-0372 and T-0409 aligned |
| "Borderline" SQL H2 rule left to the implementer | Deterministic rule plus boundary fixture file (C4.5, E1.11) |
| The specification is too large to load in one piece | Loading strategy of section 0.1: save verbatim, split at the markers (T-0001, lossless, no split file above 2,000 lines), then read one phase file at a time |
| Effort and feasibility of 560 tasks unclear | Delivery slices DS0 to DS6 with computed closures and planning effort (E13.5) |
| **Checked and found incorrect:** the document is truncated at T-0022 | The file is complete (all task blocks, appendices E1 to E15 and the closing line); the symptom comes from an input limit of the reviewing tool, which is why section 0.1 has the agent split the file and read it in parts |
| **Checked and found incorrect:** the split markers are missing or inconsistent | Every `PART` and `PHASE` marker is present once; the split is verified lossless and no split file exceeds 3,000 lines (T-0001 A1 to A4) |
