## E10. Risk register

Likelihood (L) and impact (I): L = low, M = medium, H = high, C = critical. The register is reviewed at every gate (E5.1 section 8) and finalized at T-0533 and T-0540. "Residual" is the expected level after the listed mitigations are implemented and verified.

| Id | Risk | L | I | Mitigations (tasks) | Residual | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RK-01 | Volumetric attack saturates the VPS uplink | H | H | Upstream scrubbing as a cutover dependency, XDP early drop, shield, DNS secondary, honest capacity claims (P25, P26, T-0476) | M | ops |
| RK-02 | Novel SQL injection or other payload evades signature detection | M | H | Defense in depth: normalization views, semantic evaluator, outbound leak filter, virtual patches, origin hardening report, stated limits (P14, P15, P21, P27) | M | sec |
| RK-03 | False positives block legitimate users or break the site | M | M | Monitor-first preset, baseline replay, benign corpora gates, auto-rollback, appeals, scoped exceptions (P12, P13, T-0371, T-0324) | L | sec |
| RK-04 | Ban poisoning: attacker causes a victim IP to be banned | M | H | Cross-site context rules, spoofed header stripping, shared-address mitigation, never-ban, anomaly alerts (T-0273, T-0326, T-0331, T-0500) | L | sec |
| RK-05 | Admin plane compromise | L | C | Separate host and session scope, forced MFA, step-up, tunnel exposure, route-permission tests, audit chain (T-0417, T-0439) | L | sec |
| RK-06 | Tenant isolation failure (cross-org data access) | L | C | RLS everywhere, BOLA suite, direct-DB tests, secure-definer review (T-0128, T-0503) | L | sec |
| RK-07 | SSRF through origin config, webhooks, feeds, log sinks, flattening | M | H | Single egress connector, pinned DNS, rebinding checks, 150-vector matrix, egress-lint (T-0413) | L | sec |
| RK-08 | Certificate mis-issuance or CA rate-limit lockout | M | M | Staging first, budgets, failed-validation guard, CAA, CT monitoring, operator approval (P19, T-0538) | L | dp |
| RK-09 | Unsigned zone behind an existing DS record causes validation outage | M | H | DS check blocker, post-cutover validation probe (T-0403) | L | dns |
| RK-10 | Registrar or DNS provider account compromise | L | C | Out of HDD's control; guidance, registrar lock and 2FA recommendations in runbooks (T-0527) | M | operator |
| RK-11 | Origin IP leaks and attackers bypass HDD | H | H | Lockdown (header, mTLS, firewall), exposure monitoring, re-IP assistant, verification from off-platform (P21) | M | operator |

## E11. Cutover and release checklists

### E11.1 STOP #1 (pilot, at M5)

- [ ] Provider acceptable-use confirmation recorded with date
- [ ] Pilot subzone NS records added at the existing DNS provider (`test_hostname`, `sandbox_hostname`) and `ns1/ns2` A records exist outside the delegated subzone
- [ ] Canary files installed on the origin (and `hdd-canary` if desired); static and reachable directly
- [ ] `egress_allowlist` covers CA, feeds, SMTP, resolvers
- [ ] Runner IP recorded; not in `admin_cidrs`; in the never-ban list
- [ ] SSH allow CIDRs recorded; second SSH session available for timed-revert confirmations
- [ ] Backup of the existing DNS zone and VPS firewall rules taken
- [ ] Staging ACME account email set; production issuance not yet approved

### E11.2 Pre-cutover (STOP #2, at M12): the seven gates with evidence

- [ ] Gate 1: `upstream_ddos.mode` is `always_on` or `on_demand` with contract facts recorded and AC-25 dry-run done, or `risk_acceptance_volumetric: true` with date
- [ ] Gate 2: external secondary DNS live and answering (AC-21, AC-28); mitigation activation rehearsed in dry run (AC-27)
- [ ] Gate 3: exposure board shows no overdue KEV or critical item for the origin and no expired virtual patch (AC-30, AC-31)
- [ ] Gate 4: operator reviewed `docs/ORIGIN-HARDENING.md` and posture scan results (AC-32)
- [ ] Gate 5: HDD supply-chain checks green and a signed-update rollback exercised (AC-33)
- [ ] Gate 6: AC-23 (including DS check) and AC-18 (lockdown applied) pass; apex certificate pre-issued
- [ ] Gate 7: if product surfaces will be public: AC-35, AC-36, AC-40, AC-42 pass
- [ ] Zone imported; parity clean; unsupported types acknowledged; `non_http_services` grey; mail records identical
- [ ] TTLs lowered at the old provider at least one full old-TTL period earlier; parent NS TTL recorded
- [ ] `export-zone` backup taken; old provider zone remains live and mirrored
- [ ] Monitor-first period and false-positive review plan agreed (default 48 h)
- [ ] Rollback owner, abort criteria and decision deadline agreed in writing
- [ ] Maintenance window, communications and on-call confirmed
- [ ] Any NO-GO item has an item-specific, dated, written risk acceptance from the operator

### E11.3 Cutover day

- [ ] Written go-ahead present and fresh (backup < 24 h, certificate valid, TTLs aged, secondary live, gates re-evaluated < 2 h)
- [ ] Dashboards and external probes open; alert thresholds tightened for the window
- [ ] Final backup and zone export taken
- [ ] Registrar host objects (glue) for `ns1/ns2` created where in-bailiwick
- [ ] NS changed at the registrar (or pointed at the external secondary for `hidden_primary`)
- [ ] Propagation probes from several public resolvers: A/AAAA/MX/TXT/NS/SOA, proxied vs grey, DNSSEC validation probe
- [ ] TLS handshake checks on all proxied names; HTTP checks through HDD; mail flow tested by the operator
- [ ] Abort criteria evaluated continuously (validation failures, mail routing errors, TLS errors, origin errors)
- [ ] Old provider kept live for at least one full old-TTL period after stable operation

### E11.4 Post-cutover

- [ ] Monitor-first review at +1 h, +6 h, +24 h, +48 h with would-block classification
- [ ] False-positive families fixed with dry-run evidence
- [ ] Block switch proposed with impact summary; operator confirms; switch with safe-mode command ready
- [ ] Ban layers verified end to end with a safe test source (L7, kernel, XDP if present)
- [ ] Outbound filter moved to block after a clean monitor period
- [ ] Alert noise reviewed; thresholds tuned
- [ ] Two consecutive stable days and operator sign-off recorded
- [ ] Old provider decommission plan agreed (after TTL policy)

### E11.5 Production certificate issuance (one event)

- [ ] Staging end-to-end success in the last 7 days
- [ ] CAA allows the CA; secondary serves the challenge TXT; CNAME delegation observed
- [ ] Rate-limit budgets checked against the CA's current documentation
- [ ] Operator's explicit written approval recorded verbatim
- [ ] Production flag set time-boxed; first failure stops the run
- [ ] Chain validated against public trust; SAN, lifetime, SCT, CT observation verified
- [ ] Flag auto-reset confirmed; renewal scheduling and expiry alerts active

### E11.6 Opening public signup

- [ ] Legal pages approved (`legal_approved_at`) and brand set
- [ ] Abuse intake working; abuse queue owner assigned
- [ ] Signup policy reviewed (disposable email, rate limits, friction tiers)
- [ ] SMTP delivery verified with SPF/DKIM/DMARC aligned
- [ ] Plans and quotas configured; `owner_only` unlimited plan not exposed
- [ ] AC-35, AC-36, AC-40, AC-41, AC-42, AC-43 passed on the release candidate
- [ ] Monitoring, backups and on-call active; status page live
- [ ] Operator approves `signup.mode: open` in chat

### E11.7 Release checklist (every version)

- [ ] `xtask verify` green; `xtask acceptance --tier release` report complete (no FAIL)
- [ ] `claims-audit`, `docs-test`, `egress-lint`, `unsafe-scan`, `migrations lint`, `api-diff` green
- [ ] No expired virtual patches; advisory SLAs for HDD dependencies met or excepted with expiry
- [ ] SBOMs generated; lab crates absent; reproducible build verified; provenance signed
- [ ] Release notes with migration plan (reversible or forward-only) and upgrade order
- [ ] Upgrade N-1 → N and rollback rehearsed on a VM
- [ ] Signed artifacts published to the pinned release host; checksums recorded
- [ ] Rollout channel: candidate first, stable after soak
- [ ] Post-release smoke tier on the pilot

### E11.8 Incident quick actions

- [ ] Application attack on a customer site: confirm mode and preset, check bans and events, raise preset, enable under-attack mode, notify owner
- [ ] Volumetric attack: check shield state and upstream status, hold/escalate shield, contact provider per runbook, consider standby failover
- [ ] Suspected platform breach: contain (safe mode, session revocation, key rotation), preserve evidence with hashes, notify per policy
- [ ] Certificate emergency: stop issuance flags, revoke if mis-issued, rotate keys, notify CAs as needed
- [ ] False-positive wave: scoped exceptions, rollback revision, mass-unban procedure with audit
- [ ] DNS issue: compare snapshot and live answers, check secondary lag, fail over if needed

### E11.9 Local profile release checklist (new in v5.1)

- [ ] `profile-parity` shows zero differences; `profile-lint` and `kv-lint` green

### E12.2 Walkthrough: what happens when an attacker submits `' OR 1=1--` to a login form on a vulnerable protected site

This is the primary scenario, expressed as the sequence of control points and the tasks that build them. It assumes the domain is in `block` mode with the Vulnerable-Origin Shield (Balanced) preset and the `/login` path declared as an auth endpoint.

| # | Control point | What happens | Tasks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Connection | The attacker connects over TLS; the SNI selects the tenant certificate; the HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 front end applies protocol hardening (stage 0 to 5). | T-0353 to T-0358, T-0375 |
| 2 | Client IP | The real client IP is resolved from the socket (spoofed forwarding headers are ignored); IP key is /32 or /64. | T-0315 |
| 3 | Jail check | If the IP is already banned, the request gets the branded 403 immediately and no further work happens. | T-0319 |
| 4 | Host routing | The normalized Host selects the site snapshot; unknown hosts get a neutral 404. | T-0355 |
| 5 | Body handling | The form body is read with caps; the body is decoded and inspected (never skipped on write paths). | T-0249, T-0360, T-0276 |
| 6 | Normalization | Three views are built: raw, decoded (percent/HTML/unicode escapes) and canonical (case, whitespace, comments, quote folding). | T-0241, T-0242 |
| 7 | Field kind | `username` is recognized (or declared) as a username field; policy is strict on auth endpoints. | T-0251, T-0225 |
| 8 | Detection | The SQL tokenizer and semantic evaluator see quote breakout + always-true predicate + comment truncation: H1 and H2 hard hits (rules fire under all three views). | T-0263 to T-0271 |
| 9 | Verdict | Hard hit in `block` mode outside cross-site subresource context: 403 with Ray ID; no request reaches the origin. | T-0252, T-0261, T-0273 |
| 10 | Ban | A `BanIntent` creates a ban for the IP key: TTL step 1 of the ladder (1 h), reason `hard_attack`, rule/subtype/vector/field recorded. | T-0317, T-0320 |
| 11 | Propagation | Ban is stored locally, in Redis and Postgres; the signed stream tells the host agent; kernel set drops the IP on 80/443 and XDP if enabled (≤ 2 s). | T-0316, T-0322, T-0464, T-0467 |
| 12 | Evidence | An event with redacted evidence (≤ 512 B) and the policy branch is stored; the owner sees it live and in the IP jail. | T-0252, T-0253, T-0446 |
| 13 | Notification | An alert rule for SQLi on auth endpoints notifies the owner (grouped, rate-limited). | T-0453 |
| 14 | Follow-up | Any further request from the same IP (even benign) gets the jail response; the attacker's scanner is cut off. | T-0319 |
| 15 | If something slipped | The outbound filter would mask database errors; the V13 tripwire raises a critical event on success-after-attack in monitor mode; virtual patches cover known CVEs. | T-0274, T-0408, T-0485 |
| 16 | Appeal | A mistaken block can be appealed with a light proof-of-work; the owner decides; the attacker cannot self-unban. | T-0324 |
| 17 | Proof | In the Vuln-Lab, the same payloads succeed directly against the vulnerable app and fail through HDD with a ban (AC-38/AC-39). | T-0494 to T-0499 |

### E12.3 Honest limits of the walkthrough

- Signature and structure based detection can be evaded by techniques not yet in the rules; the held-out sets and the red exercise measure this and the numbers are published with their limits.
- A cross-site subresource request carrying the payload is blocked but does not ban (to prevent ban poisoning); repeated hits convert to a rate-limit ban.
- Password fields are softened for the comment-breakout family in Balanced to protect users with symbol-heavy passwords; Paranoid makes them hard.
- Direct-to-origin traffic bypasses HDD; origin lockdown is part of the protection profile and its status is shown honestly.
- A WAF does not fix the vulnerable code; the exposure board and hardening report track what must be fixed, and virtual patches never close an item.

### E12.4 Walkthrough: the same attack against a local instance

1. The operator runs `hdd-local run` on a Windows laptop without Docker; the embedded database starts, migrations run, the setup URL appears (T-0563, T-0564).
2. In the browser, `/setup` takes the one-time token, creates the owner with MFA, and offers the local trust choice (T-0567, T-0566).
3. The operator adds a local site `shop` pointing at an application on `127.0.0.1:3001` and chooses Monitor first, then Balanced (T-0568).
4. A test client sends `admin' --` as a query parameter (GET) to `https://shop.hdd.localhost:8444/login` and as a POST body to `https://sandbox.hdd.localhost:8444/`; the inspect-first gate confirms `would_block` before each live request (section 2.2, E3.1 rule 4).
5. In `block` mode the request receives 403 with a Ray ID; the identity `lo:<hash>` of that client is banned for the site, the dashboard (browser identity) is unaffected (T-0565).
6. Stopping `hdd-local` stops protection: the site's tunnel, if any, has no listener (fail closed, C18.9). S-135 and the docs say so in plain words.

### E12.5 Walkthrough: 24/7 on a server

1. `hddctl bootstrap` hardens a fresh VM (T-0573); `hddctl hosting check` lists any gaps (T-0571).
2. `hddctl deploy` installs the services with watchdog and restart policy (T-0522, T-0572); ACME staging, then production after approval (T-0538).
3. Backups run nightly to a remote target; a restore-to-scratch runs weekly (T-0574).
4. The VM reboots after a kernel update; services return within five minutes with no manual step; proxy and DNS first serve from the last-known-good snapshot if the stores are late (T-0572).
5. The external heartbeat and uptime probe record the outage window; the status page shows the measured figure with its method (T-0574).

### E13.3 Critical path

The longest dependency chain for the headline promise (vulnerable site protected, attacker banned, proven in the lab) is: T-0001 to T-0010 (governance) → T-0029 to T-0052 (design system) → T-0071 to T-0094 (frontend foundation) → T-0105 to T-0136 (identity) → T-0153 to T-0176 (onboarding) → T-0207 to T-0220 (walking skeleton) → T-0239 to T-0262 (WAF core) → T-0263 to T-0284 (SQLi shield) → T-0315 to T-0332 (bans) → T-0353 to T-0374 (proxy pipeline) → T-0405 to T-0416 (origin protection and outbound) → T-0491 to T-0499 (acceptance and Vuln-Lab proof). Everything else hangs off this chain and can run in the lanes above. The shortest path to something the operator can run on one computer is the local walking skeleton (slice DS1, E13.5): T-0561 to T-0563 → T-0564 → T-0568, with the identity, frontend and SQLi-shield tasks that those depend on.

## E15. Coverage map (new in v5.1)

This appendix is the seed for `design/coverage/*.toml` (C19.5, T-0578). It maps standards categories to HDD mechanisms, attack groups (`AG-nn`, C5), acceptance checks (E3) and tasks (Part D), and states the limit of each. **The statuses are design targets.** `cargo xtask coverage check` fails a `covered` or `partial` row that lacks an ATK group, an AC and a task, and T-0578 downgrades any row whose evidence is missing; the generated public page (S-134) shows the counts of rows with PASS evidence. The category lists below are the editions current when this was written; T-0578 re-verifies each against the published list and records the edition and date.

Status vocabulary: **covered** = a detector is tested on held-out data with published detection and false-positive rates, the latest run has PASS evidence, and the limits name no structural blind spot for the main attack path; **partial** = part of the category is handled, or the lab proof is limited to inert interpreters, or detection depends on application behavior HDD cannot see; **signal only** = HDD raises a signal or a monitor-mode event but does not claim prevention; **not covered** = outside what HDD can see or do, stated plainly.

### E15.1 OWASP Top 10 (2021)

| ID | Category | Status | Mechanism | ATK groups | AC | Tasks | Limits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A01 | Broken Access Control | Partial | Access gate for sensitive paths, forced-browsing and traversal detection, enumeration heuristics, CSRF enforcement mode, tenant isolation of HDD itself | AG-04, AG-09, AG-10, AG-11 | AC-09, AC-36, AC-50, AC-57 | T-0288, T-0301, T-0303, T-0307, T-0575 | Authorization logic lives in the application; HDD gates paths and detects enumeration but cannot know who may see which object |
| A02 | Cryptographic Failures | Partial | TLS policy and HSTS, minimum TLS, cookie flag upgrades, outbound secret and key leak detection | AG-14, AG-16 | AC-04, AC-05, AC-10 | T-0200, T-0381, T-0408, T-0410, T-0411 | Weak cryptography inside the application or its database is not visible to HDD |
| A03 | Injection (includes cross-site scripting) | Partial | SQL tokenizer and hard families H1 to H8, shell lexer, template and expression injection, XSS tokenizer, NoSQL, LDAP, XPath, CRLF detectors; vulnerable-origin shield; bans | AG-01, AG-02, AG-03 | AC-06, AC-07, AC-09, AC-38, AC-39, AC-49 | T-0263 to T-0297, T-0283, T-0499 | Novel techniques can evade signature-based detection; stored payloads that arrive by another channel are not seen; virtual patches reduce exposure only |
| A04 | Insecure Design | Signal only | Business-flow signals, parameter-tampering heuristics, positive-security hints | AG-16, AG-11 | AC-57 | T-0312, T-0577 | Design flaws are not fixable by a firewall; HDD can observe abuse of a flawed design, not remove the flaw |
| A05 | Security Misconfiguration | Partial | Response-header policy, outbound disclosure control, decoys and exposed-file detection, XXE detection, posture scan, access gate for admin consoles | AG-05, AG-15, AG-16 | AC-05, AC-09, AC-10, AC-32, AC-57 | T-0292, T-0308, T-0309, T-0410, T-0487, T-0575 | Misconfiguration inside services HDD does not proxy (databases, internal tools, cloud accounts) is not covered |
| A06 | Vulnerable and Outdated Components | Partial | Component inventory, advisory feeds, exposure board with SLA clocks, virtual patches with expiry (never marked as fixes) | AG-06, AG-15 | AC-30, AC-31, AC-32 | T-0310, T-0481 to T-0486 | Virtual patching covers known exploit shapes only; the vulnerability stays open until patched (R-11) |
| A07 | Identification and Authentication Failures | Partial | Brute-force, credential-stuffing and spraying detection, JWT attack shapes, session-fixation signals, proof-of-work challenge, access gate login | AG-09 | AC-11, AC-35, AC-44, AC-57 | T-0333 to T-0335, T-0343, T-0344, T-0575 | HDD cannot enforce the application password policy or its MFA; distributed low-and-slow attacks may stay below thresholds |
| A08 | Software and Data Integrity Failures | Partial | Deserialization signatures, CSP report collector and SRI advisor, signed HDD releases | AG-06, AG-16 | AC-09, AC-33 | T-0296, T-0412, T-0516, T-0518 | CI/CD and update-channel integrity of the origin is outside HDD; client-side supply chain is advisory |
| A09 | Security Logging and Monitoring Failures | Partial | Events with evidence, alerts, SIEM export, hash-chained audit log for HDD itself | AG-17 | AC-20, AC-45, AC-47 | T-0131, T-0368, T-0453, T-0460 | HDD logs what crosses it; the origin application's own logging is not covered |
| A10 | Server-Side Request Forgery | Partial | SSRF-in-parameters detector with metadata and internal-range shapes, outbound egress guard with DNS pinning for HDD itself | AG-05 | AC-09, AC-17 | T-0293, T-0413 | Blind SSRF through channels HDD does not see (internal queues, file formats parsed server-side) is not covered |

### E15.7 What HDD does not cover (always shown on S-134)

1. Flaws in an application's own business logic that look like valid use.
2. Vulnerabilities in client-side code that never cross HDD.
3. Zero-day techniques with no signature, structural, behavioral or learned (Sentinel) signal.
4. Volumetric floods larger than the server uplink, unless an upstream provider is contracted and measured.
5. A compromised origin, its credentials, its CI/CD pipeline or its dependencies' build process.
6. Insider misuse and stolen valid sessions used normally.
7. Services that can be reached without crossing HDD (a directly reachable origin address, other open ports on the origin) until the Bypass Guard reports the lockdown `verified`, and only for as long as that verification stays current.
8. Malicious content inside encrypted or opaque protocols that HDD does not terminate or parse.
9. Memory-safety and logic bugs inside the origin's own runtime, frameworks and databases.
10. Anything outside the HTTP, DNS and TLS paths that HDD terminates.
11. In the local profile: protection while HDD is not running or the computer is asleep, kernel-level enforcement, authoritative DNS on port 53, and any availability claim.
